Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

Khuddakanikāye

In the Khuddaka Nikāya

Theragāthāpāḷi

Theragāthā Pāḷi

Nidānagāthā

Introductory Verses

Sīhānaṃva [T 0.0260][M 0.0019][V 0.0161][P 0.0001] nadantānaṃ, dāṭhīnaṃ girigabbhare;

Suṇātha bhāvitattānaṃ, gāthā atthūpanāyikā attūpanāyikā (sī. ka.).

Listen to the benefit-conducing verses of those with developed minds, who are like fanged lions roaring in a mountain cave.

Yathānāmā yathāgottā, yathādhammavihārino;

Yathādhimuttā sappaññā, vihariṃsu atanditā.

Those wise and diligent ones dwelt according to their names, their clans, their way of dwelling in the Dhamma, and their dispositions.

Tattha tattha vipassitvā, phusitvā accutaṃ padaṃ;

Katantaṃ paccavekkhantā, imamatthamabhāsisuṃ.

Having practiced insight in those various places and having realized the unshakeable state, while reflecting upon what had been accomplished, they spoke this meaning.

1. Ekakanipāto

1. The Book of the Ones

1. Paṭhamavaggo

1. The First Chapter

1. Subhūtittheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Subhūti

1.

1.

“Channā [V 0.0162] me kuṭikā sukhā nivātā, vassa deva yathāsukhaṃ;

Cittaṃ me susamāhitaṃ vimuttaṃ, ātāpī viharāmi vassa devā”ti.

My hut is roofed, pleasant, and sheltered from the wind; rain, O deva, as you please. My mind is well-concentrated and liberated; I dwell ardently. Rain, O deva!

Itthaṃ sudaṃ itthaṃ sumaṃ (ka. aṭṭha.) āyasmā subhūtitthero gāthaṃ abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Subhūti spoke this verse.

2. Mahākoṭṭhikattheragāthā

2. The Verses of the Elder Mahākoṭṭhika

2.

2.

“Upasanto [M 0.0220] uparato, mantabhāṇī anuddhato;

Dhunāti pāpake dhamme, dumapattaṃva māluto”ti.

Calm, restrained, wise in speech, and unagitated, he shakes off evil states, as the wind shakes a leaf from a tree.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko mahākoṭṭhito (sī. syā.) thero gāthaṃ abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Mahākoṭṭhika spoke this verse.

3. Kaṅkhārevatattheragāthā

3. The Verses of the Elder Kaṅkhārevata

3.

3.

“Paññaṃ [T 0.0261][P 0.0002] imaṃ passa tathāgatānaṃ, aggi yathā pajjalito nisīthe;

Ālokadā cakkhudadā bhavanti, ye āgatānaṃ vinayanti kaṅkha”nti.

Behold this wisdom of the Tathāgatas! Like a fire blazing in the night, they are givers of light, givers of the eye, who dispel the doubt of those who have come.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā kaṅkhārevato thero gāthaṃ abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Kaṅkhārevata spoke this verse.

4. Puṇṇattheragāthā

4. The Verses of the Elder Puṇṇa

4.

4.

“Sambhireva samāsetha, paṇḍitehatthadassibhi;

Atthaṃ mahantaṃ gambhīraṃ, duddasaṃ nipuṇaṃ aṇuṃ;

Dhīrā samadhigacchanti, appamattā vicakkhaṇā”ti.

One should associate only with the virtuous, with the wise who see the goal. The wise, being diligent and discerning, attain the meaning that is great, profound, difficult to see, subtle, and minute.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā puṇṇo mantāṇiputto mantāniputto (syā. ka.) thero gāthaṃ abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta spoke this verse.

5. Dabbattheragāthā

5. The Verses of the Elder Dabba

5.

5.

“Yo [V 0.0163] duddamiyo damena danto, dabbo santusito vitiṇṇakaṅkho;

Vijitāvī apetabheravo hi, dabbo so parinibbuto ṭhitatto”ti.

He who was difficult to tame is tamed by taming; Dabba is content, with doubt overcome. A conqueror, free from fear, that Dabba is fully extinguished, steadfast in nature.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā dabbo thero gāthaṃ abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Dabba spoke this verse.

6. Sītavaniyattheragāthā

6. The Verses of the Elder Sītavaniya

6.

6.

“Yo [M 0.0221] sītavanaṃ upagā bhikkhu, eko santusito samāhitatto;

Vijitāvī apetalomahaṃso, rakkhaṃ kāyagatāsatiṃ dhitimā”ti.

The monk who has gone to the Sītavana, alone, content, with concentrated mind, a conqueror, free from hair-raising fear, is resolute, guarding mindfulness directed to the body.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā sītavaniyo thero gāthaṃ abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Sītavaniya spoke this verse.

7. Bhalliyattheragāthā

7. The Verses of the Elder Bhalliya

7.

7.

“Yopānudī [T 0.0262] maccurājassa senaṃ, naḷasetuṃva sudubbalaṃ mahogho;

Vijitāvī apetabheravo hi, danto so parinibbuto ṭhitatto”ti.

Whoever has dispelled the army of the King of Death—as a great flood does a very weak reed bridge—he, a conqueror, free from terror, tamed, and steadfast in nature, is fully extinguished.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā bhalliyo thero gāthaṃ abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Bhalliya spoke this verse.

8. Vīrattheragāthā

8. The Verses of the Elder Vīra

8.

8.

“Yo duddamiyo damena danto, vīro santusito vitiṇṇakaṅkho;

Vijitāvī apetalomahaṃso, vīro so parinibbuto ṭhitatto”ti.

He who was difficult to tame is tamed by taming—a hero, content, with doubt overcome, a conqueror, free from hair-raising fear—that hero, steadfast in nature, is fully extinguished.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā vīro thero gāthaṃ abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Vīra spoke this verse.

9. Pilindavacchattheragāthā

9. The Verses of the Elder Pilindavaccha

9.

9.

“Svāgataṃ na durāgataṃ nāpagataṃ (sī. syā.), nayidaṃ dumantitaṃ mama;

Saṃvibhattesu dhammesu, yaṃ seṭṭhaṃ tadupāgami”nti.

My coming was a good coming, not a bad coming; this investigation of mine was not ill-considered. Among the well-analyzed teachings, I have attained that which is most excellent.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā pilindavaccho pilindivaccho (sī.) thero gāthaṃ abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Pilindavaccha spoke this verse.

10. Puṇṇamāsattheragāthā

10. The Verses of the Elder Puṇṇamāsa

10.

10.

“Vihari [M 0.0222][V 0.0164][P 0.0003] apekkhaṃ idha vā huraṃ vā, yo vedagū samito yatatto;

Sabbesu dhammesu anūpalitto, lokassa jaññā udayabbayañcā”ti.

Having abandoned longing for this world or the next, one should dwell. He who is a knower of the goal, pacified, and self-controlled, unsmeared by all things, would know the arising and passing away of the world.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā puṇṇamāso thero gāthaṃ abhāsitthāti.

Thus indeed the Venerable Elder Puṇṇamāsa spoke this verse.

Vaggo paṭhamo niṭṭhito.

The First Chapter is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this is:

Subhūti [T 0.0263] koṭṭhiko thero, kaṅkhārevatasammato;

Mantāṇiputto dabbo ca, sītavaniyo ca bhalliyo;

Vīro pilindavaccho ca, puṇṇamāso tamonudoti.

The Elder Subhūti, Koṭṭhika, the esteemed Kaṅkhārevata; Mantāṇiputta and Dabba, Sītavaniya and Bhalliya; Vīra and Pilindavaccha, and Puṇṇamāsa, the dispeller of darkness.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter

1. Cūḷavacchattheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Cūḷavaccha

11.

11.

“Pāmojjabahulo bhikkhu, dhamme buddhappavedite;

Adhigacche padaṃ santaṃ, saṅkhārūpasamaṃ sukha”nti.

A monk who has much joy in the Dhamma proclaimed by the Buddha may attain the peaceful state, the happiness of the stilling of formations.

… Cūḷavaccho cūlagavaccho (sī.) thero….

Thus the Elder Cūḷavaccha spoke this verse.

2. Mahāvacchattheragāthā

2. The Verses of the Elder Mahāvaccha

12.

12.

“Paññābalī sīlavatūpapanno, samāhito jhānarato satīmā;

Yadatthiyaṃ bhojanaṃ bhuñjamāno, kaṅkhetha kālaṃ idha vītarāgo”ti.

Possessing the power of wisdom, endowed with virtue, concentrated, delighting in jhāna, and mindful; consuming such food as is needed, being free from passion here, one should await the time.

… Mahāvaccho mahāgavaccho (sī.) thero….

Thus the Elder Mahāvaccha spoke this verse.

3. Vanavacchattheragāthā

3. The Verses of the Elder Vanavaccha

13.

13.

“Nīlabbhavaṇṇā [M 0.0223] rucirā, sītavārī sucindharā;

Indagopakasañchannā, te selā ramayanti ma”nti.

With the color of dark clouds, radiant, with cool water and pure ground, covered with cochineal insects—those mountains delight me.

… Vanavaccho thero….

Thus the Elder Vanavaccha spoke this verse.

4. Sivakasāmaṇeragāthā

4. The Verses of the Novice Sīvaka

14.

14.

“Upajjhāyo [V 0.0165] maṃ avaca, ito gacchāma sīvaka;

Gāme [T 0.0264] me vasati kāyo, araññaṃ me gato mano;

Semānakopi gacchāmi, natthi saṅgo vijānata”nti.

My preceptor said to me, 'Let us go from here, Sīvaka.' My body dwells in the village, but my mind has gone to the forest. Even while lying down, I go; for one who knows, there is no attachment.

… Sivako sāmaṇero….

Thus the novice Sīvaka spoke this verse.

5. Kuṇḍadhānattheragāthā

5. The Verses of the Elder Kuṇḍadhāna

15.

15.

“Pañca chinde pañca jahe, pañca cuttari bhāvaye;

Pañcasaṅgātigo bhikkhu, oghatiṇṇoti vuccatī”ti.

One should cut off five, abandon five, and further cultivate five. A bhikkhu who has overcome the five attachments is called 'one who has crossed the flood.'

… Kuṇḍadhāno thero….

Thus the Elder Kuṇḍadhāna spoke this verse.

6. Belaṭṭhasīsattheragāthā

6. The Verses of the Elder Belaṭṭhasīsa

16.

16.

“Yathāpi bhaddo ājañño, naṅgalāvattanī sikhī;

Gacchati appakasirena, evaṃ rattindivā mama;

Gacchanti appakasirena, sukhe laddhe nirāmise”ti.

Just as a fine, crested thoroughbred moves with little effort in the furrow, so my night and day pass with little effort, having obtained unworldly happiness.

… Belaṭṭhasīso thero….

Thus the Elder Belaṭṭhasīsa spoke this verse.

7. Dāsakattheragāthā

7. The Verses of the Elder Dāsaka

17.

17.

“Middhī [P 0.0004] yadā hoti mahagghaso ca, niddāyitā samparivattasāyī;

Mahāvarāhova nivāpapuṭṭho, punappunaṃ gabbhamupeti mando”ti.

When one is torpid and a great glutton, a heavy sleeper who lies rolling about, like a great boar fattened on fodder, the fool repeatedly enters the womb.

… Dāsako thero….

Thus the Elder Dāsaka spoke this verse.

8. Siṅgālapituttheragāthā

8. The Verses of the Elder Siṅgālapitā

18.

18.

“Ahu [M 0.0224] buddhassa dāyādo, bhikkhu bhesakaḷāvane;

Kevalaṃ aṭṭhisaññāya, apharī pathaviṃ paṭhaviṃ (sī. syā.) imaṃ;

Maññehaṃ kāmarāgaṃ so, khippameva pahissatī”ti pahīyabhi (sabbattha pāḷiyaṃ).

There was an heir of the Buddha, a bhikkhu in the Bhesakaḷā forest; with the perception of bones alone, he pervaded this earth. I think he will quickly abandon sensual lust.

… Siṅgālapitā sīgālapitā (sī.) thero….

Thus the Elder Siṅgālapitā spoke this verse.

9. Kulattheragāthā

9. The Verses of the Elder Kula

19.

19.

dha. pa. 80, 145 dhammapadepi “Udakaṃ [V 0.0166] hi nayanti nettikā, usukārā namayanti damayanti (ka.) tejanaṃ;

Dāruṃ [T 0.0265] namayanti tacchakā, attānaṃ damayanti subbatā”ti.

Irrigators lead the water, fletchers straighten the arrow-shaft, carpenters shape the wood; those of good vows tame themselves.

… Kulo kuṇḍalo (sī.), kuḷo (syā. ka.) thero….

Thus the Elder Kula spoke this verse.

10. Ajitattheragāthā

10. The Verses of the Elder Ajita

20.

20.

“Maraṇe me bhayaṃ natthi, nikanti natthi jīvite;

Sandehaṃ nikkhipissāmi, sampajāno paṭissato”ti patissatoti (sī. syā.).

I have no fear of death, no longing for life; I shall lay down this body, clearly comprehending and mindful.

… Ajito thero ….

Thus the Elder Ajita spoke this verse.

Vaggo dutiyo niṭṭhito.

The Second Chapter is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse thereof:

Cūḷavaccho mahāvaccho, vanavaccho ca sīvako;

Kuṇḍadhāno ca belaṭṭhi, dāsako ca tatopari;

Siṅgālapitiko thero, kulo ca ajito dasāti.

Cūḷavaccha, Mahāvaccha, Vanavaccha, and Sīvaka; Kuṇḍadhāna and Belaṭṭhi, Dāsaka, and after him, the Elder Siṅgālapitika, Kula, and Ajita—these are ten.

3. Tatiyavaggo

3. The Third Chapter

1. Nigrodhattheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Nigrodha

21.

21.

“Nāhaṃ bhayassa bhāyāmi, satthā no amatassa kovido;

Yattha bhayaṃ nāvatiṭṭhati, tena maggena vajanti bhikkhavo”ti.

I do not fear what is to be feared; our Teacher is skilled in the Deathless. By that path where fear does not exist, the bhikkhus go.

… Nigrodho thero….

Thus the Elder Nigrodha spoke this verse.

2. Cittakattheragāthā

2. The Verses of the Elder Cittaka

22.

22.

“Nīlā [M 0.0225] sugīvā sikhino, morā kārambhiyaṃ kāraṃviyaṃ (sī.), kāraviyaṃ (syā.) abhinadanti;

Te sītavātakīḷitā sītavātakadditakalitā (sī.), sītavātakalitā (syā.), suttaṃ jhāyaṃ jhānaṃ (syā.), jhāyiṃ (?) nibodhentī”ti.

Peacocks with beautiful blue necks and crests cry out in the Kārambhiya grove; gladdened by the cool wind, they awaken the sleeping meditator.

… Cittako thero….

… The Elder Cittaka…

3. Gosālattheragāthā

3. The Verses of the Elder Gosāla

23.

23.

“Ahaṃ [T 0.0266][V 0.0167][P 0.0005] kho veḷugumbasmiṃ, bhutvāna madhupāyasaṃ;

Padakkhiṇaṃ sammasanto, khandhānaṃ udayabbayaṃ;

Sānuṃ paṭigamissāmi, vivekamanubrūhaya”nti.

Having eaten milk-rice with honey in the bamboo grove, respectfully contemplating the arising and passing away of the aggregates, I shall return to the mountain slope to cultivate seclusion.

… Gosālo thero….

… The Elder Gosāla ….

4. Sugandhattheragāthā

4. The Verses of the Elder Sugandha

24.

24.

“Anuvassiko pabbajito, passa dhammasudhammataṃ;

Tisso vijjā anuppattā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsana”nti.

Having gone forth for less than a year, behold the excellent nature of the Dhamma! The three knowledges have been attained; the Buddha’s instruction has been fulfilled.

… Sugandho thero….

… The Elder Sugandha ….

5. Nandiyattheragāthā

5. The Verses of the Elder Nandiya

25.

25.

“Obhāsajātaṃ phalagaṃ, cittaṃ yassa abhiṇhaso;

Tādisaṃ bhikkhumāsajja, kaṇha dukkhaṃ nigacchasī”ti.

Whose mind, born of light and bearing fruit, is constantly so—by assailing such a monk, O Dark One, you will come to suffering.

… Nandiyo thero….

… The Elder Nandiya ….

6. Abhayattheragāthā

6. The Verses of the Elder Abhaya

26.

26.

“Sutvā subhāsitaṃ vācaṃ, buddhassādiccabandhuno;

Paccabyadhiṃ hi nipuṇaṃ, vālaggaṃ usunā yathā”ti.

Having heard the well-spoken words of the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun, I have penetrated the subtle truth, just as one might pierce a hair’s tip with an arrow.

… Abhayo thero….

… The Elder Abhaya ….

7. Lomasakaṅgiyattheragāthā

7. The Verses of the Elder Lomasakaṅgiya

27.

27.

“Dabbaṃ [M 0.0226] kusaṃ poṭakilaṃ, usīraṃ muñjapabbajaṃ;

Urasā panudissāmi, vivekamanubrūhaya”nti.

Wishing to cultivate seclusion, I will push aside with my chest dabba grass, kusa grass, poṭakila shrubs, usīra grass, muñja grass, and pabbaja grass.

… Lomasakaṅgiyo thero….

… The Elder Lomasakaṅgiya …

8. Jambugāmikaputtattheragāthā

8. The Verses of the Elder Jambugāmikaputta

28.

28.

“Kacci [V 0.0168] no vatthapasuto, kacci no bhūsanārato;

Kacci sīlamayaṃ gandhaṃ, kiṃ tvaṃ vāyasi kacci sīlamayaṃ gandhaṃ, tvaṃ vāsi (syā.) netarā pajā”ti.

Surely you are not devoted to robes? Surely you do not delight in adornment? Why does this fragrance of virtue waft from you, and not from other people?

… Jambugāmikaputto thero….

… The Elder Jambugāmikaputta ….

9. Hāritattheragāthā

9. The Verses of the Elder Hārita

29.

29.

“Samunnamayamattānaṃ, usukārova tejanaṃ;

Cittaṃ [T 0.0267] ujuṃ karitvāna, avijjaṃ bhinda hāritā”ti.

Straighten yourself, Hārita, as a fletcher straightens an arrow-shaft. Having made the mind upright, shatter ignorance.

… Hārito thero….

… The Elder Hārita ….

10. Uttiyattheragāthā

10. The Verses of the Elder Uttiya

30.

30.

“Ābādhe me samuppanne, sati me udapajjatha;

Ābādho me samuppanno, kālo me nappamajjitu”nti.

When illness arose in me, mindfulness arose in me: ‘My illness has arisen; it is time for me not to be heedless.’

… Uttiyo thero….

… The Elder Uttiya …

Vaggo tatiyo niṭṭhito.

The Third Chapter is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse:

Nigrodho cittako thero, gosālathero sugandho;

Nandiyo abhayo thero, thero lomasakaṅgiyo;

Jambugāmikaputto ca, hārito uttiyo isīti.

Nigrodha, the Elder Cittaka, the Elder Gosāla, Sugandha, Nandiya, the Elder Abhaya, the Elder Lomasakaṅgiya, Jambugāmikaputta, Hārita, and Uttiya the seer.

4. Catutthavaggo

4. The Fourth Chapter

1. Gahvaratīriyattheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Gahvaratīriya

31.

31.

“Phuṭṭho [M 0.0227][P 0.0006] ḍaṃsehi makasehi, araññasmiṃ brahāvane;

Nāgo saṃgāmasīseva, sato tatrādhivāsaye”ti.

Though bitten by gadflies and mosquitoes in the wilderness, in the great forest, one should mindfully endure there, like an elephant at the head of a battle.

… Gahvaratīriyo thero….

… The Elder Gahvaratīriya …

2. Suppiyattheragāthā

2. The Verses of the Elder Suppiya

32.

32.

“Ajaraṃ [V 0.0169] jīramānena, tappamānena nibbutiṃ;

Nimiyaṃ nimmissaṃ (sī.), nirāmisaṃ (syā.), nimineyyaṃ (?) paramaṃ santiṃ, yogakkhemaṃ anuttara”nti.

With this aging body, I would exchange it for the unaging; with this tormented body, for extinguishment—the supreme peace, the unsurpassed security from bondage.

… Suppiyo thero….

… The Elder Suppiya …

3. Sopākattheragāthā

3. The Verses of the Elder Sopāka

33.

33.

“Yathāpi [T 0.0268] ekaputtasmiṃ, piyasmiṃ kusalī siyā;

Evaṃ sabbesu pāṇesu, sabbattha kusalo siyā”ti.

Just as one would be solicitous for the welfare of a beloved only son, so too should one be solicitous for the welfare of all beings everywhere.

… Sopāko thero….

… The Elder Sopāka …

4. Posiyattheragāthā

4. The Verses of the Elder Posiya

34.

34.

“Anāsannavarā etā, niccameva vijānatā;

Gāmā araññamāgamma, tato gehaṃ upāvisi upāvisiṃ (sī.);

Tato uṭṭhāya pakkāmi, anāmantetvā anāmantiya (sī.) posiyo”ti.

Knowing this always: 'These women are best when not near,' he came from the forest to the village and then entered a house. Thereafter, rising up, Posiya departed without taking leave.

… Posiyo thero….

… Thus spoke the Elder Posiya …

5. Sāmaññakānittheragāthā

5. The Verses of the Elder Sāmaññakāni

35.

35.

“Sukhaṃ sukhattho labhate tadācaraṃ, kittiñca pappoti yasassa vaḍḍhati;

Yo ariyamaṭṭhaṅgikamañjasaṃ ujuṃ, bhāveti maggaṃ amatassa pattiyā”ti.

He who develops the noble eight-factored path—the straight, direct way for attaining the Deathless—that seeker of happiness, acting accordingly, obtains happiness; he attains fame, and his renown increases.

… Sāmaññakānitthero….

… Thus spoke the Elder Sāmaññakāni …

6. Kumāputtattheragāthā

6. The Verses of the Elder Kumāputta

36.

36.

“Sādhu [M 0.0228] sutaṃ sādhu caritakaṃ, sādhu sadā aniketavihāro;

Atthapucchanaṃ padakkhiṇakammaṃ, etaṃ sāmaññamakiñcanassā”ti.

Good is learning, good is conduct, good is the homeless life always. Inquiring into the meaning and right practice—this is the recluseship for one without impediments.

… Kumāputto thero….

… Thus spoke the Elder Kumāputta …

7. Kumāputtasahāyakattheragāthā

7. The Verses of the Elder, the Companion of Kumāputta

37.

37.

“Nānājanapadaṃ yanti, vicarantā asaññatā;

Samādhiñca virādhenti, kiṃsu raṭṭhacariyā karissati;

Tasmā vineyya sārambhaṃ, jhāyeyya apurakkhato”ti.

Wandering unrestrained, they travel to various lands; they fail to attain concentration. What can this country-wandering accomplish? Therefore, having dispelled contention, one should meditate without being led astray.

… Kumāputtattherassa sahāyako thero….

… Thus spoke the Elder who was the companion of the Elder Kumāputta …

8. Gavampatittheragāthā

8. The Verses of the Elder Gavampati

38.

38.

“Yo [T 0.0269][V 0.0170] iddhiyā sarabhuṃ aṭṭhapesi, so gavampati asito anejo;

Taṃ sabbasaṅgātigataṃ mahāmuniṃ, devā namassanti bhavassa pāragu”nti.

He who by psychic power made the Sarabhū river stand still, that Gavampati is unattached and free from craving. Him, the great sage who has overcome all attachments and gone to the far shore of existence, even the gods revere.

… Gavampatitthero….

… Thus spoke the Elder Gavampati …

9. Tissattheragāthā

9. The Verses of the Elder Tissa

39.

39.

saṃ. ni. 1.21, 97“Sattiyā viya omaṭṭho, ḍayhamānova ḍayhamāneva (sabbattha) matthake;

Kāmarāgappahānāya, sato bhikkhu paribbaje”ti.

As though pierced by a spear, or as though with one's head on fire, a monk should wander mindfully for the abandoning of sensual passion.

… Tisso thero….

… Thus spoke the Elder Tissa …

10. Vaḍḍhamānattheragāthā

10. The Verses of the Elder Vaḍḍhamāna

40.

40.

“Sattiyā [P 0.0007] viya omaṭṭho, ḍayhamānova matthake;

Bhavarāgappahānāya, sato bhikkhu paribbaje”ti.

As though pierced by a spear, or as though with one's head on fire, a monk should wander mindfully for the abandoning of passion for becoming.

… Vaḍḍhamāno thero….

… Thus spoke the Elder Vaḍḍhamāna …

Vaggo catuttho niṭṭhito.

The Fourth Chapter is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Gahvaratīriyo [M 0.0229] suppiyo, sopāko ceva posiyo;

Sāmaññakāni kumāputto, kumāputtasahāyako;

Gavampati tissatthero, vaḍḍhamāno mahāyasoti.

Gahvaratīriya, Suppiya, Sopāka, and Posiya; Sāmaññakāni, Kumāputta, and Kumāputta's companion; Gavampati, the Elder Tissa, and Vaḍḍhamāna of great renown.

5. Pañcamavaggo

5. The Fifth Chapter

1. Sirivaḍḍhattheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Sirivaḍḍha

41.

41.

“Vivaramanupatanti [T 0.0270] vijjutā, vebhārassa ca paṇḍavassa ca;

Nagavivaragato ca jhāyati, putto appaṭimassa tādino”ti.

Lightnings fall into the cleft between Vebhāra and Paṇḍava; and having gone into the mountain cleft, the son of the Incomparable, the Such-like One, meditates.

… Sirivaḍḍho thero….

… Thus spoke the Elder Sirivaḍḍha …

2. Khadiravaniyattheragāthā

2. The Verses of the Elder Khadiravaniya

42.

42.

“Cāle [V 0.0171] upacāle sīsūpacāle ( ) (cālā upacālā, sīsūpacālā) (ka.) patissatā paṭissatikā (syā. ka.) nu kho viharatha;

Āgato vo vālaṃ viya vedhī”ti.

O Cāla, Upacāla, and Sīsupacāla, do you indeed dwell with mindfulness established? The expert archer, who can pierce a hair, has come to you.

… Khadiravaniyo thero….

… Thus spoke the Elder Khadiravaniya …

3. Sumaṅgalattheragāthā

3. The Verses of the Elder Sumaṅgala

43.

43.

“Sumuttiko sumuttiko sāhu, sumuttikomhi tīhi khujjakehi;

Asitāsu mayā naṅgalāsu, mayā khuddakuddālāsu mayā.

Well freed, well freed! It is good, I am well freed from the three crooked things: from sickles, from plows, and from small hoes.

Yadipi idhameva idhameva, atha vāpi alameva alameva;

Jhāya sumaṅgala jhāya sumaṅgala, appamatto vihara sumaṅgalā”ti.

Even if they are here, right here, still it is enough, quite enough! Meditate, O Sumaṅgala, meditate, O Sumaṅgala! Dwell heedfully, O Sumaṅgala!

… Sumaṅgalo thero….

… The Elder Sumaṅgala…

4. Sānuttheragāthā

4. The Verses of the Elder Sānu

44.

44.

saṃ. ni. 1.239 “Mataṃ vā amma rodanti, yo vā jīvaṃ na dissati;

Jīvantaṃ maṃ amma passantī, kasmā maṃ amma rodasī”ti.

Mother, they weep for the dead, or for one who, though living, is not seen. Seeing me, who am alive and standing before you, why, mother, do you weep for me?

… Sānutthero….

… The Elder Sānu…

5. Ramaṇīyavihārittheragāthā

5. The Verses of the Elder Ramaṇīyavihārī

45.

45.

“Yathāpi [M 0.0230] bhaddo ājañño, khalitvā patitiṭṭhati;

Evaṃ [T 0.0271] dassanasampannaṃ, sammāsambuddhasāvaka”nti.

Just as a fine thoroughbred, having stumbled, re-establishes itself, so too the disciple of the Perfectly Enlightened One, endowed with vision.

… Ramaṇīyavihāritthero….

… The Elder Ramaṇīyavihārī…

6. Samiddhittheragāthā

6. The Verses of the Elder Samiddhi

46.

46.

“Saddhāyāhaṃ pabbajito, agārasmānagāriyaṃ;

Sati paññā ca me vuḍḍhā, cittañca susamāhitaṃ;

Kāmaṃ karassu rūpāni, neva maṃ byādhayissasī”ti bādhayissasīti (sī.), byāthayissasīti (?).

Through faith I have gone forth from the home life into homelessness. My mindfulness and wisdom have grown, and my mind is well-composed. Create forms as you wish; you shall not afflict me.

… Samiddhitthero….

… The Elder Samiddhi…

7. Ujjayattheragāthā

7. The Verses of the Elder Ujjaya

47.

47.

“Namo [V 0.0172][P 0.0008] te buddha vīratthu, vippamuttosi sabbadhi;

Tuyhāpadāne viharaṃ, viharāmi anāsavo”ti.

Homage to you, O Buddha, the Hero! You are completely liberated in every way. Dwelling in your teaching, I dwell free from the taints.

… Ujjayo thero….

… The Elder Ujjaya…

8. Sañjayattheragāthā

8. The Verses of the Elder Sañjaya

48.

48.

“Yato ahaṃ pabbajito, agārasmānagāriyaṃ;

Nābhijānāmi saṅkappaṃ, anariyaṃ dosasaṃhita”nti.

From when I went forth from the home life into homelessness, I do not recall having a single ignoble thought connected with corruption.

… Sañjayo thero….

… The Elder Sañjaya…

9. Rāmaṇeyyakattheragāthā

9. The Verses of the Elder Rāmaṇeyyaka

49.

49.

“Cihacihābhinadite vihavihābhinadite (sī. syā.), sippikābhirutehi ca;

Na me taṃ phandati cittaṃ, ekattanirataṃ hi me”ti.

Though the forest resounds with the ‘ciha-ciha’ cries and the calls of sippika birds, my mind does not tremble, for it is devoted to the state of unity.

… Rāmaṇeyyako thero….

… The Elder Rāmaṇeyyaka…

10. Vimalattheragāthā

10. The Verses of the Elder Vimala

50.

50.

“Dharaṇī [M 0.0231] ca siñcati vāti, māluto vijjutā carati nabhe;

Upasamanti vitakkā, cittaṃ susamāhitaṃ mamā”ti.

The earth is sprinkled, the wind blows, lightning flashes in the sky; my thoughts are stilled, and my mind is well-composed.

… Vimalo thero….

… The Elder Vimala…

Vaggo pañcamo niṭṭhito.

The Fifth Chapter is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Sirīvaḍḍho revato thero, sumaṅgalo sānusavhayo[T 0.0272];

Ramaṇīyavihārī ca, samiddhiujjayasañjayā;

Rāmaṇeyyo ca so thero, vimalo ca raṇañjahoti.

Sirīvaḍḍha, the Elder Revata, Sumaṅgala, and the one named Sānu; Ramaṇīyavihārī, Samiddhi, Ujjaya, and Sañjaya; and that Elder Rāmaṇeyya; and Vimala, the abandoner of defilements.

6. Chaṭṭhavaggo

6. The Sixth Chapter

1. Godhikattheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Godhika

51.

51.

“Vassati [V 0.0173] devo yathā sugītaṃ, channā me kuṭikā sukhā nivātā;

Cittaṃ susamāhitañca mayhaṃ, atha ce patthayasi pavassa devā”ti.

The deity rains with a sound as pleasant as a song; my hut is roofed, pleasant, and sheltered from the wind. My mind, too, is well-composed. Now, O deity, if you wish, rain on.

… Godhiko thero….

… The Elder Godhika…

2. Subāhuttheragāthā

2. The Verses of the Elder Subāhu

52.

52.

“Vassati devo yathā sugītaṃ, channā me kuṭikā sukhā nivātā;

Cittaṃ susamāhitañca kāye, atha ce patthayasi pavassa devā”ti.

The deity rains with a sound as pleasant as a song; my hut is roofed, pleasant, and sheltered from the wind. My mind, too, is well-composed in the body. Now, O deity, if you wish, rain on.

… Subāhutthero….

… The Elder Subāhu…

3. Valliyattheragāthā

3. The Verses of the Elder Valliya

53.

53.

“Vassati devo yathā sugītaṃ, channā me kuṭikā sukhā nivātā;

Tassaṃ viharāmi appamatto, atha ce patthayasi pavassa devā”ti.

The deity rains with a sound as pleasant as a song; my hut is roofed, pleasant, and sheltered from the wind. In it, I dwell heedfully. Now, O deity, if you wish, rain on.

… Valliyo thero….

… The Elder Valliya…

4. Uttiyattheragāthā

4. The Verses of the Elder Uttiya

54.

54.

“Vassati [M 0.0232][P 0.0009] devo yathā sugītaṃ, channā me kuṭikā sukhā nivātā;

Tassaṃ viharāmi adutiyo, atha ce patthayasi pavassa devā”ti.

The deity rains with a sound as pleasant as a song; my hut is roofed, pleasant, and sheltered from the wind. In it, I dwell without a second. Now, O deity, if you wish, rain on.

… Uttiyo thero….

… The Elder Uttiya…

5. Añjanavaniyattheragāthā

5. The Verses of the Elder of the Añjana Forest

55.

55.

“Āsandiṃ [T 0.0273] kuṭikaṃ katvā, ogayha añjanaṃ vanaṃ;

Tisso vijjā anuppattā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsana”nti.

Having entered the Añjana forest and made a hut with a chair, the three true knowledges have been attained; the Buddha’s teaching has been fulfilled.

… Añjanavaniyo thero….

… The Elder of the Añjana Forest…

6. Kuṭivihārittheragāthā

6. The Verses of the Elder Dwelling in a Hut

56.

56.

“Ko [V 0.0174] kuṭikāyaṃ bhikkhu kuṭikāyaṃ, vītarāgo susamāhitacitto;

Evaṃ jānāhi āvuso, amoghā te kuṭikā katā”ti.

‘Who is in this hut?’ ‘A monk is in this hut, free from passion, with a well-composed mind.’ Know this, friend: the hut you have made is not in vain.

… Kuṭivihāritthero….

… The Elder Dwelling in a Hut…

7. Dutiyakuṭivihārittheragāthā

7. The Verses of the Second Elder Dwelling in a Hut

57.

57.

“Ayamāhu purāṇiyā kuṭi, aññaṃ patthayase navaṃ kuṭiṃ;

Āsaṃ kuṭiyā virājaya, dukkhā bhikkhu puna navā kuṭī”ti.

This hut, they say, is old, and you desire another, a new one. Rid yourself of longing for a hut; O monk, a new hut is again suffering.

… Dutiyakuṭivihāritthero….

…The Second Elder Dwelling in a Hut…

8. Ramaṇīyakuṭikattheragāthā

8. The Verses of the Elder of the Delightful Hut

58.

58.

“Ramaṇīyā me kuṭikā, saddhādeyyā manoramā;

Na me attho kumārīhi, yesaṃ attho tahiṃ gacchatha nāriyo”ti.

“Delightful is my little hut, a charming gift of faith. I have no need for maidens; O women, go to those who have need of you.”

… Ramaṇīyakuṭiko thero….

…The Elder of the Delightful Hut…

9. Kosalavihārittheragāthā

9. The Verses of the Elder Kosalavihārī

59.

59.

“Saddhāyāhaṃ [M 0.0233] pabbajito, araññe me kuṭikā katā;

Appamatto ca ātāpī, sampajāno patissato”ti paṭissatoti (ka.).

“Out of faith I went forth; my hut has been made in the forest. I am diligent and ardent, clearly comprehending and mindful.”

… Kosalavihāritthero….

…the Elder Kosalavihārī…

10. Sīvalittheragāthā

10. The Verses of the Elder Sīvali

60.

60.

“Te me ijjhiṃsu saṅkappā, yadattho pāvisiṃ kuṭiṃ;

Vijjāvimuttiṃ paccesaṃ, mānānusayamujjaha”nti.

“Those aspirations of mine were fulfilled, the purpose for which I entered the hut. I have attained knowledge and liberation, having abandoned the underlying tendency of conceit.”

… Sīvalitthero….

…the Elder Sīvali…

Vaggo chaṭṭho niṭṭhito.

The sixth chapter is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this is:

Godhiko [T 0.0274] ca subāhu ca, valliyo uttiyo isi;

Añjanavaniyo thero, duve kuṭivihārino;

Ramaṇīyakuṭiko ca, kosalavhayasīvalīti.

Godhika and Subāhu, Valliya, Uttiya the sage; the Elder Añjanavaniya, the two Kuṭivihārins; Ramaṇīyakuṭika, the one named Kosala, and Sīvalī.

7. Sattamavaggo

7. The Seventh Chapter

1. Vappattheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Vappa

61.

61.

“Passati [V 0.0175] passo passantaṃ, apassantañca passati;

Apassanto apassantaṃ, passantañca na passatī”ti.

“One who sees, sees one who sees, and also sees one who does not see. One who does not see, sees neither one who does not see, nor one who sees.”

… Vappo thero….

…the Elder Vappa…

2. Vajjiputtattheragāthā

2. The Verses of the Elder Vajjiputta

62.

62.

“Ekakā [P 0.0010] mayaṃ araññe viharāma, apaviddhaṃva vanasmiṃ dārukaṃ;

Tassa me bahukā pihayanti, nerayikā viya saggagāmina”nti.

“Alone we dwell in the forest, like a log discarded in the woods. Many long for me for this, as beings in hell long for those going to heaven.”

… Vajjiputto thero….

…the Elder Vajjiputta…

3. Pakkhattheragāthā

3. The Verses of the Elder Pakkha

63.

63.

“Cutā [M 0.0234] patanti patitā, giddhā ca punarāgatā;

Kataṃ kiccaṃ rataṃ rammaṃ, sukhenanvāgataṃ sukha”nti.

“Fallen, they fall; and having fallen, the greedy come again. The duty is done, the delightful is delighted in; happiness is followed by happiness.”

… Pakkho thero….

…the Elder Pakkha…

4. Vimalakoṇḍaññattheragāthā

4. The Verses of the Elder Vimalakoṇḍañña

64.

64.

“Dumavhayāya uppanno, jāto paṇḍaraketunā;

Ketuhā [T 0.0275] ketunāyeva, mahāketuṃ padhaṃsayī”ti.

“Born of one named ‘tree,’ fathered by the White Banner; the banner-destroyer, with that very banner, demolished the great banner.”

… Vimalakoṇḍañño thero….

…the Elder Vimalakoṇḍañña…

5. Ukkhepakatavacchattheragāthā

5. The Verses of the Elder Ukkhepakatavaccha

65.

65.

“Ukkhepakatavacchassa, saṅkalitaṃ bahūhi vassehi;

Taṃ bhāsati gahaṭṭhānaṃ, sunisinno uḷārapāmojjo”ti.

“That which was collected by Ukkhepakatavaccha over many years, he speaks to the householders, well-seated and with great joy.”

… Ukkhepakatavaccho thero….

…the Elder Ukkhepakatavaccha…

6. Meghiyattheragāthā

6. The Verses of the Elder Meghiya

66.

66.

“Anusāsi [V 0.0176] mahāvīro, sabbadhammāna pāragū;

Tassāhaṃ dhammaṃ sutvāna, vihāsiṃ santike sato;

Tisso vijjā anuppattā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsana”nti.

“The Great Hero, the one gone to the far shore of all phenomena, instructed me. Having heard his Dhamma, I dwelt near him, mindful. The three knowledges have been attained; the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.”

… Meghiyo thero….

…the Elder Meghiya…

7. Ekadhammasavanīyattheragāthā

7. The Verses of the Elder Ekadhammasavanīya

67.

67.

“Kilesā jhāpitā mayhaṃ, bhavā sabbe samūhatā;

Vikkhīṇo jātisaṃsāro, natthi dāni punabbhavo”ti.

“My defilements have been burned; all states of becoming have been uprooted. The cycle of birth is exhausted; now there is no further becoming.”

… Ekadhammasavanīyo thero….

…the Elder Ekadhammasavanīya…

8. Ekudāniyattheragāthā

8. The Verses of the Elder Ekudāniya

68.

68.

udā. 37; pāci. 153 “Adhicetaso appamajjato, munino monapathesu sikkhato;

Sokā na bhavanti tādino, upasantassa sadā satīmato”ti.

“For the sage with a supreme mind, who is diligent, training in the paths of sagacity; for such a one, who is tranquil and ever mindful, sorrows do not exist.”

… Ekudāniyo thero….

…the Elder Ekudāniya…

9. Channattheragāthā

9. The Verses of the Elder Channa

69.

69.

“Sutvāna [M 0.0235] dhammaṃ mahato mahārasaṃ, sabbaññutaññāṇavarena desitaṃ;

Maggaṃ papajjiṃ papajjaṃ (ka.) amatassa pattiyā, so yogakkhemassa pathassa kovido”ti.

“Having heard the Dhamma, great and of great flavor, from the Great One, taught by the one supreme in all-knowing wisdom, I entered upon the path for the attainment of the Deathless. He is skilled in the path to security from bondage.”

… Channo thero….

Thus spoke the Elder Channa.

10. Puṇṇattheragāthā

10. The Verses of the Elder Puṇṇa

70.

70.

“Sīlameva [T 0.0276][P 0.0011] idha aggaṃ, paññavā pana uttamo;

Manussesu ca devesu, sīlapaññāṇato jaya”nti.

In this world, virtue alone is foremost, but the one with wisdom is supreme. Among humans and gods, victory comes from virtue and wisdom.

… Puṇṇo thero….

Thus spoke the Elder Puṇṇa.

Vaggo sattamo niṭṭhito.

The Seventh Chapter is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ [V 0.0177] –

The summary of this is:

Vappo ca vajjiputto ca, pakkho vimalakoṇḍañño;

Ukkhepakatavaccho ca, meghiyo ekadhammiko;

Ekudāniyachannā ca, puṇṇatthero mahabbaloti.

Vappa and Vajjiputta, Pakkha and Vimalakoṇḍañña, Ukkhepakatavaccha, Meghiya and Ekadhammika, Ekudāniya and Channa, and the Elder Puṇṇa of great power.

8. Aṭṭhamavaggo

8. The Eighth Chapter

1. Vacchapālattheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Vacchapāla

71.

71.

“Susukhumanipuṇatthadassinā, matikusalena nivātavuttinā;

Saṃsevitavuddhasīlinā saṃsevitabuddhasīlinā (ka.), nibbānaṃ na hi tena dullabha”nti.

For one who sees very subtle and refined meanings, who is skillful in thought and humble in conduct, who is virtuous, having associated with the developed ones, Nibbāna is not difficult to attain.

… Vacchapālo thero….

Thus spoke the Elder Vacchapāla.

2. Ātumattheragāthā

2. The Verses of the Elder Ātuma

72.

72.

“Yathā [M 0.0236] kaḷīro susu vaḍḍhitaggo, dunnikkhamo hoti pasākhajāto;

Evaṃ ahaṃ bhariyāyānitāya, anumaññaṃ [T 0.0277] maṃ pabbajitomhi dānī”ti.

Just as a bamboo shoot, its top well-grown and with spreading branches, is difficult to pull out; so too with me and a wife brought to me. Now, having gained permission, I have gone forth.

… Ātumo thero….

Thus spoke the Elder Ātuma.

3. Māṇavattheragāthā

3. The Verses of the Elder Māṇava

73.

73.

“Jiṇṇañca disvā dukhitañca byādhitaṃ, matañca disvā gatamāyusaṅkhayaṃ;

Tato ahaṃ nikkhamitūna pabbajiṃ, pahāya kāmāni manoramānī”ti.

Having seen the aged, the suffering, and the sick, and having seen the dead, their life-span exhausted, I then went forth from home, abandoning delightful sensual pleasures.

… Māṇavo thero….

Thus spoke the Elder Māṇava.

4. Suyāmanattheragāthā

4. The Verses of the Elder Suyāmana

74.

74.

“Kāmacchando ca byāpādo, thinamiddhañca thīnamiddhañca (sī. syā.) bhikkhuno;

Uddhaccaṃ vicikicchā ca, sabbasova na vijjatī”ti.

For that monk in whom sensual desire and ill will, sloth and torpor, restlessness and doubt, are altogether non-existent.

… Suyāmano thero….

Thus spoke the Elder Suyāmana.

5. Susāradattheragāthā

5. The Verses of the Elder Susārada

75.

75.

“Sādhu suvihitāna dassanaṃ, kaṅkhā chijjati buddhi vaḍḍhati;

Bālampi karonti paṇḍitaṃ, tasmā sādhu sataṃ samāgamo”ti.

Good is the sight of the well-composed; doubt is cut off, and wisdom increases. They make even a fool wise; therefore, association with the good is beneficial.

… Susārado thero….

Thus spoke the Elder Susārada.

6. Piyañjahattheragāthā

6. The Verses of the Elder Piyañjaha

76.

76.

“Uppatantesu [V 0.0178] nipate, nipatantesu uppate;

Vase avasamānesu, ramamānesu no rame”ti.

Among those who rise up with conceit, one should be humble; among those who are diminished in virtue, one should strive. One should dwell with those who are not overcome by defilements; among those who revel, one should not revel.

… Piyañjaho thero….

Thus spoke the Elder Piyañjaha.

7. Hatthārohaputtattheragāthā

7. The Verses of the Elder Hatthārohaputta

77.

77.

“Idaṃ [M 0.0237][P 0.0012] pure cittamacāri cārikaṃ, yenicchakaṃ yatthakāmaṃ yathāsukhaṃ;

Tadajjahaṃ niggahessāmi yoniso, hatthippabhinnaṃ viya aṅkusaggaho”ti.

Formerly, this mind wandered about, going wherever it wished, wherever it desired, just as it pleased. Today I shall restrain it with wise attention, like a mahout with a goad controls an elephant in must.

… Hatthārohaputto thero….

Thus spoke the Elder Hatthārohaputta.

8. Meṇḍasirattheragāthā

8. The Verses of the Elder Meṇḍasira

78.

78.

“Anekajātisaṃsāraṃ[T 0.0278], sandhāvissaṃ anibbisaṃ;

Tassa me dukkhajātassa, dukkhakkhandho aparaddho”ti.

Not finding what I sought, I have transmigrated through a saṃsāra of countless births. For me, who was born to suffering, this aggregate of suffering has been destroyed.

… Meṇḍasiro thero….

Thus spoke the Elder Meṇḍasira.

9. Rakkhitattheragāthā

9. The Verses of the Elder Rakkhita

79.

79.

“Sabbo rāgo pahīno me, sabbo doso samūhato;

Sabbo me vigato moho, sītibhūtosmi nibbuto”ti.

All lust has been abandoned by me, all aversion has been uprooted. All delusion has departed from me; I have become cooled, fully extinguished.

… Rakkhito thero….

Thus spoke the Elder Rakkhita.

10. Uggattheragāthā

10. The Verses of the Elder Ugga

80.

80.

“Yaṃ [M 0.0238] mayā pakataṃ kammaṃ, appaṃ vā yadi vā bahuṃ;

Sabbametaṃ parikkhīṇaṃ, natthi dāni punabbhavo”ti.

Whatever kamma I have done, whether it be minor or major, all of it is exhausted. Now there is no future existence.

… Uggo thero….

Thus spoke the Elder Ugga.

Vaggo aṭṭhamo niṭṭhito.

The Eighth Chapter is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse:

Vacchapālo ca yo thero, ātumo māṇavo isi;

Suyāmano susārado, thero yo ca piyañjaho;

Ārohaputto meṇḍasiro, rakkhito uggasavhayoti.

The Elder Vacchapāla, and the Elder Ātuma, the sage Māṇava; Suyāmana, Susārada, and the Elder Piyañjaha; Ārohaputta, Meṇḍasira, Rakkhita, and the one named Ugga.

9. Navamavaggo

9. The Ninth Chapter

1. Samitiguttattheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Samitigutta

81.

81.

“Yaṃ [V 0.0179] mayā pakataṃ pāpaṃ, pubbe aññāsu jātisu;

Idheva taṃ vedanīyaṃ, vatthu aññaṃ na vijjatī”ti.

Whatever evil kamma was done by me in previous lives, it is to be experienced in this very life; there is no other ground for it.

… Samitigutto thero….

… Thus spoke the Elder Samitigutta….

2. Kassapattheragāthā

2. The Verses of the Elder Kassapa

82.

82.

“Yena [T 0.0279] yena subhikkhāni, sivāni abhayāni ca;

Tena puttaka gacchassu, mā sokāpahato bhavā”ti.

Dear son, go to whatever regions have abundant alms-food, and are safe and secure. Do not be overcome by sorrow.

… Kassapo thero….

… Thus spoke the Elder Kassapa….

3. Sīhattheragāthā

3. The Verses of the Elder Sīha

83.

83.

“Sīhappamatto vihara, rattindivamatandito;

Bhāvehi kusalaṃ dhammaṃ, jaha sīghaṃ samussaya”nti.

O Sīha, dwell heedfully, untiring day and night. Develop wholesome states, and quickly abandon this bodily frame.

… Sīho thero….

… Thus spoke the Elder Sīha….

4. Nītattheragāthā

4. The Verses of the Elder Nīta

84.

84.

“Sabbarattiṃ [P 0.0013] supitvāna, divā saṅgaṇike rato;

Kudāssu nāma dummedho, dukkhassantaṃ karissatī”ti.

Having slept the whole night and delighting in company by day, when, indeed, will you, O witless one, make an end of suffering?

… Nīto thero….

… Thus spoke the Elder Nīta….

5. Sunāgattheragāthā

5. The Verses of the Elder Sunāga

85.

85.

“Cittanimittassa kovido, pavivekarasaṃ vijāniya;

Jhāyaṃ nipako patissato, adhigaccheyya sukhaṃ nirāmisa”nti.

One who is skilled in the sign of the mind, having known the taste of seclusion, meditating, skillful, and mindful, should attain the unworldly bliss.

… Sunāgo thero….

… Thus spoke the Elder Sunāga….

6. Nāgitattheragāthā

6. The Verses of the Elder Nāgita

86.

86.

“Ito [V 0.0180] bahiddhā puthu aññavādinaṃ, maggo na nibbānagamo yathā ayaṃ;

Itissu saṅghaṃ bhagavānusāsati, satthā sayaṃ pāṇitaleva dassaya”nti.

Outside of this Dispensation, among those of various other doctrines, there is no path leading to Nibbāna like this one. Thus the Blessed One instructs the Saṅgha; the Teacher himself shows it as if on the palm of his hand.

… Nāgito thero….

… Thus spoke the Elder Nāgita….

7. Paviṭṭhattheragāthā

7. The Verses of the Elder Paviṭṭha

87.

87.

“Khandhā [M 0.0239] diṭṭhā yathābhūtaṃ, bhavā sabbe padālitā;

Vikkhīṇo jātisaṃsāro, natthi dāni punabbhavo”ti.

The aggregates have been seen as they truly are; all existences have been shattered. The round of births is exhausted; now there is no further becoming.

… Paviṭṭho thero….

… Thus spoke the Elder Paviṭṭha….

8. Ajjunattheragāthā

8. The Verses of the Elder Ajjuna

88.

88.

“Asakkhiṃ [T 0.0280] vata attānaṃ, uddhātuṃ udakā thalaṃ;

Vuyhamāno mahogheva, saccāni paṭivijjhaha”nti.

Ah, being swept along by the great flood, I was able to pull myself from the water onto dry land, for I have penetrated the Truths.

… Ajjuno thero….

… Thus spoke the Elder Ajjuna….

9. (Paṭhama)-devasabhattheragāthā

9. The Verses of the Elder Devasabha (the First)

89.

89.

“Uttiṇṇā paṅkapalipā, pātālā parivajjitā;

Mutto oghā ca ganthā ca, sabbe mānā visaṃhatā”ti.

I have crossed over the mud and the mire; the abyss has been avoided. I am freed from the floods and the ties; all conceits have been destroyed.

… Devasabho thero….

… Thus spoke the Elder Devasabha….

10. Sāmidattattheragāthā

10. The Verses of the Elder Sāmidatta

90.

90.

“Pañcakkhandhā pariññātā, tiṭṭhanti chinnamūlakā;

Vikkhīṇo jātisaṃsāro, natthi dāni punabbhavo”ti.

The five aggregates are fully understood; they stand with their root severed. The round of births is exhausted; now there is no further becoming.

… Sāmidatto thero….

… Thus spoke the Elder Sāmidatta….

Vaggo navamo niṭṭhito.

The Ninth Chapter is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Thero samitigutto ca, kassapo sīhasavhayo;

Nīto sunāgo nāgito, paviṭṭho ajjuno isi;

Devasabho ca yo thero, sāmidatto mahabbaloti.

The Elder Samitigutta, Kassapa, and the one named Sīha; Nīta, Sunāga, Nāgita, Paviṭṭha, the sage Ajjuna; the Elder Devasabha, and Sāmidatta of great power.

10. Dasamavaggo

10. The Tenth Chapter

1. Paripuṇṇakattheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Paripuṇṇaka

91.

91.

“Na [V 0.0181] tathā mataṃ satarasaṃ, sudhannaṃ yaṃ mayajja paribhuttaṃ;

Aparimitadassinā gotamena, buddhena desito dhammo”ti.

The food of many flavors and the ambrosia are not so cherished as the Dhamma taught by the Buddha, Gotama of limitless vision, which I have enjoyed today.

… Paripuṇṇako thero….

… Thus spoke the Elder Paripuṇṇaka….

2. Vijayattheragāthā

2. The Verses of the Elder Vijaya

92.

92.

“Yassāsavā [T 0.0281][M 0.0240][P 0.0014] parikkhīṇā, āhāre ca anissito;

Suññatā animitto ca, vimokkho yassa gocaro;

Ākāseva sakuntānaṃ, padaṃ tassa durannaya”nti.

For whom the taints are destroyed, who is not dependent in regard to food, whose pasture is emptiness, the signless, and liberation—his track is as hard to trace as that of birds in the sky.

… Vijayo thero….

Thus the Elder Vijaya spoke this verse.

3. Erakattheragāthā

3. The Verse of the Elder Eraka

93.

93.

“Dukkhā kāmā eraka, na sukhā kāmā eraka;

Yo kāme kāmayati, dukkhaṃ so kāmayati eraka;

Yo kāme na kāmayati, dukkhaṃ so na kāmayati erakā”ti.

Sensual pleasures are suffering, Eraka; sensual pleasures are not happiness, Eraka. Whoever desires sensual pleasures, desires suffering, Eraka. Whoever does not desire sensual pleasures, does not desire suffering, Eraka.

… Erako thero….

Thus the Elder Eraka spoke this verse.

4. Mettajittheragāthā

4. The Verse of the Elder Mettaji

94.

94.

“Namo hi tassa bhagavato, sakyaputtassa sirīmato;

Tenāyaṃ aggappattena, aggadhammo aggo dhammo (sī.) sudesito”ti.

Homage to that Blessed One, the glorious son of the Sakyans. By him, who has reached the supreme, this supreme Dhamma has been well taught.

… Mettaji thero….

Thus the Elder Mettaji spoke this verse.

5. Cakkhupālattheragāthā

5. The Verse of the Elder Cakkhupāla

95.

95.

“Andhohaṃ hatanettosmi, kantāraddhānapakkhando pakkhanno (sī.), pakkanto (syā. sī. aṭṭha.);

Sayamānopi gacchissaṃ, na sahāyena pāpenā”ti.

I am blind, my eyes are destroyed; I travel a long road through the wilderness. Even if I have to crawl, I will go on, but not with an evil companion.

… Cakkhupālo thero….

Thus the Elder Cakkhupāla spoke this verse.

6. Khaṇḍasumanattheragāthā

6. The Verse of the Elder Khaṇḍasumana

96.

96.

“Ekapupphaṃ [V 0.0182] cajitvāna, asīti asītiṃ (sī.) vassakoṭiyo;

Saggesu paricāretvā, sesakenamhi nibbuto”ti.

Having offered a single flower, for eighty crores of years I enjoyed bliss in the heavens; with the remainder of that kamma, I have become extinguished.

… Khaṇḍasumano thero….

Thus the Elder Khaṇḍasumana spoke this verse.

7. Tissattheragāthā

7. The Verse of the Elder Tissa

97.

97.

“Hitvā satapalaṃ kaṃsaṃ, sovaṇṇaṃ satarājikaṃ;

Aggahiṃ mattikāpattaṃ, idaṃ dutiyābhisecana”nti.

Having abandoned a golden bowl of a hundred palas, with many engravings, I took up an earthen bowl. This is the second consecration.

… Tisso thero….

Thus the Elder Tissa spoke this verse.

8. Abhayattheragāthā

8. The Verse of the Elder Abhaya

98.

98.

“Rūpaṃ [T 0.0282][M 0.0241] disvā sati muṭṭhā, piyaṃ nimittaṃ manasikaroto;

Sārattacitto vedeti, tañca ajjhosa tiṭṭhati;

Tassa vaḍḍhanti āsavā, bhavamūlopagāmino”ti bhavamūlā bhavagāminoti (sī. ka.).

Upon seeing a form, mindfulness is lost for one who attends to a pleasing sign. With a passionate mind one experiences it and abides engrossed in it. For such a one, the taints, which lead to the root of existence, increase.

… Abhayo thero….

Thus the Elder Abhaya spoke this verse.

9. Uttiyattheragāthā

9. The Verse of the Elder Uttiya

99.

99.

“Saddaṃ sutvā sati muṭṭhā, piyaṃ nimittaṃ manasikaroto;

Sārattacitto vedeti, tañca ajjhosa tiṭṭhati;

Tassa vaḍḍhanti āsavā, saṃsāraṃ upagāmino”ti.

Upon hearing a sound, mindfulness is lost for one who attends to a pleasing sign. With a passionate mind one experiences it and abides engrossed in it. For such a one, the taints, which lead to saṃsāra, increase.

… Uttiyo thero….

Thus the Elder Uttiya spoke this verse.

10. (Dutiya)-devasabhattheragāthā

10. The Verse of the Elder Devasabha (the Second)

100.

100.

“Sammappadhānasampanno, satipaṭṭhānagocaro;

Vimuttikusumasañchanno, parinibbissatyanāsavo”ti.

Endowed with the right strivings, resorting to the establishments of mindfulness, adorned with the flower of liberation, being free from taints, one will attain final Nibbāna.

… Devasabho thero….

Thus the Elder Devasabha spoke this verse.

Vaggo dasamo niṭṭhito.

The tenth chapter is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this chapter:

Paripuṇṇako ca vijayo, erako mettajī muni;

Cakkhupālo khaṇḍasumano, tisso ca abhayo tathā;

Uttiyo ca mahāpañño, thero devasabhopi cāti.

Paripuṇṇaka and Vijaya, Eraka, Mettaji the sage; Cakkhupāla, Khaṇḍasumana, Tissa, and likewise Abhaya; Uttiya of great wisdom, and also the Elder Devasabha.

11. Ekādasamavaggo

11. The Eleventh Chapter

1. Belaṭṭhānikattheragāthā

1. The Verse of the Elder Belaṭṭhānika

101.

101.

“Hitvā [V 0.0183][P 0.0015] gihittaṃ anavositatto, mukhanaṅgalī odariko kusīto;

Mahāvarāhova [T 0.0283] nivāpapuṭṭho, punappunaṃ gabbhamupeti mando”ti.

Having abandoned the household life, but with his task unfinished, harsh in speech, a glutton, and lazy—like a great boar fattened on slops, the fool enters the womb again and again.

… Belaṭṭhāniko thero….

Thus the Elder Belaṭṭhānika spoke this verse.

2. Setucchattheragāthā

2. The Verse of the Elder Setuccha

102.

102.

“Mānena [M 0.0242] vañcitāse, saṅkhāresu saṃkilissamānāse;

Lābhālābhena mathitā, samādhiṃ nādhigacchantī”ti.

Deceived by conceit, being defiled in the formations, crushed by gain and loss, they do not attain concentration.

… Setuccho thero….

Thus the Elder Setuccha spoke this verse.

3. Bandhurattheragāthā

3. The Verse of the Elder Bandhura

103.

103.

“Nāhaṃ etena atthiko, sukhito dhammarasena tappito;

Pitvā pītvāna (sī. syā.) rasaggamuttamaṃ, na ca kāhāmi visena santhava”nti.

I have no need of this; satisfied by the taste of the Dhamma, I am happy. Having drunk the supreme, highest taste, I will not make acquaintance with poison.

… Bandhuro bandhano (ka.) thero….

Thus the Elder Bandhura spoke this verse.

4. Khitakattheragāthā

4. The Verse of the Elder Khitaka

104.

104.

“Lahuko vata me kāyo, phuṭṭho ca pītisukhena vipulena;

Tūlamiva eritaṃ mālutena, pilavatīva me kāyo”ti.

How light indeed is my body, pervaded by abundant joy and happiness! Like a tuft of cotton tossed by the wind, my body seems to float.

… Khitako thero….

… The Elder Khitaka….

5. Malitavambhattheragāthā

5. The Verses of the Elder Malitavambha

105.

105.

“Ukkaṇṭhitopi na vase, ramamānopi pakkame;

Na tvevānatthasaṃhitaṃ, vase vāsaṃ vicakkhaṇo”ti.

One should not remain, even if discontented; one should depart, even if delighting. A discerning person should certainly not take up residence in a dwelling connected with what is unbeneficial.

… Malitavambho thero….

… The Elder Malitavambha….

6. Suhemantattheragāthā

6. The Verses of the Elder Suhemanta

106.

106.

“Sataliṅgassa [V 0.0184] atthassa, satalakkhaṇadhārino;

Ekaṅgadassī dummedho, satadassī ca paṇḍito”ti.

Of a matter that has a hundred signs and bears a hundred characteristics, the one of little wisdom sees only a single aspect, whereas the wise one sees the hundred.

… Suhemanto thero….

… The Elder Suhemanta….

7. Dhammasavattheragāthā

7. The Verses of the Elder Dhammasava

107.

107.

“Pabbajiṃ [M 0.0243] tulayitvāna, agārasmānagāriyaṃ;

Tisso [T 0.0284] vijjā anuppattā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsana”nti.

Having reflected, I went forth from the home life into homelessness. The three true knowledges have been attained; the Buddha’s teaching has been fulfilled.

… Dhammasavo thero….

… The Elder Dhammasava….

8. Dhammasavapituttheragāthā

8. The Verses of the Elder, Father of Dhammasava

108.

108.

“Sa vīsavassasatiko, pabbajiṃ anagāriyaṃ;

Tisso vijjā anuppattā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsana”nti.

Being one hundred and twenty years of age, I went forth into homelessness. The three true knowledges have been attained; the Buddha’s teaching has been fulfilled.

… Dhammasavapitu thero….

… The Elder, Father of Dhammasava….

9. Saṅgharakkhitattheragāthā

9. The Verses of the Elder Saṅgharakkhita

109.

109.

“Na [P 0.0016] nūnāyaṃ paramahitānukampino, rahogato anuvigaṇeti sāsanaṃ;

Tathāhayaṃ viharati pākatindriyo, migī yathā taruṇajātikā vane”ti.

Surely this one does not reflect in seclusion on the teaching of the one compassionate for the highest welfare; for he dwells with faculties exposed, like a young doe in the forest.

… Saṅgharakkhito thero….

… The Elder Saṅgharakkhita….

10. Usabhattheragāthā

10. The Verses of the Elder Usabha

110.

110.

“Nagā nagaggesu susaṃvirūḷhā, udaggameghena navena sittā;

Vivekakāmassa araññasaññino, janeti bhiyyo usabhassa kalyata”nti.

The trees, well-grown on the mountain peaks, sprinkled by a new, rising rain cloud, generate even more fitness of mind for Usabha, who desires seclusion and is mindful of the forest.

… Usabho thero….

… The Elder Usabha….

Vaggo ekādasamo niṭṭhito.

The Eleventh Chapter is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse:

Belaṭṭhāniko setuccho, bandhuro khitako isi;

Malitavambho suhemanto, dhammasavo dhammasavapitā;

Saṅgharakkhitatthero [T 0.0285] ca, usabho ca mahāmunīti.

Belaṭṭhānika, Setuccha, Bandhana, Khitaka the seer, Malitavambha, Suhemanta, Dhammasava, Dhammasava’s Father, the Elder Saṅgharakkhita, and Usabha the great sage.

12. Dvādasamavaggo

12. The Twelfth Chapter

1. Jentattheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Jenta

111.

111.

“Duppabbajjaṃ [M 0.0244][V 0.0185] ve duradhivāsā gehā, dhammo gambhīro duradhigamā bhogā;

Kicchā vutti no itarītareneva, yuttaṃ cintetuṃ satatamaniccata”nti.

Indeed, renunciation is very difficult; houses are difficult to dwell in. The Dhamma is profound; possessions are difficult to obtain. Our livelihood is difficult, maintained only by one requisite or another. It is fitting to constantly contemplate impermanence.

… Jento thero….

… The Elder Jenta….

2. Vacchagottattheragāthā

2. The Verses of the Elder Vacchagotta

112.

112.

“Tevijjohaṃ mahājhāyī, cetosamathakovido;

Sadattho me anuppatto, kataṃ buddhassa sāsana”nti.

I am one with the three knowledges, a great meditator, skilled in the calming of the mind. My own welfare has been attained; the Buddha’s teaching has been fulfilled.

… Vacchagotto thero….

… The Elder Vacchagotta….

3. Vanavacchattheragāthā

3. The Verses of the Elder Vanavaccha

113.

113.

“Acchodikā puthusilā,gonaṅgulamigāyutā;

Ambusevālasañchannā, te selā ramayanti ma”nti.

With clear waters and broad stones, frequented by langurs and deer, and covered with moss—those rocky mountains delight me.

… Vanavaccho thero….

… The Elder Vanavaccha….

4. Adhimuttattheragāthā

4. The Verses of the Elder Adhimutta

114.

114.

“Kāyaduṭṭhullagaruno, hiyyamānamhi hīyamānamhi (sī.) jīvite;

Sarīrasukhagiddhassa, kuto samaṇasādhutā”ti.

For one who is heavy with the coarseness of the body, as life is declining, for one who is greedy for bodily pleasure, whence is the goodness of a recluse?

… Adhimutto thero….

… The Elder Adhimutta….

5. Mahānāmattheragāthā

5. The Verses of the Elder Mahānāma

115.

115.

“Esāvahiyyase pabbatena, bahukuṭajasallakikena sallakitena (sī.), sallarikena (syā.);

Nesādakena [T 0.0286] girinā, yasassinā paricchadenā”ti.

You are falling away from this renowned mountain, Nesādaka, which is abundant with kuṭaja and sallakī trees and covered with a retinue of various trees and vines.

… Mahānāmo thero….

… The Elder Mahānāma….

6. Pārāpariyattheragāthā

6. The Verses of the Elder Pārāpariya

116.

116.

“Chaphassāyatane [M 0.0245][V 0.0186][P 0.0017] hitvā, guttadvāro susaṃvuto;

Aghamūlaṃ vamitvāna, patto me āsavakkhayo”ti.

Having abandoned the six bases of contact, with guarded doors and well-restrained, having vomited out the root of evil, I have attained the destruction of the taints.

… Pārāpariyo pārāsariyo (sī.), pāraṃpariyo (ka.) thero ….

… The Elder Pārāpariya …

7. Yasattheragāthā

7. The Verses of the Elder Yasa

117.

117.

“Suvilitto suvasano,sabbābharaṇabhūsito;

Tisso vijjā ajjhagamiṃ, kataṃ buddhassa sāsana”nti.

Well-anointed, well-dressed, adorned with all ornaments, I have attained the three knowledges; the Buddha’s teaching has been done.

… Yaso thero….

… The Elder Yasa …

8. Kimilattheragāthā

8. The Verses of the Elder Kimila

118.

118.

“Abhisattova nipatati, vayo rūpaṃ aññamiva tatheva santaṃ;

Tasseva sato avippavasato, aññasseva sarāmi attāna”nti.

As if urged on, it falls away—this youth, this form. Though it is just as it is, it seems like another. Though I am present and not parted from it, I perceive myself as if I were another.

… Kimilo kimbilo (sī. syā.) thero….

… The Elder Kimila …

9. Vajjiputtattheragāthā

9. The Verses of the Elder Vajjiputta

119.

119.

“Rukkhamūlagahanaṃ pasakkiya, nibbānaṃ hadayasmiṃ opiya;

Jhāya gotama mā ca pamādo, kiṃ te biḷibiḷikā karissatī”ti.

Having gone to a thicket at the root of a tree, placing Nibbāna in your heart, meditate, Gotama, and be not heedless. What will chattering do for you?

… Vajjiputto thero….

… The Elder Vajjiputta …

10. Isidattattheragāthā

10. The Verses of the Elder Isidatta

120.

120.

“Pañcakkhandhā pariññātā, tiṭṭhanti chinnamūlakā;

Dukkhakkhayo [T 0.0287] anuppatto,patto me āsavakkhayo”ti.

The five aggregates have been fully understood; with their root cut, they remain. The destruction of suffering has been reached; I have attained the destruction of the taints.

… Isidatto thero….

… The Elder Isidatta …

Vaggo dvādasamo niṭṭhito.

The Twelfth Section is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ [V 0.0187] –

The summary thereof:

Jento [M 0.0246] ca vacchagotto ca, vaccho ca vanasavhayo;

Adhimutto mahānāmo, pārāpariyo yasopi ca;

Kimilo vajjiputto ca, isidatto mahāyasoti.

Jenta, Vacchagotta, Vaccha named Vana, Adhimutta, Mahānāma, Pārāpariya, and Yasa, Kimila, Vajjiputta, and Isidatta of great renown.

Ekakanipāto niṭṭhito.

The Book of Ones is finished.

Tatruddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Vīsuttarasataṃ therā, katakiccā anāsavā;

Ekakeva nipātamhi, susaṅgītā mahesibhīti.

One hundred and twenty elders, their task completed, free from taints, in this very Book of Ones, have been well recited by the great seers.

2. Dukanipāto

2. The Book of Twos

1. Paṭhamavaggo

1. The First Section

1. Uttarattheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Uttara

121.

121.

“Natthi [M 0.0247][V 0.0188][P 0.0018] koci bhavo nicco, saṅkhārā vāpi sassatā;

Uppajjanti ca te khandhā, cavanti aparāparaṃ.

No becoming whatsoever is permanent, nor are formations eternal. Those aggregates arise and pass away, again and again.

122.

122.

“Etamādīnaṃ ñatvā, bhavenamhi anatthiko;

Nissaṭo sabbakāmehi, patto me āsavakkhayo”ti.

Knowing this peril, I have no interest in becoming. Released from all sensual pleasures, I have attained the destruction of the taints.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā uttaro thero gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus the venerable Elder Uttara spoke these verses.

2. Piṇḍolabhāradvājattheragāthā

2. The Verses of the Elder Piṇḍolabhāradvāja

123.

123.

“Nayidaṃ [T 0.0288] anayena jīvitaṃ, nāhāro hadayassa santiko;

Āhāraṭṭhitiko samussayo, iti disvāna carāmi esanaṃ.

This life is not sustained by improper means, nor is food for the heart’s appeasement. The body is sustained by food—seeing this, I wander on my alms round.

124.

124.

“Paṅkoti hi naṃ pavedayuṃ, yāyaṃ vandanapūjanā kulesu;

Sukhumaṃ sallaṃ durubbahaṃ, sakkāro kāpurisena dujjaho”ti.

For they have declared it to be ‘mire’—this homage and veneration among families. It is a subtle dart, hard to extract; honor is hard for a base person to relinquish.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā piṇḍolabhāradvājo thero gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus the venerable Elder Piṇḍolabhāradvāja spoke these verses.

3. Valliyattheragāthā

3. The Verses of the Elder Valliya

125.

125.

“Makkaṭo pañcadvārāyaṃ, kuṭikāyaṃ pasakkiya;

Dvārena anupariyeti, ghaṭṭayanto muhuṃ muhuṃ.

A monkey, having entered the five-doored hut, roams about from door to door, striking them again and again.

126.

126.

“Tiṭṭha makkaṭa mā dhāvi, na hi te taṃ yathā pure;

Niggahītosi paññāya, neva dūraṃ gamissatī”ti.

Stay, monkey, do not run! It is not for you as it was before. You are restrained by wisdom; you will not go far from here.

… Valliyo thero….

… The Elder Valliya …

4. Gaṅgātīriyattheragāthā

4. The Verses of the Elder Gaṅgātīriya

127.

127.

“Tiṇṇaṃ [M 0.0248][V 0.0189] me tālapattānaṃ, gaṅgātīre kuṭī katā;

Chavasittova me patto, paṃsukūlañca cīvaraṃ.

My hut of three palm leaves is made on the bank of the Ganges; my bowl is like a vessel for a corpse, and my robe a dust-heap rag.

128.

128.

“Dvinnaṃ antaravassānaṃ, ekā vācā me bhāsitā;

Tatiye antaravassamhi, tamokhandho tamokkhandho (sī. syā.) padālito”ti.

During two rains-retreats, only a single word was spoken by me; in the third rains-retreat, the mass of darkness was split asunder.

… Gaṅgātīriyo thero….

… The Elder Gaṅgātīriya …

5. Ajinattheragāthā

5. The Verses of the Elder Ajina

129.

129.

“Api ce hoti tevijjo, maccuhāyī anāsavo;

Appaññātoti naṃ bālā, avajānanti ajānatā.

Even if one possesses the three knowledges, has left death behind, and is free from taints, fools, in their ignorance, disregard him as someone unknown.

130.

130.

“Yo [P 0.0019] ca kho annapānassa, lābhī hotīdha puggalo;

Pāpadhammopi ce hoti, so nesaṃ hoti sakkato”ti.

Indeed, whoever in this world is a recipient of food and drink, even if they are of evil disposition, is honored by them.

… Ajino thero….

… the Elder Ajina …

6. Meḷajinattheragāthā

6. The Verses of the Elder Meḷajina

131.

131.

“Yadāhaṃ [T 0.0289] dhammamassosiṃ, bhāsamānassa satthuno;

Na kaṅkhamabhijānāmi, sabbaññūaparājite.

When I heard the Dhamma from the Teacher as he was speaking, I have never known doubt in the All-Knowing, the Unconquered One.

132.

132.

“Satthavāhe mahāvīre, sārathīnaṃ varuttame;

Magge paṭipadāyaṃ vā, kaṅkhā mayhaṃ na vijjatī”ti.

In the caravan leader, the Great Hero, the most excellent of charioteers, for me there exists no doubt regarding the path or the practice.

… Meḷajino thero….

… the Elder Meḷajina …

7. Rādhattheragāthā

7. The Verses of the Elder Rādha

133.

133.

dha. pa. 13 dhammapade “Yathā agāraṃ ducchannaṃ, vuṭṭhī samativijjhati;

Evaṃ abhāvitaṃ cittaṃ, rāgo samativijjhati.

Just as an ill-thatched house is penetrated by rain, so an uncultivated mind is penetrated by lust.

134.

134.

dha. pa. 14 dhammapade “Yathā agāraṃ succhannaṃ, vuḍḍhī na samativijjhati;

Evaṃ subhāvitaṃ cittaṃ, rāgo na samativijjhatī”ti.

Just as a well-thatched house is not penetrated by rain, so a well-cultivated mind is not penetrated by lust.

… Rādho thero….

… the Elder Rādha …

8. Surādhattheragāthā

8. The Verses of the Elder Surādha

135.

135.

“Khīṇā [M 0.0249][V 0.0190] hi mayhaṃ jāti, vusitaṃ jinasāsanaṃ;

Pahīno jālasaṅkhāto, bhavanetti samūhatā.

Destroyed for me is birth, the Conqueror's teaching has been lived. That which is known as the net is abandoned, the guide to becoming is uprooted.

136.

136.

“Yassatthāya pabbajito, agārasmānagāriyaṃ;

So me attho anuppatto, sabbasaṃyojanakkhayo”ti.

The purpose for which I went forth from the home life into homelessness—that purpose has been attained by me: the destruction of all fetters.

… Surādho thero….

… the Elder Surādha …

9. Gotamattheragāthā

9. The Verses of the Elder Gotama

137.

137.

“Sukhaṃ supanti munayo, ye itthīsu na bajjhare;

Sadā ve rakkhitabbāsu, yāsu saccaṃ sudullabhaṃ.

Happily sleep the sages who are not bound in regard to women—in whom, who must ever be guarded, truth is very hard to find.

138.

138.

“Vadhaṃ carimha te kāma, anaṇā dāni te mayaṃ;

Gacchāma dāni nibbānaṃ, yattha gantvā na socatī”ti.

We have practiced for your destruction, O sensual pleasures; now we are debtless to you. Now we go to Nibbāna, where, having gone, one does not grieve.

… Gotamo thero….

… the Elder Gotama …

10. Vasabhattheragāthā

10. The Verses of the Elder Vasabha

139.

139.

“Pubbe [T 0.0290] hanati attānaṃ, pacchā hanati so pare;

Suhataṃ hanti attānaṃ, vītaṃseneva pakkhimā.

First he destroys himself, and afterwards he destroys others. He utterly destroys himself, just as a decoy bird destroys other birds.

140.

140.

“Na brāhmaṇo bahivaṇṇo, anto vaṇṇo hi brāhmaṇo;

Yasmiṃ pāpāni kammāni, sa ve kaṇho sujampatī”ti.

One is not a brahmin by outward appearance; a brahmin is so by inner quality. He in whom there are evil deeds, he is indeed a dark one, O Sujampati.

… Vasabho thero….

… the Elder Vasabha …

Vaggo paṭhamo niṭṭhito.

The First Chapter is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Uttaro ceva piṇḍolo, valliyo tīriyo isi;

Ajino ca meḷajino, rādho surādho gotamo;

Vasabhena ime honti, dasa therā mahiddhikāti.

Uttara and Piṇḍola, Valliya, Tīriya the seer, Ajina and Meḷajina, Rādha, Surādha, and Gotama; together with Vasabha, these are the ten elders of great psychic power.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter

1. Mahācundattheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Mahācunda

141.

141.

“Sussūsā [M 0.0250][V 0.0191][P 0.0020] sutavaddhanī, sutaṃ paññāya vaddhanaṃ;

Paññāya atthaṃ jānāti, ñāto attho sukhāvaho.

Eager listening increases learning; learning is an augmenter of wisdom. By wisdom one understands the meaning, and the meaning understood brings happiness.

142.

142.

“Sevetha pantāni senāsanāni, careyya saṃyojanavippamokkhaṃ;

Sace ratiṃ nādhigaccheyya tattha, saṅghe vase rakkhitatto satimā”ti.

One should resort to secluded lodgings; one should practice for release from the fetters. If one should not find delight there, one should live in the Sangha, self-guarded and mindful.

… Mahācundo thero….

… the Elder Mahācunda …

2. Jotidāsattheragāthā

2. The Verses of the Elder Jotidāsa

143.

143.

“Ye kho te veṭhamissena veghamissena (sī. syā.), ve gamissena, vekhamissena (ka.), nānattena ca kammunā;

Manusse uparundhanti, pharusūpakkamā janā;

Tepi [T 0.0291] tattheva kīranti, na hi kammaṃ panassati.

Those people of harsh undertakings who oppress humans by ensnaring and by various actions—they too are treated in that very same way, for a deed does not perish.

144.

144.

“Yaṃ karoti naro kammaṃ, kalyāṇaṃ yadi pāpakaṃ;

Tassa tasseva dāyādo, yaṃ yaṃ kammaṃ pakubbatī”ti.

Whatever deed a person does, be it good or evil, of that very deed they are the heir, whatever deed they perform.

… Jotidāso thero….

… the Elder Jotidāsa …

3. Heraññakānittheragāthā

3. The Verses of the Elder Heraññakāni

145.

145.

“Accayanti ahorattā, jīvitaṃ uparujjhati;

Āyu khīyati maccānaṃ, kunnadīnaṃva odakaṃ.

Days and nights pass away, life is brought to an end; the lifespan of mortals wastes away, like the water of small rivers.

146.

146.

“Atha pāpāni kammāni, karaṃ bālo na bujjhati;

Pacchāssa kaṭukaṃ hoti, vipāko hissa pāpako”ti.

And so the fool, doing evil deeds, does not understand; afterwards, it is bitter for him, for his result is evil.

… Heraññakānitthero….

… the Elder Heraññakāni …

4. Somamittattheragāthā

4. The Verses of the Elder Somamitta

147.

147.

“Parittaṃ dārumāruyha, yathā sīde mahaṇṇave;

Evaṃ kusītamāgamma, sādhujīvīpi sīdati;

Tasmā taṃ parivajjeyya, kusītaṃ hīnavīriyaṃ.

Just as one, having mounted a small piece of wood, would sink in the great ocean, so too, by depending on a lazy person, even one who lives well sinks. Therefore, one should avoid that lazy person of inferior energy.

148.

148.

“Pavivittehi [M 0.0251][V 0.0192] ariyehi, pahitattehi jhāyibhi;

Niccaṃ āraddhavīriyehi, paṇḍitehi sahāvase”ti.

One should associate with the noble ones who are secluded, resolute, meditative, constantly energetic, and wise.

… Somamitto thero….

… the Elder Somamitta …

5. Sabbamittattheragāthā

5. The Verses of the Elder Sabbamitta

149.

149.

“Jano janamhi sambaddho sambaddho (syā. ka.), janamevassito jano;

Jano janena heṭhīyati, heṭheti ca bodhiyati, bādheti ca (ka.) jano janaṃ.

A person is bound to a person, a person relies on a person; a person is oppressed by a person, and a person oppresses a person.

150.

150.

“Ko [P 0.0021] hi tassa janenattho, janena janitena vā;

Janaṃ ohāya gacchaṃ taṃ, heṭhayitvā bādhayitvā (ka.) bahuṃ jana”nti.

What benefit is there from another person, or from one who is begotten? One goes on, having abandoned people, having oppressed many people.

… Sabbamitto thero….

… the Elder Sabbamitta …

6. Mahākāḷattheragāthā

6. The Verses of the Elder Mahākāḷa

151.

151.

“Kāḷī [T 0.0292] itthī brahatī dhaṅkarūpā, satthiñca bhetvā aparañca satthiṃ;

Bāhañca bhetvā aparañca bāhaṃ, sīsañca bhetvā dadhithālakaṃva;

Esā nisinnā abhisandahitvā.

A dark woman, large, of crow-like appearance, having broken one thigh and then the other thigh, having broken one arm and then the other arm, having smashed the head like a pot of curd—she sits, having put the parts together again.

152.

152.

“Yo ve avidvā upadhiṃ karoti, punappunaṃ dukkhamupeti mando;

Tasmā pajānaṃ upadhiṃ na kayirā, māhaṃ puna bhinnasiro sayissa”nti passissanti (ka.).

Whoever, being ignorant, creates a substrate of existence, the fool encounters suffering again and again. Therefore, a knowing one should not create a substrate, lest I lie down again with a broken head.

… Mahākāḷo thero….

… the Elder Mahākāḷa …

7. Tissattheragāthā

7. The Verses of the Elder Tissa

153.

153.

“Bahū sapatte labhati, muṇḍo saṅghāṭipāruto;

Lābhī annassa pānassa, vatthassa sayanassa ca.

The shaven one, covered by the outer robe, who is an obtainer of food and drink, and of clothing and lodging, gains many enemies.

154.

154.

“Etamādīnavaṃ ñatvā, sakkāresu mahabbhayaṃ;

Appalābho anavassuto, sato bhikkhu paribbaje”ti.

Having known this drawback, the great danger in honors, a mindful bhikkhu, with little gain and unattached, should wander.

… Tisso thero….

… the Elder Tissa …

8. Kimilattheragāthā

8. The Verses of the Elder Kimila

155.

155.

“Pācīnavaṃsadāyamhi[M 0.0252], sakyaputtā sahāyakā;

Pahāyānappake bhoge, uñchāpattāgate ratā.

In the forest grove of Pācinavaṃsa, the Sakyan sons, who were companions, having abandoned abundant wealth, delight in what is received from gleanings and in the alms bowl.

156.

156.

“Āraddhavīriyā [V 0.0193] pahitattā, niccaṃ daḷhaparakkamā;

Ramanti dhammaratiyā, hitvāna lokiyaṃ rati”nti.

With aroused energy and resolute minds, always of firm exertion, they delight in the pleasure of the Dhamma, having abandoned worldly pleasure.

… Kimilo kimbilo (sī. syā. pī.) thero….

… the Elder Kimila…

9. Nandattheragāthā

9. The Verses of the Elder Nanda

157.

157.

“Ayoniso [T 0.0293] manasikārā, maṇḍanaṃ anuyuñjisaṃ;

Uddhato capalo cāsiṃ, kāmarāgena aṭṭito.

Through unwise attention, I pursued adornment; I was agitated and fickle, afflicted by sensual lust.

158.

158.

“Upāyakusalenāhaṃ, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Yoniso paṭipajjitvā, bhave cittaṃ udabbahi”nti.

Through the Buddha, skillful in means, the Kinsman of the Sun, having practiced wisely, I lifted up my mind from existence.

… Nando thero….

… the Elder Nanda…

10. Sirimattheragāthā

10. The Verses of the Elder Sirimā

159.

159.

“Pare ca naṃ pasaṃsanti, attā ce asamāhito;

Moghaṃ pare pasaṃsanti, attā hi asamāhito.

Others may praise him, but if he himself is uncomposed, their praise is in vain, for he himself is uncomposed.

160.

160.

“Pare ca naṃ garahanti, attā ce susamāhito;

Moghaṃ pare garahanti, attā hi susamāhito”ti.

Others may blame him, but if he himself is well-composed, their blame is in vain, for he himself is well-composed.

… Sirimā thero….

… the Elder Sirimā…

Vaggo dutiyo niṭṭhito.

The Second Chapter is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse thereof:

Cundo [P 0.0022] ca jotidāso ca, thero heraññakāni ca;

Somamitto sabbamitto, kālo tisso ca kimilo kimbilo (sī. syā. pī.), chandalakkhaṇānulomaṃ;

Nando ca sirimā ceva, dasa therā mahiddhikāti.

Cunda and Jotidāsa, and the Elder Heraññakāni; Somamitta, Sabbamitta, Kāḷa, Tissa, and Kimila; Nanda and Sirimā—these ten elders are of great psychic power.

3. Tatiyavaggo

3. The Third Chapter

1. Uttarattheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Uttara

161.

161.

“Khandhā [M 0.0253][V 0.0194] mayā pariññātā, taṇhā me susamūhatā;

Bhāvitā mama bojjhaṅgā, patto me āsavakkhayo.

The aggregates have been fully understood by me, my craving is thoroughly uprooted; my factors of enlightenment have been developed, I have attained the destruction of the taints.

162.

162.

“Sohaṃ [T 0.0294] khandhe pariññāya, abbahitvāna abbuhitvāna (ka.) jāliniṃ;

Bhāvayitvāna bojjhaṅge, nibbāyissaṃ anāsavo”ti.

Having fully understood the aggregates, having pulled out the net of craving, having developed the factors of enlightenment, free of taints, I will attain final Nibbāna.

… Uttaro thero….

… the Elder Uttara…

2. Bhaddajittheragāthā

2. The Verses of the Elder Bhaddaji

163.

163.

“Panādo nāma so rājā, yassa yūpo suvaṇṇayo;

Tiriyaṃ soḷasubbedho soḷasapabbedho (sī. aṭṭha.), soḷasabbāṇo (?), ubbhamāhu uddhamāhu (sī.), uccamāhu (syā.) sahassadhā.

There was that king named Panāda, whose palace was made of gold; it was sixteen ubbedhas across, and they say it rose a thousand-fold in height.

164.

164.

“Sahassakaṇḍo satageṇḍu, dhajālu haritāmayo;

Anaccuṃ tattha gandhabbā, chasahassāni sattadhā”ti.

It had a thousand storeys and hundreds of pinnacles, was adorned with flags, and made of pure gold; there, six thousand celestial musicians danced in seven places.

… Bhaddajitthero….

… the Elder Bhaddaji…

3. Sobhitattheragāthā

3. The Verses of the Elder Sobhita

165.

165.

“Satimā paññavā bhikkhu, āraddhabalavīriyo;

Pañca kappasatānāhaṃ, ekarattiṃ anussariṃ.

A bhikkhu, mindful and wise, with aroused strength and energy, I recollected five hundred aeons as though in a single night.

166.

166.

“Cattāro satipaṭṭhāne, satta aṭṭha ca bhāvayaṃ;

Pañca kappasatānāhaṃ, ekarattiṃ anussari”nti.

Developing the four foundations of mindfulness, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold path, I recollected five hundred aeons as though it were a single night.

… Sobhito thero….

… The Elder Sobhita…

4. Valliyattheragāthā

4. The Verses of the Elder Valliya

167.

167.

“Yaṃ kiccaṃ daḷhavīriyena, yaṃ kiccaṃ boddhumicchatā;

Karissaṃ nāvarajjhissaṃ nāvarujjhissaṃ (ka. sī. ka.), passa vīriyaṃ parakkama.

Whatever should be done with firm energy, whatever should be done by one wishing to awaken, I will do; I will not fall short. Behold my energy and striving!

168.

168.

“Tvañca me maggamakkhāhi, añjasaṃ amatogadhaṃ;

Ahaṃ monena monissaṃ, gaṅgāsotova sāgara”nti.

And you, declare to me the path, the straight way plunging into the Deathless. I shall proceed to it, as the current of the Ganges flows to the ocean.

… Valliyo thero….

… The Elder Valliya …

5. Vītasokattheragāthā

5. The Verses of the Elder Vītasoka

169.

169.

“Kese [M 0.0254][V 0.0195] me olikhissanti, kappako upasaṅkami;

Tato [T 0.0295] ādāsamādāya, sarīraṃ paccavekkhisaṃ.

The barber approached, intending to cut my hair; thereupon, taking a mirror, I contemplated my body.

170.

170.

“Tuccho [P 0.0023] kāyo adissittha, andhakāro tamo byagā;

Sabbe coḷā samucchinnā, natthi dāni punabbhavo”ti.

The body was seen as empty; the darkness was dispelled. All the rags of defilement have been cut off; now there is no future becoming.

… Vītasoko thero….

… The Elder Vītasoka …

6. Puṇṇamāsattheragāthā

6. The Verses of the Elder Puṇṇamāsa

171.

171.

“Pañca nīvaraṇe hitvā, yogakkhemassa pattiyā;

Dhammādāsaṃ gahetvāna, ñāṇadassanamattano.

Having abandoned the five hindrances for the attainment of security from the yokes, I took up the Dhamma-mirror of my own knowledge and vision.

172.

172.

“Paccavekkhiṃ imaṃ kāyaṃ, sabbaṃ santarabāhiraṃ;

Ajjhattañca bahiddhā ca, tuccho kāyo adissathā”ti.

I contemplated this entire body, with all that is internal and external. Both internally and externally, the body was seen to be empty.

… Puṇṇamāso thero….

… The Elder Puṇṇamāsa …

7. Nandakattheragāthā

7. The Verses of the Elder Nandaka

173.

173.

“Yathāpi bhaddo ājañño, khalitvā patitiṭṭhati;

Bhiyyo laddāna saṃvegaṃ, adīno vahate dhuraṃ.

Just as a fine thoroughbred, having stumbled, stands firm again; gaining even more spiritual urgency, it bears the yoke undaunted.

174.

174.

“Evaṃ dassanasampannaṃ, sammāsambuddhasāvakaṃ;

Ājānīyaṃ maṃ dhāretha, puttaṃ buddhassa orasa”nti.

Thus you should regard me—perfected in vision, a disciple of the Perfectly Enlightened One—as a thoroughbred, a heart-born son of the Buddha.

… Nandako thero….

… The Elder Nandaka …

8. Bharatattheragāthā

8. The Verses of the Elder Bharata

175.

175.

“Ehi nandaka gacchāma, upajjhāyassa santikaṃ;

Sīhanādaṃ nadissāma, buddhaseṭṭhassa sammukhā.

Come, Nandaka, let us go to the preceptor’s presence; we shall roar a lion’s roar before the Supreme Buddha.

176.

176.

“Yāya no anukampāya, amhe pabbājayī muni;

So no attho anuppatto, sabbasaṃyojanakkhayo”ti.

That purpose for which the Sage ordained us out of compassion—that aim has been attained by us: the destruction of all fetters.

… Bharato thero….

… The Elder Bharata …

9. Bhāradvājattheragāthā

9. The Verses of the Elder Bhāradvāja

177.

177.

“Nadanti [T 0.0296][M 0.0255][V 0.0196] evaṃ sappaññā, sīhāva girigabbhare;

Vīrā vijitasaṅgāmā, jetvā māraṃ savāhaniṃ savāhanaṃ (bahūsu).

Thus do the wise ones roar, like lions in a mountain cavern—heroes, victorious in battle, having conquered Māra with his army.

178.

178.

“Satthā ca pariciṇṇo me, dhammo saṅgho ca pūjito;

Ahañca vitto sumano, puttaṃ disvā anāsava”nti.

The Teacher has been attended to by me, the Dhamma and the Sangha have been revered; and I am delighted and glad at heart, having seen my son free from the taints.

… Bhāradvājo thero….

… The Elder Bhāradvāja …

10. Kaṇhadinnattheragāthā

10. The Verses of the Elder Kaṇhadinna

179.

179.

“Upāsitā sappurisā, sutā dhammā abhiṇhaso;

Sutvāna paṭipajjissaṃ, añjasaṃ amatogadhaṃ.

True persons have been associated with, the Dhamma has been frequently heard; having heard, I shall enter upon the straight path that plunges into the Deathless.

180.

180.

“Bhavarāgahatassa me sato, bhavarāgo puna me na vijjati;

Na cāhu na ca me bhavissati, na ca me etarahi vijjatī”ti.

For me, once afflicted by craving for becoming, that craving is no longer found. It has not been, nor will it be, nor is it present in me now.

… Kaṇhadinno thero….

… The Elder Kaṇhadinna …

Vaggo tatiyo niṭṭhito.

The Third Chapter is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Uttaro bhaddajitthero, sobhito valliyo isi;

Vītasoko ca yo thero, puṇṇamāso ca nandako;

Bharato bhāradvājo ca, kaṇhadinno mahāmunīti.

Uttara, the Elder Bhaddaji, Sobhita, Valliya the sage, Vītasoka the Elder, Puṇṇamāsa and Nandaka, Bharata, Bhāradvāja, and Kaṇhadinna the Great Sage.

4. Catutthavaggo

4. The Fourth Chapter

1. Migasirattheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Migasira

181.

181.

“Yato [P 0.0024] ahaṃ pabbajito, sammāsambuddhasāsane;

Vimuccamāno uggacchiṃ, kāmadhātuṃ upaccagaṃ.

Since I went forth in the Dispensation of the Perfectly Enlightened One, being liberated, I have risen up; I have transcended the sense-sphere realm.

182.

182.

“Brahmuno [T 0.0297][V 0.0197] pekkhamānassa, tato cittaṃ vimucci me;

Akuppā me vimuttīti, sabbasaṃyojanakkhayā”ti.

While the Exalted One was looking on, thereupon my mind was liberated. My liberation is unshakeable, due to the destruction of all fetters.

… Migasiro thero….

… The Elder Migasira …

2. Sivakattheragāthā

2. The Verses of the Elder Sivaka

183.

183.

“Aniccāni [M 0.0256] gahakāni, tattha tattha punappunaṃ;

Gahakāraṃ gahakārakaṃ (sī. pī.) gavesanto, dukkhā jāti punappunaṃ.

Impermanent are the houses built here and there, again and again. Seeking the house-builder, birth is suffering, again and again.

184.

184.

“Gahakāraka diṭṭhosi, puna gehaṃ na kāhasi;

Sabbā te phāsukā bhaggā, thūṇikā thūṇirā (pī. ka.), dhuṇirā (syā.) ca vidālitā padālitā (sī. syā.);

Vimariyādikataṃ cittaṃ, idheva vidhamissatī”ti.

O house-builder, you are seen! You will not build a house again. All your rafters are broken, and your ridge-pole is shattered. The mind has reached the unconditioned; it will be extinguished right here.

… Sivako sīvako (sī.) thero….

… The Elder Sivaka ….

3. Upavāṇattheragāthā

3. The Verses of the Elder Upavāṇa

185.

185.

“Arahaṃ sugato loke, vātehābādhito … bādhito (ka.) muni;

Sace uṇhodakaṃ atthi, munino dehi brāhmaṇa.

The Arahant, the Well-Gone One in the world, the sage is afflicted by a wind ailment. If there is hot water, brahmin, give it to the sage.

186.

186.

“Pūjito pūjaneyyānaṃ pūjanīyānaṃ (sī.), sakkareyyāna sakkato;

Apacitopaceyyānaṃ apacanīyānaṃ (sī.), apacineyyānaṃ (syā.), tassa icchāmi hātave”ti.
