Honored by those worthy of honor, respected by those worthy of respect, revered by those worthy of reverence—I wish to bring it to him.

… Upavāṇo thero….

… The Elder Upavāṇa ….

4. Isidinnattheragāthā

4. The Verses of the Elder Isidinna

187.

187.

“Diṭṭhā mayā dhammadharā upāsakā, kāmā aniccā iti bhāsamānā;

Sārattarattā maṇikuṇḍalesu, puttesu dāresu ca te apekkhā.

I have seen lay followers, upholders of the Dhamma, who say, ‘Sensual pleasures are impermanent.’ Yet they are passionately attached to jeweled earrings, and are full of longing for their sons and wives.

188.

188.

“Addhā na jānanti yatodha dhammaṃ, kāmā [T 0.0298] aniccā iti cāpi āhu;

Rāgañca tesaṃ na balatthi chettuṃ, tasmā sitā puttadāraṃ dhanañcā”ti.

Indeed, they do not truly know the Dhamma here, though they say, ‘Sensual pleasures are impermanent.’ They lack the strength to cut off their passion; therefore, they cling to children, wives, and wealth.

… Isidinno thero….

… The Elder Isidinna ….

5. Sambulakaccānattheragāthā

5. The Verses of the Elder Sambulakaccāna

189.

189.

“Devo [M 0.0257] ca vassati devo ca gaḷagaḷāyati,

Ekako cāhaṃ bherave bile viharāmi;

Tassa mayhaṃ ekakassa bherave bile viharato,

Natthi bhayaṃ vā chambhitattaṃ vā lomahaṃso vā.

The sky rains, the sky thunders, and I dwell alone in a fearsome cave. For me, dwelling alone in that fearsome cave, there is no fear, nor trembling, nor bristling of the hair.

190.

190.

“Dhammatā [V 0.0198] mamasā yassa me, ekakassa bherave bile;

Viharato natthi bhayaṃ vā, chambhitattaṃ vā lomahaṃso vā”ti.

This is my nature: for me, dwelling alone in a fearsome cave, there is no fear, nor trembling, nor bristling of the hair.

… Sambulakaccāno sambahulakaccāno (ka.) thero….

… Thus spoke the Elder Sambulakaccāna …

6. Nitakattheragāthā

6. The Verses of the Elder Nitaka

191.

191.

udā. 34 udānepi “Kassa [P 0.0025] selūpamaṃ cittaṃ, ṭhitaṃ nānupakampati;

Virattaṃ rajanīyesu, kuppanīye na kuppati;

Yassevaṃ bhāvitaṃ cittaṃ, kuto taṃ dukkhamessati.

Whose mind is like a rock, steadfast and unshakeable; dispassionate towards the enticing, not angered by the provoking? For one whose mind is thus developed, from where can suffering come to him?

192.

192.

“Mama selūpamaṃ cittaṃ, ṭhitaṃ nānupakampati;

Virattaṃ rajanīyesu, kuppanīye na kuppati;

Mamevaṃ bhāvitaṃ cittaṃ, kuto maṃ dukkhamessatī”ti.

My mind is like a rock, steadfast and unshakeable; dispassionate towards the enticing, not angered by the provoking. Since my mind is thus developed, from where can suffering come to me?

… Nitako khitako (sī. syā.) thero….

… The Elder Nitaka ….

7. Soṇapoṭiriyattheragāthā

7. The Verses of the Elder Soṇa Poṭiriyaputta

193.

193.

“Na tāva supituṃ hoti, ratti nakkhattamālinī;

Paṭijaggitumevesā, ratti hoti vijānatā.

This is no time for sleep, this night garlanded with stars. For one who knows, this night is for keeping vigil.

194.

194.

“Hatthikkhandhāvapatitaṃ[T 0.0299], kuñjaro ce anukkame;

Saṅgāme me mataṃ seyyo, yañce jīve parājito”ti.

Should I fall from the elephant’s back and the great beast trample upon me, better for me to die in battle than to live on, defeated.

… Soṇo poṭiriyo selissariyo (sī.), poṭṭiriyaputto (syā.) thero ….

… Thus spoke the Elder Soṇa Poṭiriyaputta …

8. Nisabhattheragāthā

8. The Verses of the Elder Nisabha

195.

195.

“Pañca [M 0.0258] kāmaguṇe hitvā, piyarūpe manorame;

Saddhāya gharā nikkhamma, dukkhassantakaro bhave.

Having abandoned the five strands of sensual pleasure, which are dear and delightful to the mind, having gone forth from home out of faith, one should become an ender of suffering.

196.

196.

“Nābhinandāmi maraṇaṃ, nābhinandāmi jīvitaṃ;

Kālañca paṭikaṅkhāmi, sampajāno patissato”ti.

I do not delight in death, I do not delight in life; I await my time, mindful and clearly comprehending.

… Nisabho thero….

… Thus spoke the Elder Nisabha …

9. Usabhattheragāthā

9. The Verses of the Elder Usabha

197.

197.

“Ambapallavasaṅkāsaṃ, aṃse katvāna cīvaraṃ;

Nisinno hatthigīvāyaṃ, gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisiṃ.

Having placed on my shoulder my robe, which resembled a mango sprout, I sat on an elephant’s neck and entered a village for alms-food.

198.

198.

“Hatthikkhandhato [V 0.0199] oruyha, saṃvegaṃ alabhiṃ tadā;

Sohaṃ ditto tadā santo, patto me āsavakkhayo”ti.

Having descended from the elephant’s back, I then experienced a sense of spiritual urgency. I, who at that time was conceited, being agitated, have now attained the destruction of the taints.

… Usabho thero….

… Thus spoke the Elder Usabha …

10. Kappaṭakurattheragāthā

10. The Verses of the Elder Kappaṭakura

199.

199.

“Ayamiti kappaṭo kappaṭakuro, acchāya atibharitāya atibhariyāya (sī. ka.), accaṃ bharāya (syā.);

Amataghaṭikāyaṃ dhammakaṭamatto dhammakaṭapatto (syā. ka. aṭṭha.), dhammakaṭamaggo (sī. aṭṭha.), katapadaṃ jhānāni ocetuṃ.

This Kappaṭakura, though in the sphere of the Deathless, by going too far has a mind like a rag, devoid of the Dhamma. Let him develop the jhānas on the path that has been established.

200.

200.

“Mā [P 0.0026] kho tvaṃ kappaṭa pacālesi, mā tvaṃ upakaṇṇamhi tāḷessaṃ;

Na [T 0.0300] hi na vā (ka.) tvaṃ kappaṭa mattamaññāsi, saṅghamajjhamhi pacalāyamānoti.

Do not nod off, Kappaṭa, lest I admonish you near the ear. Indeed, Kappaṭa, you do not know the measure, nodding off in the midst of the Sangha.

… Kappaṭakuro thero….

Thus the Elder Kappaṭakura spoke these verses.

Vaggo catuttho niṭṭhito.

The Fourth Chapter is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Migasiro [M 0.0259] sivako ca, upavāno ca paṇḍito;

Isidinno ca kaccāno, nitako ca mahāvasī;

Poṭiriyaputto nisabho, usabho kappaṭakuroti.

Migasira, Sivaka, and Upavāna the wise; Isidinna, Kaccāna, Nitaka the great master, Poṭiriyaputta, Nisabha, Usabha, and Kappaṭakura.

5. Pañcamavaggo

5. The Fifth Chapter

1. Kumārakassapattheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Kumārakassapa

201.

201.

“Aho buddhā aho dhammā, aho no satthu sampadā;

Yattha etādisaṃ dhammaṃ, sāvako sacchikāhi”ti.

Oh, the Buddhas! Oh, the Dhammas! Oh, the accomplishment of our Teacher, whereby a disciple can realize such a Dhamma!

202.

202.

“Asaṅkheyyesu kappesu, sakkāyādhigatā ahū;

Tesamayaṃ pacchimako, carimoyaṃ samussayo;

Jātimaraṇasaṃsāro, natthi dāni punabbhavo”ti.

For incalculable eons, identities were acquired. This is the last of them; this is the final bodily frame. The round of birth and death is over; now there is no more renewed existence.

… Kumārakassapo thero….

… The Elder Kumārakassapa ….

2. Dhammapālattheragāthā

2. The Verses of the Elder Dhammapāla

203.

203.

“Yo [V 0.0200] have daharo bhikkhu, yuñjati buddhasāsane;

Jāgaro sa hi suttesu patisuttesu (sī. ka.), amoghaṃ tassa jīvitaṃ.

A young bhikkhu who applies himself to the Buddha's Dispensation, who is wakeful among those who sleep—his life is not in vain.

204.

204.

“Tasmā [T 0.0301] saddhañca sīlañca, pasādaṃ dhammadassanaṃ;

Anuyuñjetha medhāvī, saraṃ buddhāna sāsana”nti.

Therefore a wise person, remembering the Buddha’s Dispensation, should be devoted to faith and virtue, to confidence and the vision of the Dhamma.

… Dhammapālo thero….

… The Elder Dhammapāla ….

3. Brahmālittheragāthā

3. The Verses of the Elder Brahmāli

205.

205.

“Kassindriyāni samathaṅgatāni, assā yathā sārathinā sudantā;

Pahīnamānassa anāsavassa, devāpi kassa tassa (bahūsu) pihayanti tādino”ti.

“Whose faculties have attained a state of calm, like horses well-tamed by a skilled charioteer? For which one who has abandoned conceit, is free from taints, and is steadfast, do even the gods yearn?”

206.

206.

dha. pa. 94 dhammapadepi “Mayhindriyāni [M 0.0260] samathaṅgatāni, assā yathā sārathinā sudantā;

Pahīnamānassa anāsavassa, devāpi mayhaṃ pihayanti tādino”ti.

“My faculties have attained a state of calm, like horses well-tamed by a skilled charioteer. For me, who has abandoned conceit, is free from taints, and is steadfast, do even the gods yearn.”

… Brahmāli thero….

… The Elder Brahmāli ….

4. Mogharājattheragāthā

4. The Verses of the Elder Mogharāja

207.

207.

“Chavipāpaka [P 0.0027] cittabhaddaka, mogharāja satataṃ samāhito;

Hemantikasītakālarattiyo hemantikakālarattiyo (ka.), bhikkhu tvaṃsi kathaṃ karissasi”.

“O Mogharāja, of poor complexion but good mind, ever concentrated, how will you, a bhikkhu, manage during the cold winter nights?”

208.

208.

“Sampannasassā magadhā, kevalā iti me sutaṃ;

Palālacchannako seyyaṃ, yathaññe sukhajīvino”ti.

“The lands of Magadha are entirely rich in crops, so I have heard. I shall make my bed with a covering of straw, just as others who live in comfort do.”

… Mogharājā thero….

… The Elder Mogharāja ….

5. Visākhapañcālaputtattheragāthā

5. The Verses of the Elder Visākha Pañcālaputta

209.

209.

“Na ukkhipe no ca parikkhipe pare, okkhipe pāragataṃ na eraye;

Na [T 0.0302] cattavaṇṇaṃ parisāsu byāhare, anuddhato sammitabhāṇi subbato.

“One should not exalt oneself nor disparage others; one should not look down upon them, nor find fault with one who has gone beyond. One should not proclaim one's own praise in assemblies, but be unagitated, measured in speech, and of good practices.

210.

210.

“Susukhumanipuṇatthadassinā, matikusalena nivātavuttinā;

Saṃsevitavuddhasīlinā, nibbānaṃ na hi tena dullabha”nti.

“For one who sees the very subtle and fine meaning, who is skilled in wisdom and humble in conduct, who cultivates the virtue well-practiced by the Buddhas, Nibbāna is indeed not difficult to obtain.”

… Visākho pañcālaputto thero ….

… The Elder Visākha Pañcālaputta ….

6. Cūḷakattheragāthā

6. The Verses of the Elder Cūḷaka

211.

211.

“Nadanti [V 0.0201] morā susikhā supekhuṇā, sunīlagīvā sumukhā sugajjino;

Susaddalā cāpi mahāmahī ayaṃ, subyāpitambu suvalāhakaṃ nabhaṃ.

“The peacocks cry out, with beautiful crests and plumage, with beautiful blue necks, fair faces, and lovely calls. This great earth is also lush with green grass and well-watered, and the sky has beautiful clouds.

212.

212.

“Sukallarūpo [M 0.0261] sumanassa jhāyataṃ jhāyitaṃ (syā. ka.), sunikkamo sādhu subuddhasāsane;

Susukkasukkaṃ nipuṇaṃ sududdasaṃ, phusāhi taṃ uttamamaccutaṃ pada”nti.

“For one with a good mind who is meditating, the condition is suitable. Excellent is the good practice in the Buddha's good Dispensation. Attain that supreme, unmoving state—exceedingly pure, subtle, and very hard to see.”

… Cūḷako cūlako (sī. aṭṭha.) thero….

… The Elder Cūḷaka ….

7. Anūpamattheragāthā

7. The Verses of the Elder Anūpama

213.

213.

“Nandamānāgataṃ cittaṃ, sūlamāropamānakaṃ;

Tena teneva vajasi, yena sūlaṃ kaliṅgaraṃ.

“The mind that has come to delight is like being placed on a stake. You go to that very place where the stake is, the sprout of existence.

214.

214.

“Tāhaṃ cittakaliṃ brūmi, taṃ brūmi cittadubbhakaṃ;

Satthā te dullabho laddho, mānatthe maṃ niyojayī”ti.

“I call you, O mind, a villain; I call you a treacherous friend. The Teacher, so difficult to find, has been found by you. Do not engage me in what is harmful!”

… Anūpamo thero….

… The Elder Anūpama ….

8. Vajjitattheragāthā

8. The Verses of the Elder Vajjita

215.

215.

“Saṃsaraṃ [T 0.0303] dīghamaddhānaṃ, gatīsu parivattisaṃ;

Apassaṃ ariyasaccāni, andhabhūto andhībhūto (ka.) puthujjano.

“For a long time I wandered, revolving through the destinations; not seeing the Noble Truths, I was a blind worldling.

216.

216.

“Tassa [P 0.0028] me appamattassa, saṃsārā vinaḷīkatā;

Sabbā gatī samucchinnā, natthi dāni punabbhavo”ti.

“For me, being diligent, the round of births has been uprooted; all destinations are cut off; now there is no more renewed existence.”

… Vajjito thero….

… The Elder Vajjita ….

9. Sandhitattheragāthā

9. The Verses of the Elder Sandhita

217.

217.

“Assatthe haritobhāse, saṃvirūḷhamhi pādape;

Ekaṃ buddhagataṃ saññaṃ, alabhitthaṃ alabhiṃ haṃ (ka.) patissato.

“At the assattha tree, king among trees, of verdant hue and luxuriant growth, being mindful, I obtained a singular perception directed toward the Buddha.

218.

218.

“Ekatiṃse ito kappe, yaṃ saññamalabhiṃ tadā;

Tassā saññāya vāhasā, patto me āsavakkhayo”ti.

“Thirty-one eons ago from this one, when I gained that perception; by means of that perception, I have attained the destruction of the taints.”

… Sandhito thero….

… The Elder Sandhita ….

Vaggo pañcamo niṭṭhito.

The Fifth Chapter is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ [V 0.0202] –

The summary for it:

Kumārakassapo [M 0.0262] thero, dhammapālo ca brahmāli;

Mogharājā visākho ca, cūḷako ca anūpamo;

Vajjito sandhito thero, kilesarajavāhanoti.

The Elder Kumārakassapa, and Dhammapāla, and Brahmāli, Mogharāja, and Visākha, and Cūḷaka, and Anūpama, Vajjita, and the Elder Sandhita, who has washed away the dust of defilements.

Dukanipāto niṭṭhito.

The Book of Twos is finished.

Tatruddānaṃ –

The summary therein:

Gāthādukanipātamhi, navuti ceva aṭṭha ca;

Therā ekūnapaññāsaṃ, bhāsitā nayakovidāti.

In the Book of Twos, there are ninety-eight verses; they were spoken by forty-nine Elders skilled in the method.

3. Tikanipāto

3. The Book of Threes

1. Aṅgaṇikabhāradvājattheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Aṅgaṇika Bhāradvāja

219.

219.

“Ayoni [T 0.0304][M 0.0263][V 0.0203][P 0.0029] suddhimanvesaṃ, aggiṃ paricariṃ vane;

Suddhimaggaṃ ajānanto, akāsiṃ amaraṃ tapaṃ akāsiṃ aparaṃ tapaṃ (syā.), akāsiṃ amataṃ tapaṃ (ka.).

Improperly seeking purity, I tended the fire in the forest; not knowing the path to purity, I performed austerities, thinking it the way to the deathless.

220.

220.

“Taṃ sukhena sukhaṃ laddhaṃ, passa dhammasudhammataṃ;

Tisso vijjā anuppattā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ.

That happiness has been gained through happiness—behold the excellent nature of the Dhamma! The three knowledges have been attained; the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

221.

221.

“Brahmabandhu pure āsiṃ, idāni khomhi brāhmaṇo;

Tevijjo nhātako nahātako (sī. aṭṭha.) camhi, sottiyo camhi vedagū”ti.

Formerly I was a kinsman of Brahmā, but now I am truly a brahmin. I am endowed with the three knowledges, one who has bathed, one who is prosperous, and a master of knowledge.

… Aṅgaṇikabhāradvājo thero….

… The Elder Aṅgaṇika-Bhāradvāja …

2. Paccayattheragāthā

2. The Verses of the Elder Paccaya

222.

222.

“Pañcāhāhaṃ pabbajito, sekho appattamānaso,

Vihāraṃ me paviṭṭhassa, cetaso paṇidhī ahu.

For five days I had been gone forth, a trainee with my goal unattained. As I entered my dwelling, a resolution of mind arose:

223.

223.

“Nāsissaṃ na pivissāmi, vihārato na nikkhame;

Napi passaṃ nipātessaṃ, taṇhāsalle anūhate.

“I will not eat, I will not drink, nor will I leave my dwelling; nor will I lay down on my side, until the dart of craving is un-uprooted.”

224.

224.

“Tassa mevaṃ viharato, passa vīriyaparakkamaṃ;

Tisso vijjā anuppattā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsana”nti.

For me, abiding thus—behold my energy and striving! The three knowledges have been attained; the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

… Paccayo thero….

… The Elder Paccaya …

3. Bākulattheragāthā

3. The Verses of the Elder Bākula

225.

225.

“Yo pubbe karaṇīyāni, pacchā so kātumicchati;

Sukhā so dhaṃsate ṭhānā, pacchā ca manutappati.

Whoever wishes to do later what should be done before, falls from a state of happiness and is afterwards remorseful.

226.

226.

“Yañhi kayirā tañhi vade, yaṃ na kayirā na taṃ vade;

Akarontaṃ [T 0.0305] bhāsamānaṃ, parijānanti paṇḍitā.

What one would do, that one should say; what one would not do, that one should not say. The wise fully understand one who speaks but does not act.

227.

227.

“Susukhaṃ [M 0.0264][V 0.0204] vata nibbānaṃ, sammāsambuddhadesitaṃ;

Asokaṃ virajaṃ khemaṃ, yattha dukkhaṃ nirujjhatī”ti.

Oh, how truly blissful is Nibbāna, taught by the Perfectly Enlightened One—sorrowless, dustless, secure, where suffering ceases.

… Bākulo bākkulo (sī.) thero….

… The Elder Bākula …

4. Dhaniyattheragāthā

4. The Verses of the Elder Dhaniya

228.

228.

“Sukhaṃ ce jīvituṃ icche, sāmaññasmiṃ apekkhavā;

Saṅghikaṃ nātimaññeyya, cīvaraṃ pānabhojanaṃ.

If one should wish to live happily, having regard for the state of a recluse, one should not disdain the robes, drink, and food that are the property of the Saṅgha.

229.

229.

“Sukhaṃ ce jīvituṃ icche, sāmaññasmiṃ apekkhavā;

Ahi mūsikasobbhaṃva, sevetha sayanāsanaṃ.

If one should wish to live happily, having regard for the state of a recluse, one should resort to a dwelling and seat, just as a snake resorts to a mouse-hole.

230.

230.

“Sukhaṃ ce [P 0.0030] jīvituṃ icche, sāmaññasmiṃ apekkhavā;

Itarītarena tusseyya, ekadhammañca bhāvaye”ti.

If one should wish to live happily, having regard for the state of a recluse, one should be content with whatever is received, and should develop the one Dhamma.

… Dhaniyo thero….

Thus the Elder Dhaniya spoke these verses.

5. Mātaṅgaputtattheragāthā

5. The Verses of the Elder Mātaṅgaputta

231.

231.

“Atisītaṃ atiuṇhaṃ, atisāyamidaṃ ahu;

Iti vissaṭṭhakammante, khaṇā accenti māṇave.

“‘It is too cold,’ ‘it is too hot,’ ‘it is too late in the evening’—for beings who have abandoned their work in this way, the opportune moments pass by.”

232.

232.

“Yo ca sītañca uṇhañca, tiṇā bhiyyo na maññati;

Karaṃ purisakiccāni, so sukhā na vihāyati.

But one who regards cold and heat as no more than grass, while performing the duties of a man, does not fall away from happiness.

233.

233.

“Dabbaṃ kusaṃ poṭakilaṃ, usīraṃ muñjapabbajaṃ;

Urasā panudissāmi, vivekamanubrūhaya”nti.

Dabba grass, kusa grass, thorny bushes, usīra root, muñja grass, and pabbaja grass—I will push them aside with my chest, cultivating seclusion.

… Mātaṅgaputto thero….

… The Elder Mātaṅgaputta …

6. Khujjasobhitattheragāthā

6. The Verses of the Elder Khujjasobhita

234.

234.

“Ye cittakathī bahussutā, samaṇā pāṭaliputtavāsino;

Tesaññataroyamāyuvā, dvāre tiṭṭhati khujjasobhito.

Among the eloquent and greatly learned recluses dwelling in Pāṭaliputta is a certain venerable one, Khujjasobhita, who stands at the gate.

235.

235.

“Ye [T 0.0306][M 0.0265] cittakathī bahussutā, samaṇā pāṭaliputtavāsino;

Tesaññataroyamāyuvā, dvāre tiṭṭhati māluterito.

Among the eloquent and greatly learned recluses dwelling in Pāṭaliputta is a certain venerable one; impelled by the wind, he stands at the gate.

236.

236.

“Suyuddhena suyiṭṭhena, saṅgāmavijayena ca;

Brahmacariyānuciṇṇena, evāyaṃ sukhamedhatī”ti.

By a good battle, a good offering, victory in combat, and by practicing the holy life—in this way this one experiences happiness.

… Khujjasobhito thero….

… The Elder Khujjasobhita …

7. Vāraṇattheragāthā

7. The Verses of the Elder Vāraṇa

237.

237.

“Yodha [V 0.0205] koci manussesu, parapāṇāni hiṃsati;

Asmā lokā paramhā ca, ubhayā dhaṃsate naro.

Whatever person here among humans harms other living beings, that person falls away from both: from this world and from the next.

238.

238.

“Yo ca mettena cittena, sabbapāṇānukampati;

Bahuñhi so pasavati, puññaṃ tādisako naro.

But one who, with a mind of loving-kindness, has compassion for all beings—such a person indeed generates abundant merit.

239.

239.

“Subhāsitassa sikkhetha, samaṇūpāsanassa ca;

Ekāsanassa ca raho, cittavūpasamassa cā”ti.

One should train in what is well-spoken, and in attending on recluses; and in sitting alone in a secluded place, and in the calming of the mind.

… Vāraṇo thero….

… The Elder Vāraṇa …

8. Vassikattheragāthā

8. The Verses of the Elder Vassika

240.

240.

“Ekopi saddho medhāvī, assaddhānīdha ñātinaṃ;

Dhammaṭṭho sīlasampanno, hoti atthāya bandhunaṃ.

Even a single person here, if faithful and wise, established in the Dhamma and accomplished in virtue, is for the welfare of their faithless kinsmen and relatives.

241.

241.

“Niggayha anukampāya, coditā ñātayo mayā;

Ñātibandhavapemena, kāraṃ katvāna bhikkhusu.

Having admonished them out of compassion, my kinsmen were urged on by me; out of affection for their kinsmen and relatives, they made respectful offerings to the bhikkhus.

242.

242.

“Te abbhatītā kālaṅkatā, pattā te tidivaṃ sukhaṃ;

Bhātaro mayhaṃ mātā ca, modanti kāmakāmino”ti.

They have passed on, having met their time, and have attained the happiness of heaven. My mother and my brothers rejoice, enjoying all the pleasures they desire.

… Vassiko passiko (sī. syā. pī.) thero….

… The Elder Vassika ….

9. Yasojattheragāthā

9. The Verses of the Elder Yasoja

243.

243.

“Kālapabbaṅgasaṅkāso, kiso dhamanisanthato;

Mattaññū [T 0.0307] annapānamhi, adīnamanaso naro”.

With limbs dark as reeds, emaciated, with veins standing out, that man knows the measure in food and drink and is of undaunted mind.

244.

244.

“Phuṭṭho [M 0.0266][P 0.0031] ḍaṃsehi makasehi, araññasmiṃ brahāvane;

Nāgo saṅgāmasīseva, sato tatrādhivāsaye.

Touched by gadflies and mosquitoes in the wilderness, in the great forest, one should mindfully endure there, like an elephant at the head of a battle.

245.

245.

“Yathā brahmā tathā eko, yathā devo tathā duve;

Yathā gāmo tathā tayo, kolāhalaṃ tatuttari”nti.

As a Brahmā, so is one; as a deva, so are two; as a village, so are three; more than that is a clamor.

… Yasojo thero….

… The Elder Yasoja ….

10. Sāṭimattiyattheragāthā

10. The Verses of the Elder Sāṭimattiya

246.

246.

“Ahu [V 0.0206] tuyhaṃ pure saddhā, sā te ajja na vijjati;

Yaṃ tuyhaṃ tuyhamevetaṃ, natthi duccaritaṃ mama.

Formerly you had faith, but today it is not to be found. Let what is yours be yours alone; there is no misconduct on my part.

247.

247.

“Aniccā hi calā saddā, evaṃ diṭṭhā hi sā mayā;

Rajjantipi virajjanti, tattha kiṃ jiyyate muni.

For faith is impermanent and fickle; so have I seen it. People become passionate and then dispassionate. In that, how is a sage diminished?

248.

248.

“Paccati munino bhattaṃ, thokaṃ thokaṃ kule kule;

Piṇḍikāya carissāmi, atthi jaṅghabalaṃ jaṅghābalaṃ (sī.) mamā”ti.

A sage’s meal is cooked little by little in family after family. I will go about for alms-food; I have strength in my legs.

… Sāṭimattiyo thero….

… The Elder Sāṭimattiya ….

11. Upālittheragāthā

11. The Verses of the Elder Upāli

249.

249.

“Saddhāya abhinikkhamma, navapabbajito navo;

Mitte bhajeyya kalyāṇe, suddhājīve atandite.

Having gone forth out of faith, a newly ordained one, a novice, should associate with good friends who are of pure livelihood and diligent.

250.

250.

“Saddhāya abhinikkhamma, navapabbajito navo;

Saṅghasmiṃ viharaṃ bhikkhu, sikkhetha vinayaṃ budho.

Having gone forth out of faith, a newly ordained one, a novice, a wise bhikkhu dwelling in the Saṅgha should train in the Vinaya.

251.

251.

“Saddhāya abhinikkhamma, navapabbajito navo;

Kappākappesu kusalo, careyya apurakkhato”ti.

Having gone forth out of faith, a newly ordained one, a novice, skilled in what is allowable and unallowable, should fare on without being put forward.

… Upālitthero….

… The Elder Upāli ….

12. Uttarapālattheragāthā

12. The Verses of the Elder Uttarapāla

252.

252.

“Paṇḍitaṃ [T 0.0308] vata maṃ santaṃ, alamatthavicintakaṃ;

Pañca kāmaguṇā loke, sammohā pātayiṃsu maṃ.

Though I was wise, one capable of contemplating the goal, the five strands of sensual pleasure in the world caused me to fall into delusion.

253.

253.

“Pakkhando māravisaye, daḷhasallasamappito;

Asakkhiṃ maccurājassa, ahaṃ pāsā pamuccituṃ.

Having rushed into Māra’s domain, pierced by a strong dart, I was able to escape from the snare of the King of Death.

254.

254.

“Sabbe [M 0.0267] kāmā pahīnā me, bhavā sabbe padālitā vidālitā (sī. pī. aṭṭha.);

Vikkhīṇo jātisaṃsāro, natthi dāni punabbhavo”ti.

All sensual pleasures have been abandoned by me, all states of being have been shattered; the round of births is destroyed, now there is no more renewed existence.

… Uttarapālo thero….

… The Elder Uttarapāla ….

13. Abhibhūtattheragāthā

13. The Verses of the Elder Abhibhūta

255.

255.

“Suṇātha ñātayo sabbe, yāvantettha samāgatā;

Dhammaṃ vo desayissāmi, dukkhā jāti punappunaṃ.

Listen, all you kinsmen, however many have assembled here; I will teach you the Dhamma: birth again and again is suffering.

256.

256.

saṃ. ni. 1.185 “Ārambhatha ārabhatha (sī. syā.), ārabbhatha (ka.) nikkamatha, yuñjatha buddhasāsane;

Dhunātha maccuno senaṃ, naḷāgāraṃva kuñjaro.

Strive, go forth, apply yourselves to the Buddha’s Dispensation! Destroy the army of Death, as an elephant destroys a reed hut.

257.

257.

“Yo [V 0.0207] imasmiṃ dhammavinaye, appamatto vihassati vihessati (syā. pī.);

Pahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ, dukkhassantaṃ karissatī”ti.

Whoever dwells heedfully in this Dhamma and Vinaya, having abandoned the round of births, will make an end of suffering.”

… Abhibhūto thero….

… The Elder Abhibhūta ….

14. Gotamattheragāthā

14. The Verses of the Elder Gotama

258.

258.

“Saṃsaraṃ [P 0.0032] hi nirayaṃ agacchissaṃ, petalokamagamaṃ punappunaṃ;

Dukkhamamhipi tiracchānayoniyaṃ, nekadhā hi vusitaṃ ciraṃ mayā.

Wandering in saṃsāra, I went to hell; again and again I went to the realm of ghosts. In the animal womb, a state of suffering, I have also dwelt for a long time in many ways.

259.

259.

“Mānusopi ca bhavobhirādhito, saggakāyamagamaṃ sakiṃ sakiṃ;

Rūpadhātusu [T 0.0309] arūpadhātusu, nevasaññisu asaññisuṭṭhitaṃ.

A human existence has also been obtained; from time to time I have gone to a heavenly body. I have been established in the form realms and the formless realms, in the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception and among non-percipient beings.

260.

260.

“Sambhavā suviditā asārakā, saṅkhatā pacalitā saderitā;

Taṃ viditvā mahamattasambhavaṃ, santimeva satimā samajjhaga”nti.

Existences are well understood to be essenceless, conditioned, wavering, and agitated. Having understood that and my own existence, being mindful, I have attained peace itself.

… Gotamo thero….

… The Elder Gotama ….

15. Hāritattheragāthā

15. The Verses of the Elder Hārita

261.

261.

“Yo pubbe karaṇīyāni, pacchā so kātumicchati;

Sukhā so dhaṃsate ṭhānā, pacchā ca manutappati.

One who wishes to do later what should be done before falls from his state of happiness, and afterwards he is tormented by remorse.

262.

262.

“Yañhi [M 0.0268] kayirā tañhi vade, yaṃ na kayirā na taṃ vade;

Akarontaṃ bhāsamānaṃ, parijānanti paṇḍitā.

One should speak only of what one would do; one should not speak of what one would not do. The wise discern one who speaks but does not act.

263.

263.

“Susukhaṃ vata nibbānaṃ, sammāsambuddhadesitaṃ;

Asokaṃ virajaṃ khemaṃ, yattha dukkhaṃ nirujjhatī”ti.

Oh, how extremely blissful is Nibbāna, taught by the Perfectly Enlightened One! It is sorrowless, stainless, and secure, where suffering ceases.

… Hārito thero….

… The Elder Hārita ….

16. Vimalattheragāthā

16. The Verses of the Elder Vimala

264.

264.

“Pāpamitte vivajjetvā, bhajeyyuttamapuggalaṃ;

Ovāde cassa tiṭṭheyya, patthento acalaṃ sukhaṃ.

Having avoided evil friends, one should associate with the best of persons; one should stand in his instruction, aspiring for unshakable happiness.

265.

265.

“Parittaṃ dārumāruyha, yathā sīde mahaṇṇave;

Evaṃ kusītamāgamma, sādhujīvīpi sīdati;

Tasmā taṃ parivajjeyya, kusītaṃ hīnavīriyaṃ.

Just as one who boards a small plank would sink in the great ocean, so even one who lives well sinks when relying on a lazy person. Therefore one should avoid that lazy person who is deficient in energy.

266.

266.

“Pavivittehi [V 0.0208] ariyehi, pahitattehi jhāyibhi;

Niccaṃ [T 0.0310] āraddhavīriyehi, paṇḍitehi sahāvase”ti.

One should live together with the secluded, noble ones, with those of resolute mind who are absorbed in jhāna, with the wise who are ever energetic.

… Vimalo thero….

… The Elder Vimala …

Tikanipāto niṭṭhito.

The Book of the Threes is finished.

Tatruddānaṃ –

The summary therein:

Aṅgaṇiko bhāradvājo, paccayo bākulo isi;

Dhaniyo mātaṅgaputto, sobhito vāraṇo isi.

Aṅgaṇika Bhāradvāja, Paccaya, Bākula the sage; Dhaniya, Mātaṅgaputta, Sobhita, Vāraṇa the sage.

Vassiko ca yasojo ca, sāṭimattiyupāli ca;

Uttarapālo abhibhūto, gotamo hāritopi ca.

Vassika and Yasoja, Sāṭimattiya and Upāli; Uttarapāla, Abhibhūta, Gotama, and also Hārita.

Thero tikanipātamhi, nibbāne vimalo kato;

Aṭṭhatālīsa gāthāyo, therā soḷasa kittitāti.

In the Book of the Threes, the Elder Vimala has become stainless in Nibbāna. Sixteen elders are proclaimed, and forty-eight verses.

4. Catukanipāto

4. The Book of the Fours

1. Nāgasamālattheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Nāgasamāla

267.

267.

“Alaṅkatā [M 0.0269][V 0.0209][P 0.0033] suvasanā, mālinī candanussadā;

Majjhe mahāpathe nārī, turiye naccati naṭṭakī.

Adorned and well-dressed, wearing garlands, smeared with sandalwood, a female dancer was dancing to music in the middle of the highway.

268.

268.

“Piṇḍikāya paviṭṭhohaṃ, gacchanto naṃ udikkhisaṃ;

Alaṅkataṃ suvasanaṃ, maccupāsaṃva oḍḍitaṃ.

I had entered for alms-food and, as I was walking, I saw her, adorned and well-dressed, like a snare of Death that had been set.

269.

269.

“Tato me manasīkāro, yoniso udapajjatha;

Ādīnavo pāturahu, nibbidā samatiṭṭhatha sampatiṭṭhatha (ka.).

Then wise attention arose in me; the danger became manifest, and disenchantment was firmly established.

270.

270.

“Tato cittaṃ vimucci me, passa dhammasudhammataṃ;

Tisso [T 0.0311] vijjā anuppattā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsana”nti.

Then my mind was liberated. Behold the excellence of the Dhamma! The three knowledges have been attained; the Buddha’s teaching has been done.

… Nāgasamālo thero….

… The Elder Nāgasamāla …

2. Bhaguttheragāthā

2. The Verses of the Elder Bhagu

271.

271.

“Ahaṃ middhena pakato, vihārā upanikkhamiṃ;

Caṅkamaṃ abhiruhanto, tattheva papatiṃ chamā.

Overcome by drowsiness, I went out from my dwelling; and while ascending the walking path, I fell to the ground right there.

272.

272.

“Gattāni parimajjitvā, punapāruyha caṅkamaṃ;

Caṅkame caṅkamiṃ sohaṃ, ajjhattaṃ susamāhito.

Having rubbed my limbs, I again ascended the walking path. I walked back and forth on the path, inwardly well composed.

273.

273.

“Tato me manasīkāro, yoniso udapajjatha;

Ādīnavo pāturahu, nibbidā samatiṭṭhatha.

Then wise attention arose in me; the danger became manifest, and disenchantment was firmly established.

274.

274.

“Tato cittaṃ vimucci me, passa dhammasudhammataṃ;

Tisso vijjā anuppattā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsana”nti.

Then my mind was liberated. Behold the excellence of the Dhamma! The three true knowledges have been attained; the Buddha’s teaching has been done.

… Bhagutthero….

… The Elder Bhagu …

3. Sabhiyattheragāthā

3. The Verses of the Elder Sabhiya

275.

275.

dha. pa. 6 dhammapadepi “Pare ca na vijānanti, mayamettha yamāmase;

Ye ca tattha vijānanti, tato sammanti medhagā.

Others do not understand that here we shall perish; but those who do understand this, thereby have their quarrels settled.

276.

276.

“Yadā [V 0.0210] ca avijānantā, iriyantyamarā viya;

Vijānanti ca ye dhammaṃ, āturesu anāturā.

While the ignorant conduct themselves as if they were immortal, those who understand the Dhamma are unafflicted among the afflicted.

277.

277.

“Yaṃ [M 0.0270] kiñci sithilaṃ kammaṃ, saṃkiliṭṭhañca yaṃ vataṃ;

Saṅkassaraṃ brahmacariyaṃ, na taṃ hoti mahapphalaṃ.

Whatever deed is slack, whatever observance is defiled, a holy life practiced with misgiving—this is not of great fruit.

278.

278.

“Yassa sabrahmacārīsu, gāravo nūpalabbhati;

Ārakā hoti saddhammā, nabhaṃ puthaviyā yathā”ti.

One in whom no respect is found for his companions in the holy life is as far from the good Dhamma as the sky is from the earth.

… Sabhiyo thero….

… The Elder Sabhiya …

4. Nandakattheragāthā

4. The Verses of the Elder Nandaka

279.

279.

“Dhiratthu [T 0.0312] pūre duggandhe, mārapakkhe avassute;

Navasotāni te kāye, yāni sandanti sabbadā.

Shame on this foul-smelling body, full of filth, leaky, and on Māra’s side. There are nine streams in your body that are always flowing.

280.

280.

“Mā [P 0.0034] purāṇaṃ amaññittho, māsādesi tathāgate;

Saggepi te na rajjanti, kimaṅgaṃ pana kimaṅga pana (sī.) mānuse.

Do not think of the past; do not treat the Tathāgatas with contempt. They are not attached even to heaven, what then to the human realm?

281.

281.

“Ye ca kho bālā dummedhā, dummantī mohapārutā;

Tādisā tattha rajjanti, mārakhittamhi bandhane.

But those fools of little wisdom, of poor counsel, cloaked in delusion—such as these are attached to that, caught in the bond cast by Māra.

282.

282.

“Yesaṃ rāgo ca doso ca, avijjā ca virājitā;

Tādī tattha na rajjanti, chinnasuttā abandhanā”ti.

But those for whom lust, hatred, and ignorance have faded away—such ones are not attached to that. Their thread is cut; they are without bonds.

… Nandako thero….

… The Elder Nandaka …

5. Jambukattheragāthā

5. The Verses of the Elder Jambuka

283.

283.

“Pañcapaññāsavassāni, rajojallamadhārayiṃ;

Bhuñjanto māsikaṃ bhattaṃ, kesamassuṃ alocayiṃ.

For fifty-five years I wore dust and dirt; eating a meal only once a month, I plucked out my hair and beard.

284.

284.

“Ekapādena aṭṭhāsiṃ, āsanaṃ parivajjayiṃ;

Sukkhagūthāni ca khādiṃ, uddesañca na sādiyiṃ.

I stood on one foot; I avoided a seat. I ate dry dung and did not accept food designated for me.

285.

285.

“Etādisaṃ karitvāna, bahuṃ duggatigāminaṃ;

Vuyhamāno mahoghena, buddhaṃ saraṇamāgamaṃ.

Having performed many such practices that lead to a bad destination, being swept away by the great flood, I went to the Buddha for refuge.

286.

286.

“Saraṇagamanaṃ passa, passa dhammasudhammataṃ;

Tisso vijjā anuppattā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsana”nti.

Behold my going for refuge! Behold the excellence of the Dhamma! The three true knowledges have been attained; the Buddha’s teaching has been done.

… Jambuko thero….

… The Elder Jambuka …

6. Senakattheragāthā

6. The Verses of the Elder Senaka

287.

287.

“Svāgataṃ [M 0.0271][V 0.0211] vata me āsi, gayāyaṃ gayaphagguyā;

Yaṃ addasāsiṃ sambuddhaṃ, desentaṃ dhammamuttamaṃ.

Indeed, my coming to Gayā, to the Phaggu, was a good one, for I saw the Perfectly Enlightened One teaching the supreme Dhamma.

288.

288.

“Mahappabhaṃ [T 0.0313] gaṇācariyaṃ, aggapattaṃ vināyakaṃ;

Sadevakassa lokassa, jinaṃ atuladassanaṃ.

Of great radiance, teacher of the multitude, who has attained the supreme, the Guide, the Victor for the world with its gods, one of incomparable vision.

289.

289.

“Mahānāgaṃ mahāvīraṃ, mahājutimanāsavaṃ;

Sabbāsavaparikkhīṇaṃ, satthāramakutobhayaṃ.

The great nāga, the great hero, of great splendor, taintless, with all taints utterly destroyed, the Teacher who is fearless from any quarter.

290.

290.

“Cirasaṃkiliṭṭhaṃ vata maṃ, diṭṭhisandānabandhitaṃ sandhitaṃ (sī. syā.), sanditaṃ (pī. sī. aṭṭha.);

Vimocayi so bhagavā, sabbaganthehi senaka”nti.

That Blessed One liberated me, Senaka—who was long defiled and bound by the fetter of views—from all ties.

… Senako thero….

… The Elder Senaka …

7. Sambhūtattheragāthā

7. The Verses of the Elder Sambhūta

291.

291.

“Yo dandhakāle tarati, taraṇīye ca dandhaye;

Ayoni ayoniso (syā.) saṃvidhānena, bālo dukkhaṃ nigacchati.

The fool who hurries when it is time to be slow, and is slow when it is time to hurry, through his unwise arrangements, comes to suffering.

292.

292.

“Tassatthā parihāyanti, kāḷapakkheva candimā;

Āyasakyañca āyasasyañca (sī.) pappoti, mittehi ca virujjhati.

His advantages decline like the moon in the dark fortnight. He reaps dishonor and comes into conflict with his friends.

293.

293.

“Yo dandhakāle dandheti, taraṇīye ca tāraye;

Yoniso saṃvidhānena, sukhaṃ pappoti paṇḍito.

The wise person who is slow when it is time to be slow, and hurries when it is time to hurry, through his wise arrangements, attains happiness.

294.

294.

“Tassatthā paripūrenti, sukkapakkheva candimā;

Yaso kittiñca pappoti, mittehi na virujjhatī”ti.

His advantages increase like the moon in the bright fortnight. He obtains fame and renown and does not come into conflict with his friends.

… Sambhūto thero….

… The Elder Sambhūta …

8. Rāhulattheragāthā

8. The Verses of the Elder Rāhula

295.

295.

“Ubhayeneva [P 0.0035] sampanno, rāhulabhaddoti maṃ vidū;

Yañcamhi putto buddhassa, yañca dhammesu cakkhumā.

Endowed in two respects, they know me as ‘Rāhula the Auspicious’: because I am the Buddha’s son and because I have the eye in the Dhamma.

296.

296.

“Yañca me āsavā khīṇā, yañca natthi punabbhavo;

Arahā [T 0.0314] dakkhiṇeyyomhi, tevijjo amataddaso.

Because my taints are destroyed and there is no more renewed existence for me, I am an arahant, worthy of gifts, endowed with the three true knowledges, a seer of the Deathless.

297.

297.

“Kāmandhā [M 0.0272] jālapacchannā, taṇhāchādanachāditā;

Pamattabandhunā baddhā, macchāva kumināmukhe.

Blinded by sensual pleasures, covered by a net, veiled by the shroud of craving, bound by their kinsman, negligence, beings are like fish in the mouth of a fish-trap.

298.

298.

“Taṃ [V 0.0212] kāmaṃ ahamujjhitvā, chetvā mārassa bandhanaṃ;

Samūlaṃ taṇhamabbuyha, sītibhūtosmi nibbuto”ti.

Having cast off that sensual pleasure, having cut Māra’s bond, having plucked out craving by the root, I have become cool, quenched.

… Rāhulo thero….

… The Elder Rāhula …

9. Candanattheragāthā

9. The Verses of the Elder Candana

299.

299.

“Jātarūpena sañchannā pacchannā (sī.), dāsīgaṇapurakkhatā;

Aṅkena puttamādāya, bhariyā maṃ upāgami.

Adorned with gold, attended by a retinue of slave-women, holding our son on her hip, my wife approached me.

300.

300.

“Tañca disvāna āyantiṃ, sakaputtassa mātaraṃ;

Alaṅkataṃ suvasanaṃ, maccupāsaṃva oḍḍitaṃ.

When I saw her coming—the mother of my son, adorned and beautifully dressed—it was like seeing a snare of Death set out.

301.

301.

“Tato me manasīkāro, yoniso udapajjatha;

Ādīnavo pāturahu, nibbidā samatiṭṭhatha.

Then wise attention arose in me: the danger became manifest, and disenchantment was firmly established.

302.

302.

“Tato cittaṃ vimucci me, passa dhammasudhammataṃ;

Tisso vijjā anuppattā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsana”nti.

Then my mind was liberated. Behold the excellence of the Dhamma! The three true knowledges have been attained; the Buddha’s teaching has been done.

… Candano thero….

… The Elder Candana …

10. Dhammikattheragāthā

10. The Verses of the Elder Dhammika

303.

303.

jā. 1.10.102 jātakepi “Dhammo have rakkhati dhammacāriṃ, dhammo suciṇṇo sukhamāvahati;

Esānisaṃso dhamme suciṇṇe, na duggatiṃ gacchati dhammacārī.

The Dhamma surely protects one who practices the Dhamma; the Dhamma well-practiced brings happiness. This is the benefit of the well-practiced Dhamma: one who practices the Dhamma does not go to a woeful state.

304.

304.

jā. 1.15.385 “Nahi dhammo adhammo ca, ubho samavipākino;

Adhammo [T 0.0315] nirayaṃ neti, dhammo pāpeti suggatiṃ.

For the Dhamma and Adhamma do not both have the same result. Adhamma leads to hell; the Dhamma brings one to a good destination.

305.

305.

“Tasmā hi dhammesu kareyya chandaṃ, iti modamāno sugatena tādinā;

Dhamme ṭhitā sugatavarassa sāvakā, nīyanti dhīrā saraṇavaraggagāmino.

Therefore, delighting in the Well-Gone One, the Such-like One, one should generate zeal for the Dhammas. The wise disciples of the supreme Well-Gone One, established in the Dhamma, who have gone to the supreme, best refuge, are led forth.

306.

306.

“Vipphoṭito [M 0.0273] gaṇḍamūlo, taṇhājālo samūhato;

So khīṇasaṃsāro na catthi kiñcanaṃ,

Cando yathā dosinā puṇṇamāsiya”nti.

The root of the boil has been lanced, the net of craving uprooted. He, with saṃsāra destroyed, has no impediment, like the moon on a full-moon night, free from fault.

… Dhammiko thero….

… The Elder Dhammika …

11. Sappakattheragāthā

11. The Verses of the Elder Sappaka

307.

307.

“Yadā balākā sucipaṇḍaracchadā, kāḷassa meghassa bhayena tajjitā;

Palehiti ālayamālayesinī, tadā nadī ajakaraṇī rameti maṃ.

When the egrets with pure white wings, terrified by the black cloud, desiring their home, flee to their nest, then the Ajakaraṇī river delights me.

308.

308.

“Yadā [V 0.0213][P 0.0036] balākā suvisuddhapaṇḍarā, kāḷassa meghassa bhayena tajjitā;

Pariyesati leṇamaleṇadassinī, tadā nadī ajakaraṇī rameti maṃ.

When the egrets, so very pure and white, terrified by the black cloud, seeing no shelter, search for a refuge, then the Ajakaraṇī river delights me.

309.

309.

“Kaṃ nu tattha na ramenti, jambuyo ubhato tahiṃ;

Sobhenti āpagākūlaṃ, mama leṇassa mahāleṇassa (syā. ka.) pacchato.

Whom, indeed, would the rose-apple trees there not delight, as they beautify both banks of the river behind my refuge?

310.

310.

“Tā matamadasaṅghasuppahīnā,

Bhekā [T 0.0316] mandavatī panādayanti;

‘Nājja girinadīhi vippavāsasamayo,

Khemā ajakaraṇī sivā surammā’”ti.

Those frogs, having abandoned their intoxicated and conceited groups, croak gently: ‘Today is not a time to live away from the mountain streams! The Ajakaraṇī is safe, auspicious, and utterly delightful.’

… Sappako thero….

… The Elder Sappaka …

12. Muditattheragāthā

12. The Verses of the Elder Mudita

311.

311.

“Pabbajiṃ jīvikatthohaṃ, laddhāna upasampadaṃ;

Tato saddhaṃ paṭilabhiṃ, daḷhavīriyo parakkamiṃ.

For the sake of a livelihood I went forth; having obtained the higher ordination, I then gained faith. Then, firm in energy, I strove.

312.

312.

“Kāmaṃ bhijjatuyaṃ kāyo, maṃsapesī visīyaruṃ visiyantu (ka.);

Ubho jaṇṇukasandhīhi, jaṅghāyo papatantu me.

Indeed, let this body break apart, let the lumps of flesh be scattered; let my shanks fall from both my knee joints.

313.

313.

“Nāsissaṃ [M 0.0274] na pivissāmi, vihārā ca na nikkhame;

Napi passaṃ nipātessaṃ, taṇhāsalle anūhate.

I will not eat, I will not drink, and I will not leave my dwelling; nor will I even lie down on my side while the dart of craving is unextracted.

314.

314.

“Tassa mevaṃ viharato, passa vīriyaparakkamaṃ;

Tisso vijjā anuppattā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsana”nti.

For me, abiding thus—behold my energy and striving! The three knowledges have been attained; the Buddha’s teaching has been fulfilled.

… Mudito thero….

… The Elder Mudita …

Catukkanipāto niṭṭhito.

The Chapter of Fours is finished.

Tatruddānaṃ –

Therein, the summary:

Nāgasamālo bhagu ca, sabhiyo nandakopi ca;

Jambuko senako thero, sambhūto rāhulopi ca.

Nāgasamāla and Bhagu, Sabhiya and Nandaka too; Jambuka, the Elder Senaka, Sambhūta and Rāhula as well.

Bhavati candano thero, dasete idāni naveva therā dissanti buddhasāvakā;

Dhammiko sappako thero, mudito cāpi te tayo;

Gāthāyo dve ca paññāsa, therā sabbepi terasāti idāni dvādaseva therā dissanti.

There is the Elder Candana; these ten are disciples of the Buddha. Dhammika, the Elder Sappaka, and Mudita too—these three. The verses are fifty-two, and all the elders are thirteen.

5. Pañcakanipāto

5. The Book of the Fives

1. Rājadattattheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Rājadatta

315.

315.

“Bhikkhu [T 0.0317][M 0.0275][V 0.0214][P 0.0037] sivathikaṃ sīvathikaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) gantvā, addasa itthimujjhitaṃ;

Apaviddhaṃ susānasmiṃ, khajjantiṃ kimihī phuṭaṃ.

A bhikkhu, having gone to the charnel ground, saw a woman’s body that had been cast away, discarded in the cemetery, being devoured by and infested with worms.

316.

316.

“Yañhi eke jigucchanti, mataṃ disvāna pāpakaṃ;

Kāmarāgo pāturahu, andhova savatī vasatī (sī.) ahuṃ.

While some are disgusted on seeing a foul corpse, for me sensual lust arose; I was like one who is blind, while it was oozing.

317.

317.

“Oraṃ odanapākamhā, tamhā ṭhānā apakkamiṃ;

Satimā sampajānohaṃ, ekamantaṃ upāvisiṃ.

Quicker than it takes for rice to cook, I departed from that place. Mindful and clearly comprehending, I sat down to one side.

318.

318.

“Tato me manasīkāro, yoniso udapajjatha;

Ādīnavo pāturahu, nibbidā samatiṭṭhatha.

Then wise attention arose in me; the danger became manifest, and disenchantment was firmly established.

319.

319.

“Tato cittaṃ vimucci me, passa dhammasudhammataṃ;

Tisso vijjā anuppattā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsana”nti.

Then my mind was liberated. Behold the good lawfulness of the Dhamma! The three true knowledges have been attained; the Buddha’s teaching has been done.

… Rājadatto thero….

… The Elder Rājadatta …

2. Subhūtattheragāthā

2. The Verses of the Elder Subhūta

320.

320.

“Ayoge yuñjamattānaṃ, puriso kiccamicchako kiccamicchato (sī.), kiccamicchayaṃ (katthaci);

Caraṃ ce nādhigaccheyya, ‘taṃ me dubbhagalakkhaṇaṃ’.

Should a person desiring the goal yoke himself to the wrong practice, though he strives, he would not attain it. That was the mark of my misfortune.

321.

321.

“Abbūḷhaṃ aghagataṃ vijitaṃ, ekañce ossajeyya kalīva siyā;

Sabbānipi ce ossajeyya andhova siyā, samavisamassa adassanato.

The miserable state is not uprooted. If one were to abandon just one thing, one would be like a wicked person; if one were to abandon all things, one would be like a blind person, from not seeing the even and the uneven.

322.

322.

“Yañhi [T 0.0318] kayirā tañhi vade, yaṃ na kayirā na taṃ vade;

Akarontaṃ bhāsamānaṃ, parijānanti paṇḍitā.

One should speak only of what one does; one should not speak of what one does not do. The wise recognize one who speaks but does not act.

323.

323.

dha. pa. 51 dhammapadepi “Yathāpi ruciraṃ pupphaṃ, vaṇṇavantaṃ agandhakaṃ;

Evaṃ subhāsitā vācā, aphalā hoti akubbato.

Just as a beautiful flower, colorful but without fragrance, even so is a well-spoken word fruitless for one who does not act upon it.

324.

324.

dha. pa. 52 “Yathāpi [M 0.0276] ruciraṃ pupphaṃ, vaṇṇavantaṃ sugandhakaṃ sagandhakaṃ (sī. syā. pī.);

Evaṃ subhāsitā vācā, saphalā hoti kubbato”ti sakubbato (sī. pī.), sukubbato (syā.).

Just as a beautiful flower, colorful and fragrant, even so is a well-spoken word fruitful for one who acts upon it.

… Subhūto thero….

… The Elder Subhūta …

3. Girimānandattheragāthā

3. The Verses of the Elder Girimānanda

325.

325.

“Vassati [V 0.0215][P 0.0038] devo yathā sugītaṃ, channā me kuṭikā sukhā nivātā;

Tassaṃ viharāmi vūpasanto, atha ce patthayasī pavassa deva.

The god rains as if with a beautiful song; my little hut is roofed, pleasant, and sheltered from the wind. I dwell therein pacified, so if you wish, O god, rain on.

326.

326.

“Vassati devo yathā sugītaṃ, channā me kuṭikā sukhā nivātā;

Tassaṃ viharāmi santacitto, atha ce patthayasī pavassa deva.

The god rains as if with a beautiful song; my little hut is roofed, pleasant, and sheltered from the wind. I dwell therein with a peaceful mind, so if you wish, O god, rain on.

327.

327.

“Vassati devo…pe… tassaṃ viharāmi vītarāgo…pe….

The god rains … I dwell therein free from lust …

328.

328.

“Vassati devo…pe… tassaṃ viharāmi vītadoso…pe….

The god rains … I dwell therein free from hatred …

329.

329.

“Vassati devo…pe… tassaṃ [T 0.0319] viharāmi vītamoho;

Atha ce patthayasī pavassa devā”ti.

The god rains … I dwell therein free from delusion. So if you wish, O god, rain on!

… Girimānando thero….

… The Elder Girimānanda …

4. Sumanattheragāthā

4. The Verses of the Elder Sumana

330.

330.

“Yaṃ patthayāno dhammesu, upajjhāyo anuggahi;

Amataṃ abhikaṅkhantaṃ, kataṃ kattabbakaṃ mayā.

The preceptor favored me, who was aspiring in the teachings and longing for the Deathless. What was to be done has been done by me.

331.

331.

“Anuppatto sacchikato, sayaṃ dhammo anītiho;

Visuddhiñāṇo nikkaṅkho, byākaromi tavantike.

The Dhamma has been attained and realized by myself, a Dhamma not based on hearsay. With purified knowledge, free from doubt, I make this declaration in your presence.

332.

332.

“Pubbenivāsaṃ jānāmi, dibbacakkhu visodhitaṃ;

Sadattho me anuppatto, kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ.

I know my past lives, the divine eye has been purified. My own goal has been attained by me; the teaching of the Buddha has been done.

333.

333.

“Appamattassa me sikkhā, sussutā tava sāsane;

Sabbe me āsavā khīṇā, natthi dāni punabbhavo.

For me, being diligent, the training in your teaching has been well learned. All my taints are destroyed; now there is no future existence.

334.

334.

“Anusāsi [M 0.0277] maṃ ariyavatā, anukampi anuggahi;

Amogho tuyhamovādo, antevāsimhi sikkhito”ti.

You instructed me with the noble practice; you had compassion and favored me. Your advice was not in vain; I am a resident pupil who is trained.

… Sumano thero….

… The Elder Sumana …

5. Vaḍḍhattheragāthā

5. The Verses of the Elder Vaḍḍha

335.

335.

“Sādhū hi kira me mātā, patodaṃ upadaṃsayi;

Yassāhaṃ vacanaṃ sutvā, anusiṭṭho janettiyā;

Āraddhavīriyo pahitatto, patto sambodhimuttamaṃ.

Indeed, it was good that my mother showed me the goad. Having heard her words, instructed by my mother, with energy aroused and mind resolute, I have attained supreme enlightenment.

336.

336.

“Arahā [V 0.0216] dakkhiṇeyyomhi, tevijjo amataddaso;

Jetvā namucino senaṃ, viharāmi anāsavo.

I am an Arahant, worthy of offerings, endowed with the three knowledges, a seer of the Deathless. Having conquered the army of Namuci, I dwell free from taints.

337.

337.

“Ajjhattañca [T 0.0320] bahiddhā ca, ye me vijjiṃsu āsavā;

Sabbe asesā ucchinnā, na ca uppajjare puna.

Whatever internal and external taints existed for me, all have been cut off without remainder; they will not arise again.

338.

338.

“Visāradā kho bhaginī, etamatthaṃ abhāsayi;

‘Apihā nūna mayipi, vanatho te na vijjati’.

Confidently, sister, you spoke this matter: ‘Surely you have no longing even for me; in you the jungle of defilements no longer exists.’

339.

339.

“Pariyantakataṃ dukkhaṃ, antimoyaṃ samussayo;

Jātimaraṇasaṃsāro, natthi dāni punabbhavo”ti.

An end has been made to suffering; this is the final body. The round of birth and death is over; now there is no future existence.

… Vaḍḍho thero….

… The Elder Vaḍḍha …

6. Nadīkassapattheragāthā

6. The Verses of the Elder Nadīkassapa

340.

340.

“Atthāya vata me buddho, nadiṃ nerañjaraṃ agā;

Yassāhaṃ dhammaṃ sutvāna, micchādiṭṭhiṃ vivajjayiṃ.

Indeed, for my benefit the Buddha came to the Nerañjarā river; having heard his Dhamma, I abandoned wrong view.

341.

341.

“Yajiṃ [P 0.0039] uccāvace yaññe, aggihuttaṃ juhiṃ ahaṃ;

‘Esā suddhī’ti maññanto, andhabhūto andhībhūto (ka.) puthujjano.

I performed high and low sacrifices; I tended the fire offering, thinking, ‘This is purification,’ a blind worldling.

342.

342.

“Diṭṭhigahanapakkhando pakkhanto (sī.), pakkhanno (syā. pī.), parāmāsena mohito;

Asuddhiṃ maññisaṃ suddhiṃ, andhabhūto aviddasu.

Plunged into the thicket of views, deluded by misapprehension, I considered what is impure to be pure—blind and ignorant.

343.

343.

“Micchādiṭṭhi pahīnā me, bhavā sabbe padālitā vidālitā (ka.);

Juhāmi dakkhiṇeyyaggiṃ, namassāmi tathāgataṃ.

Wrong view has been abandoned by me, all states of existence have been shattered. I tend the fire of the one worthy of offerings; I pay homage to the Tathāgata.

344.

344.

“Mohā [M 0.0278] sabbe pahīnā me, bhavataṇhā padālitā;

Vikkhīṇo jātisaṃsāro, natthi dāni punabbhavo”ti.

All delusions have been abandoned by me; the craving for existence has been shattered. The round of births is exhausted; now there is no future existence.

… Nadīkassapo thero….

… The Elder Nadīkassapa …

7. Gayākassapattheragāthā

7. The Verses of the Elder Gayākassapa

345.

345.

“Pāto majjhanhikaṃ sāyaṃ, tikkhattuṃ divasassahaṃ;

Otariṃ udakaṃ sohaṃ, gayāya gayaphagguyā.

At dawn, noon, and evening, three times a day, I entered the water at Gayā during the Phaggu festival.

346.

346.

“‘Yaṃ [T 0.0321] mayā pakataṃ pāpaṃ, pubbe aññāsu jātisu;

Taṃ dānīdha pavāhemi’, evaṃdiṭṭhi pure ahuṃ.

‘Whatever evil I have done in other former lives, that I now wash away here’—such was my view in the past.

347.

347.

“Sutvā [V 0.0217] subhāsitaṃ vācaṃ, dhammatthasahitaṃ padaṃ;

Tathaṃ yāthāvakaṃ atthaṃ, yoniso paccavekkhisaṃ;

Having heard a well-spoken utterance, a phrase connected with the goal and the Dhamma, I wisely investigated its true and actual meaning;

348.

348.

“Ninhātasabbapāpomhi, nimmalo payato suci;

Suddho suddhassa dāyādo, putto buddhassa oraso.

I have washed away all evil; I am stainless, restrained, and pure. Pure, an heir to the Pure One, I am the Buddha’s legitimate son.

349.

349.

“Ogayhaṭṭhaṅgikaṃ sotaṃ, sabbapāpaṃ pavāhayiṃ;

Tisso vijjā ajjhagamiṃ, kataṃ buddhassa sāsana”nti.

Having plunged into the eight-factored stream, I have washed away all evil. I have attained the three true knowledges; the Buddha’s teaching has been done.

… Gayākassapo thero….

… The Elder Gayākassapa …

8. Vakkalittheragāthā

8. The Verses of the Elder Vakkali

350.

350.

“Vātarogābhinīto tvaṃ, viharaṃ kānane vane;

Paviṭṭhagocare lūkhe, kathaṃ bhikkhu karissasi.

“Afflicted by a wind-disease, dwelling in a forest grove, with a rough resort for alms—how will you manage, bhikkhu?”

351.

351.

“Pītisukhena vipulena, pharamāno samussayaṃ;

Lūkhampi abhisambhonto, viharissāmi kānane.

Pervading my body with abundant rapture and happiness, I will dwell in the forest, overcoming even what is rough.

352.

352.

“Bhāvento satipaṭṭhāne, indriyāni balāni ca;

Bojjhaṅgāni ca bhāvento, viharissāmi kānane.

Developing the establishments of mindfulness, the spiritual faculties and the powers, and developing the factors of enlightenment, I will dwell in the forest.

353.

353.

“Āraddhavīriye pahitatte, niccaṃ daḷhaparakkame āraddhavīriyo pahitatto, niccaṃ daḷhaparakkamo (sī.);

Samagge sahite disvā, viharissāmi kānane.

Seeing companions with aroused energy and resolute minds, always firm in exertion, harmonious and united, I will dwell in the forest.

354.

354.

“Anussaranto sambuddhaṃ, aggaṃ dantaṃ samāhitaṃ;

Atandito [T 0.0322] rattindivaṃ, viharissāmi kānane”ti.

Recollecting the Perfectly Enlightened One—the supreme, the tamed, the composed—unwearied day and night, I will dwell in the forest.

… Vakkalitthero….

… The Elder Vakkali …

9. Vijitasenattheragāthā

9. The Verses of the Elder Vijitasena

355.

355.

“Olaggessāmi [M 0.0279] te citta, āṇidvāreva hatthinaṃ;

Na taṃ pāpe niyojessaṃ, kāmajāla kāmajālaṃ (syā.) sarīraja sarīrajaṃ (syā. ka.).

I will check you, O mind, as one checks an elephant at a gate with a pillar. I will not yoke you to what is evil, to the body-born net of sensual pleasures.

356.

356.

“Tvaṃ [P 0.0040] olaggo na gacchasi na gañchisi (pī), dvāravivaraṃ gajova alabhanto;

Na ca cittakali punappunaṃ, pasakka pasahaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) pāparato carissasi.

Checked, you will not go astray, like an elephant not finding an opening in the gate. And you, wretched mind, will no longer persist again and again, delighting in evil.

357.

357.

“Yathā kuñjaraṃ adantaṃ, navaggahamaṅkusaggaho;

Balavā āvatteti akāmaṃ, evaṃ āvattayissaṃ taṃ.

Just as a strong hook-wielder turns back a newly captured, untamed elephant against its will, so will I turn you back.

358.

358.

“Yathā varahayadamakusalo, sārathi pavaro dameti ājaññaṃ;

Evaṃ damayissaṃ taṃ, patiṭṭhito pañcasu balesu.

Just as an excellent charioteer, skilled in taming noble steeds, tames a thoroughbred, so, established in the five powers, will I tame you.

359.

359.

“Satiyā [V 0.0218] taṃ nibandhissaṃ, payutto te damessāmi payatatto vodapessāmi (sī.);

Vīriyadhuraniggahito, na yito dūraṃ [T 0.0323] gamissase cittā”ti.

I will bind you with mindfulness; having yoked you, I will tame you. Held fast by the yoke of energy, you will not go far from here, O mind.

… Vijitaseno thero….

… The Elder Vijitasena …

10. Yasadattattheragāthā

10. The Verses of the Elder Yasadatta

360.

360.

“Upārambhacitto dummedho, suṇāti jinasāsanaṃ;

Ārakā hoti saddhammā, nabhaso pathavī yathā.

A fool with a fault-finding mind who hears the Victor’s teaching is as far from the good Dhamma as the earth is from the sky.

361.

361.

“Upārambhacitto dummedho, suṇāti jinasāsanaṃ;

Parihāyati saddhammā, kāḷapakkheva candimā.

A fool with a fault-finding mind who hears the Victor’s teaching declines from the good Dhamma like the moon in the waning fortnight.

362.

362.

“Upārambhacitto dummedho, suṇāti jinasāsanaṃ;

Parisussati saddhamme, maccho appodake yathā.

A fool with a fault-finding mind who hears the Victor’s teaching dries up in the good Dhamma like a fish in little water.

363.

363.

“Upārambhacitto dummedho, suṇāti jinasāsanaṃ;

Na virūhati saddhamme, khette bījaṃva pūtikaṃ.

A fool with a fault-finding mind who hears the Victor’s teaching does not grow in the good Dhamma, like a rotten seed in a field.

364.

364.

“Yo ca tuṭṭhena cittena, suṇāti jinasāsanaṃ;

Khepetvā āsave sabbe, sacchikatvā akuppataṃ;

Pappuyya paramaṃ santiṃ, parinibbātināsavo”ti.

But one who with a pleased mind hears the Victor’s teaching, having destroyed all the taints and realized the unshakable, having attained the supreme peace, taintless, attains final Nibbāna.

… Yasadatto thero….

Thus the Elder Yasadatta spoke these verses.

11. Soṇakuṭikaṇṇattheragāthā

11. The Verses of the Elder Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa

365.

365.

“Upasampadā [M 0.0280] ca me laddhā, vimutto camhi anāsavo;

So ca me bhagavā diṭṭho, vihāre ca sahāvasiṃ.

I have obtained the higher ordination; I am liberated and free from taints. I have seen the Blessed One and have dwelt together with him in the dwelling.

366.

366.

“Bahudeva rattiṃ bhagavā, abbhokāsetināmayi;

Vihārakusalo satthā, vihāraṃ pāvisī tadā.

For a great part of the night the Blessed One spent time in the open air. Then the Teacher, skilled in dwellings, entered his dwelling.

367.

367.

“Santharitvāna saṅghāṭiṃ, seyyaṃ kappesi gotamo;

Sīho [T 0.0324] selaguhāyaṃva, pahīnabhayabheravo.

Having spread his outer robe, Gotama, who had abandoned fear and terror, lay down to rest like a lion in a mountain cave.

368.

368.

“Tato kalyāṇavākkaraṇo, sammāsambuddhasāvako;

Soṇo abhāsi saddhammaṃ, buddhaseṭṭhassa sammukhā.

Then Soṇa, of gracious speech, a disciple of the Perfectly Enlightened One, spoke the good Dhamma in the presence of the Best of Buddhas.

369.

369.

“Pañcakkhandhe pariññāya, bhāvayitvāna añjasaṃ;

Pappuyya paramaṃ santiṃ, parinibbissatyanāsavo”ti.

Having fully understood the five aggregates and developed the direct path, having attained the supreme peace, taintless, one will attain final Nibbāna.

… Soṇo kuṭikaṇṇathero….

Thus the Elder Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa spoke these verses.

12. Kosiyattheragāthā

12. The Verses of the Elder Kosiya

370.

370.

“Yo [V 0.0219][P 0.0041] ve garūnaṃ vacanaññu dhīro, vase ca tamhi janayetha pemaṃ;

So bhattimā nāma ca hoti paṇḍito, ñatvā ca dhammesu visesi assa.

“The wise one who understands the speech of his teachers, and dwelling with them generates affection; he is called devoted and wise, and having known the Dhammas, he would be distinguished.”

371.

371.

“Yaṃ āpadā uppatitā uḷārā, nakkhambhayante paṭisaṅkhayantaṃ;

So thāmavā nāma ca hoti paṇḍito, ñatvā ca dhammesu visesi assa.

“When great calamities arise, they do not shake the one who reflects; he is called steadfast and wise, and having known the Dhammas, he would be distinguished.”

372.

372.

“Yo ve samuddova ṭhito anejo, gambhīrapañño nipuṇatthadassī;

Asaṃhāriyo nāma ca hoti paṇḍito, ñatvā ca dhammesu visesi assa.

“He who stands like the ocean, unperturbed, of profound wisdom, a seer of subtle meaning; he is called unshakeable and wise, and having known the Dhammas, he would be distinguished.”

373.

373.

“Bahussuto dhammadharo ca hoti, dhammassa [T 0.0325] hoti anudhammacārī;

So tādiso nāma ca hoti paṇḍito, ñatvā ca dhammesu visesi assa.

“He who is learned and a bearer of the Dhamma, who practices in accordance with the Dhamma; such a one is called wise, and having known the Dhammas, he would be distinguished.”

374.

374.

“Atthañca [M 0.0281] yo jānāti bhāsitassa, atthañca ñatvāna tathā karoti;

Atthantaro nāma sa hoti paṇḍito, ñatvā ca dhammesu visesi assā”ti.

“He who knows the meaning of what is spoken, and having understood the meaning acts accordingly; he is called one who penetrates the meaning, a wise man, and having known the Dhammas, he would be distinguished.”

… Kosiyo thero….

Thus the Elder Kosiya spoke these verses.

Pañcakanipāto niṭṭhito.

The Book of Fives is finished.

Tatruddānaṃ –

The summary therein:

Rājadatto subhūto ca, girimānandasumanā;

Vaḍḍho ca kassapo thero, gayākassapavakkalī.

Rājadatta and Subhūta, Girimānanda and Sumanā; Vaḍḍha and the Elder Kassapa, Gayākassapa and Vakkali.

Vijito yasadatto ca, soṇo kosiyasavhayo;

Saṭṭhi ca pañca gāthāyo, therā ca ettha dvādasāti.

Vijita and Yasadatta, Soṇa and he named Kosiya; sixty-five are the verses, and the elders here are twelve.

6. Chakkanipāto

6. The Book of Sixes

1. Uruveḷakassapattheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Uruveḷakassapa

375.

375.

“Disvāna [M 0.0282][V 0.0220][P 0.0042] pāṭihīrāni, gotamassa yasassino;

Na tāvāhaṃ paṇipatiṃ, issāmānena vañcito.

“Having seen the miracles of the glorious Gotama, I still did not pay homage, being deceived by jealousy and conceit.”

376.

376.

“Mama saṅkappamaññāya, codesi narasārathi;

Tato [T 0.0326] me āsi saṃvego, abbhuto lomahaṃsano.

“Having understood my intention, the Guide of Men admonished me; then a sense of spiritual urgency arose in me, amazing, causing my hair to stand on end.”

377.

377.

“Pubbe jaṭilabhūtassa, yā me siddhi parittikā;

Tāhaṃ tadā nirākatvā niraṃkatvā (syā. ka.), pabbajiṃ jinasāsane.

“Whatever slight attainment I had formerly as a matted-hair ascetic, I rejected it then and went forth in the Victor’s Dispensation.”

378.

378.

“Pubbe yaññena santuṭṭho, kāmadhātupurakkhato;

Pacchā rāgañca dosañca, mohañcāpi samūhaniṃ.

“Formerly I was content with sacrifice, giving precedence to the sense-sphere realm; afterwards I uprooted lust, hatred, and delusion.”

379.

379.

“Pubbenivāsaṃ jānāmi, dibbacakkhu visodhitaṃ;

Iddhimā paracittaññū, dibbasotañca pāpuṇiṃ.

“I know my former existences, my divine eye is purified; I possess psychic powers, I know the minds of others, and I have attained the divine ear.”

380.

380.

“Yassa catthāya pabbajito, agārasmānagāriyaṃ;

So me attho anuppatto, sabbasaṃyojanakkhayo”ti.

“The goal for which I went forth from the home life into homelessness—that goal I have attained: the destruction of all fetters.”

… Uruveḷakassapo thero….

… The Elder Uruveḷakassapa …

2. Tekicchakārittheragāthā

2. The Verses of the Elder Tekicchakārī

381.

381.

“Atihitā vīhi, khalagatā sālī;

Na ca labhe piṇḍaṃ, kathamahaṃ kassaṃ.

“The paddy has been brought in, the rice is on the threshing floor; and I do not receive alms-food—what am I to do?”

382.

382.

“Buddhamappameyyaṃ anussara pasanno;

Pītiyā phuṭasarīro hohisi satatamudaggo.

“Recollect the immeasurable Buddha with a confident mind; with your body pervaded by rapture, you will be constantly uplifted.”

383.

383.

“Dhammamappameyyaṃ anussara pasanno;

Pītiyā phuṭasarīro hohisi satatamudaggo.

“Recollect the immeasurable Dhamma with a confident mind; with your body pervaded by rapture, you will be constantly uplifted.”

384.

384.

“Saṅghamappameyyaṃ anussara pasanno;

Pītiyā phuṭasarīro hohisi satatamudaggo.

“Recollect the immeasurable Sangha with a confident mind; with your body pervaded by rapture, you will be constantly uplifted.”

385.

385.

“Abbhokāse [M 0.0283][V 0.0221] viharasi, sītā hemantikā imā ratyo;

Mā sītena pareto vihaññittho, pavisa [T 0.0327] tvaṃ vihāraṃ phusitaggaḷaṃ.

“You are dwelling in the open, and these are cold winter nights. Do not be afflicted, overcome by the cold. Enter your dwelling and fasten the bolt.”

386.

386.

“Phusissaṃ catasso appamaññāyo, tāhi ca sukhito viharissaṃ;

Nāhaṃ sītena vihaññissaṃ, aniñjito viharanto”ti.

“I will enter into the four immeasurables, and by means of them I will dwell happily. I will not be afflicted by the cold while I dwell unshaken.”

… Tekicchakārī tekicchakāni (sī. syā. pī.) thero….

Thus the Elder Tekicchakārī spoke these verses.

3. Mahānāgattheragāthā

3. The Verses of the Elder Mahānāga

387.

387.

“Yassa [P 0.0043] sabrahmacārīsu, gāravo nūpalabbhati;

Parihāyati saddhammā, maccho appodake yathā.

“One in whom no respect is found for his companions in the holy life falls away from the good Dhamma, like a fish in little water.”

388.

388.

“Yassa sabrahmacārīsu, gāravo nūpalabbhati;

Na virūhati saddhamme, khette bījaṃva pūtikaṃ.

“One in whom no respect is found for his companions in the holy life does not grow in the good Dhamma, like a rotten seed in a field.”

389.

389.

“Yassa sabrahmacārīsu, gāravo nūpalabbhati;

Ārakā hoti nibbānā nibbāṇā (sī.), dhammarājassa sāsane.

“One in whom no respect is found for his companions in the holy life is far from Nibbāna in the Dispensation of the Dhamma King.”

390.

390.

“Yassa sabrahmacārīsu, gāravo upalabbhati;

Na vihāyati saddhammā, maccho bavhodake bahvodake (sī.), bahodake (syā.) yathā.

“One in whom respect is found for his companions in the holy life does not fall away from the good Dhamma, like a fish in abundant water.”

391.

391.

“Yassa sabrahmacārīsu, gāravo upalabbhati;

So virūhati saddhamme, khette bījaṃva bhaddakaṃ.

“One in whom respect is found for his companions in the holy life grows in the good Dhamma, like a healthy seed in a field.”

392.

392.

“Yassa sabrahmacārīsu, gāravo upalabbhati;

Santike hoti nibbānaṃ nibbāṇaṃ (sī.), dhammarājassa sāsane”ti.

“One in whom respect is found for his companions in the holy life is near to Nibbāna in the Dispensation of the Dhamma King.”

… Mahānāgo thero….

Thus the Elder Mahānāga spoke these verses.

4. Kullattheragāthā

4. The Verses of the Elder Kulla

393.

393.

“Kullo sivathikaṃ gantvā, addasa itthimujjhitaṃ;

Apaviddhaṃ [T 0.0328] susānasmiṃ, khajjantiṃ kimihī phuṭaṃ.

“Having gone to the charnel ground, Kulla saw a woman’s body cast away, discarded in the cemetery, being devoured, filled with worms.”

394.

394.

“Āturaṃ [M 0.0284] asuciṃ pūtiṃ, passa kulla samussayaṃ;

Uggharantaṃ paggharantaṃ, bālānaṃ abhinanditaṃ.

“‘Behold this body, Kulla: diseased, impure, and putrid, oozing and trickling, yet delighted in by fools.’”

395.

395.

“Dhammādāsaṃ gahetvāna, ñāṇadassanapattiyā;

Paccavekkhiṃ imaṃ kāyaṃ, tucchaṃ santarabāhiraṃ.

Having taken up the mirror of the Dhamma for the attainment of knowledge and vision, I reflected on this body, empty both internally and externally.

396.

396.

“Yathā idaṃ tathā etaṃ, yathā etaṃ tathā idaṃ;

Yathā adho tathā uddhaṃ, yathā uddhaṃ tathā adho.

As this is, so is that; as that is, so is this. As below, so above; as above, so below.

397.

397.

“Yathā [V 0.0222] divā tathā rattiṃ, yathā rattiṃ tathā divā;

Yathā pure tathā pacchā, yathā pacchā tathā pure.

As by day, so by night; as by night, so by day. As before, so after; as after, so before.

398.

398.

“Pañcaṅgikena turiyena, na ratī hoti tādisī;

Yathā ekaggacittassa, sammā dhammaṃ vipassato”ti.

There is no such delight from a five-piece orchestra as there is for one with a concentrated mind who rightly sees the Dhamma with insight.

… Kullo thero….

Thus the Elder Kulla spoke these verses.

5. Mālukyaputtattheragāthā

5. The Verses of the Elder Mālukyaputta

399.

399.

“Manujassa pamattacārino, taṇhā vaḍḍhati māluvā viya;

So plavatī plavati (sī. pī. ka.), pariplavati (syā.) hurā huraṃ, phalamicchaṃva vanasmi vānaro.

For a person who lives heedlessly, craving grows like a māluvā creeper. He leaps from one existence to another, like a monkey in the forest seeking fruit.

400.

400.

“Yaṃ esā sahate sahati (pī. ka.) jammī, taṇhā loke visattikā;

Sokā tassa pavaḍḍhanti, abhivaṭṭhaṃva abhivuṭṭhaṃva (syā.), abhivaḍḍhaṃva (ka.) bīraṇaṃ.

Whomever this wretched, clinging craving in the world overcomes, his sorrows flourish like bīraṇa grass drenched with rain.

401.

401.

“Yo cetaṃ sahate sahati (pī. ka.) jammiṃ, taṇhaṃ loke duraccayaṃ;

Sokā tamhā papatanti, udabindūva pokkharā.

But whoever overcomes this wretched craving, so hard to surmount in the world, sorrows fall away from him like a water drop from a lotus leaf.

402.

402.

“Taṃ [P 0.0044] vo vadāmi bhaddaṃ vo, yāvantettha samāgatā;

Taṇhāya [T 0.0329] mūlaṃ khaṇatha, usīratthova bīraṇaṃ;

Mā vo naḷaṃva sotova, māro bhañji punappunaṃ.

This I say to you—good fortune to you all who have gathered here: dig up the root of craving as one seeking usīra root digs up bīraṇa grass. Do not let Māra break you again and again, as a river’s current breaks a reed.

403.

403.

“Karotha buddhavacanaṃ, khaṇo vo mā upaccagā;

Khaṇātītā hi socanti, nirayamhi samappitā.

Do the Buddha’s word; let the opportune moment not pass you by. For those who let the moment pass grieve when they are consigned to hell.

404.

404.

“Pamādo rajo pamādo sabbadā (sī. ka.), suttanipātaṭṭhakathāyaṃ uṭṭhānasuttavaṇṇanā oloketabbā, pamādānupatito rajo;

Appamādena vijjāya, abbahe sallamattano”ti.

Heedlessness is a defilement, a defilement that follows upon heedlessness. By means of heedfulness and knowledge, one should pull out the arrow from oneself.

… Mālukyaputto māluṅkyaputto (sī. syā. pī.) thero….

… The Elder Mālukyaputta …

6. Sappadāsattheragāthā

6. The Verses of the Elder Sappadāsa

405.

405.

“Paṇṇavīsativassāni[M 0.0285], yato pabbajito ahaṃ;

Accharāsaṅghātamattampi, cetosantimanajjhagaṃ.

For twenty-five years since I went forth, I did not attain peace of mind even for the duration of a finger-snap.

406.

406.

“Aladdhā cittassekaggaṃ, kāmarāgena aṭṭito addito (syā. sī. aṭṭha.), aḍḍito (ka.);

Bāhā paggayha kandanto, vihārā upanikkhamiṃ nūpanikkhamiṃ (sabbattha), dupanikkhamiṃ (?).

Not having gained one-pointedness of mind, afflicted by sensual lust, wailing with my arms upraised, I went out from the monastery.

407.

407.

“Satthaṃ vā āharissāmi, ko attho jīvitena me;

Kathaṃ hi sikkhaṃ paccakkhaṃ, kālaṃ kubbetha mādiso.

“I shall take up a weapon! What use is this life to me? How could one like me die after having repudiated the training?”

408.

408.

“Tadāhaṃ [V 0.0223] khuramādāya, mañcakamhi upāvisiṃ;

Parinīto khuro āsi, dhamaniṃ chettumattano.

Then, having taken a razor, I sat down on my cot. The razor was placed to cut my own artery.

409.

409.

“Tato me manasīkāro, yoniso udapajjatha;

Ādīnavo pāturahu, nibbidā samatiṭṭhatha.

Then wise attention arose in me. The danger became manifest; disenchantment was firmly established.

410.

410.

“Tato cittaṃ vimucci me, passa dhammasudhammataṃ;

Tisso [T 0.0330] vijjā anuppattā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsana”nti.

Then my mind was liberated. Behold the good lawfulness of the Dhamma! The three true knowledges have been attained; the Buddha’s teaching has been done.

… Sappadāso thero….

… The Elder Sappadāsa …

7.Kātiyānattheragāthā

7. The Verses of the Elder Kātiyāna

411.

411.

“Uṭṭhehi nisīda kātiyāna, mā niddābahulo ahu jāgarassu;

Mā taṃ alasaṃ pamattabandhu, kūṭeneva jinātu maccurājā.

Arise, sit up, Kātiyāna! Do not be one of much sleep; be wakeful! Let not the King of Death, that kinsman of the heedless, conquer you who are lazy by trickery.

412.

412.

“Seyyathāpi sayathāpi (sī. pī.) mahāsamuddavego, evaṃ jātijarātivattate taṃ;

So karohi sudīpamattano tvaṃ, na hi tāṇaṃ tava vijjateva aññaṃ.

Just as the surge of the great ocean advances, so do birth and old age roll over you. Make an island for yourself, for no other refuge exists for you.

413.

413.

“Satthā hi vijesi maggametaṃ, saṅgā jātijarābhayā atītaṃ;

Pubbāpararattamappamatto, anuyuñjassu daḷhaṃ karohi yogaṃ.

The Teacher has indeed realized this path that goes beyond attachment and the fear of birth and aging. During the first and last watches of the night, being heedful, apply yourself; make your exertion firm.

414.

414.

“Purimāni [M 0.0286] pamuñca bandhanāni, saṅghāṭikhuramuṇḍabhikkhabhojī;

Mā khiḍḍāratiñca mā niddaṃ, anuyuñjittha jhāya kātiyāna.

Release your former fetters! As one who wears the outer robe, is shaven-headed, and subsists on almsfood, do not indulge in delight in play or in sleep. Meditate, Kātiyāna!

415.

415.

“Jhāyāhi [P 0.0045] jināhi kātiyāna, yogakkhemapathesu [T 0.0331] kovidosi;

Pappuyya anuttaraṃ visuddhiṃ, parinibbāhisi vārināva joti.

Meditate and conquer, Kātiyāna! You are skilled in the paths to security from bondage. Having attained the unsurpassed purity, you will be utterly extinguished, like a fire by water.

416.

416.

“Pajjotakaro parittaraṃso, vātena vinamyate latāva;

Evampi tuvaṃ anādiyāno, māraṃ indasagotta niddhunāhi;

So vedayitāsu vītarāgo, kālaṃ kaṅkha idheva sītibhūto”ti.

Just as a lamp with a feeble flame is bent by the wind like a creeper, so you too, without grasping, should shake off Māra, O Indasagotta. Having become free from passion for feelings, become cool right here and await your time.

… Kātiyāno thero….

… The Elder Kātiyāna …

8. Migajālattheragāthā

8. The Verses of the Elder Migajāla

417.

417.

“Sudesito cakkhumatā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Sabbasaṃyojanātīto, sabbavaṭṭavināsano.

Well taught by the One with Vision, the Buddha, Kinsman of the Sun, is the Dhamma. It leads beyond all fetters and destroys every round of existence.

418.

418.

“Niyyāniko uttaraṇo, taṇhāmūlavisosano;

Visamūlaṃ āghātanaṃ, chetvā pāpeti nibbutiṃ.

It is emancipating, a means of crossing over, that which dries up the root of craving. Having cut off the slaughtering-place, the root of poison, it leads one to Nibbāna.

419.

419.

“Aññāṇamūlabhedāya[V 0.0224], kammayantavighāṭano;

Viññāṇānaṃ pariggahe, ñāṇavajiranipātano.

It is for shattering the root of ignorance, for dismantling the mechanism of kamma. Upon the grasping of consciousnesses, it is the felling with the diamond-bolt of knowledge.

420.

420.

“Vedanānaṃ viññāpano, upādānappamocano;

Bhavaṃ aṅgārakāsuṃva, ñāṇena anupassano anupassako (sī. pī.).

It makes known the feelings and brings release from clinging. It is the seeing of existence with wisdom as like a pit of glowing embers.

421.

421.

“Mahāraso sugambhīro, jarāmaccunivāraṇo;

Ariyo [T 0.0332] aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, dukkhūpasamano sivo.

Of great savor, profoundly deep, a ward against aging and death is the Noble Eightfold Path—the appeasement of suffering, the secure.

422.

422.

“Kammaṃ kammanti ñatvāna, vipākañca vipākato;

Paṭiccuppannadhammānaṃ, yathāvālokadassano;

Mahākhemaṅgamo santo, pariyosānabhaddako”ti.

It is the knowing of kamma as kamma and its result as result; the seeing of dependently arisen phenomena as they are. It leads to the great security; it is peaceful and auspicious in its conclusion.

… Migajālo thero….

… The Elder Migajāla …

9. Purohitaputtajentattheragāthā

9. The Verses of the Elder Jenta, the Purohita’s Son

423.

423.

“Jātimadena [M 0.0287] mattohaṃ, bhogaissariyena ca;

Saṇṭhānavaṇṇarūpena, madamatto acārihaṃ.

I was intoxicated with pride in my birth, and with wealth and sovereignty. Intoxicated with conceit over my figure, complexion, and form, I went about.

424.

424.

“Nāttano samakaṃ kañci, atirekaṃ ca maññisaṃ;

Atimānahato bālo, patthaddho ussitaddhajo.

I considered no one my equal, and certainly no one my superior. A fool destroyed by excessive pride, I was stubborn, with my banner of pride raised high.

425.

425.

“Mātaraṃ pitarañcāpi, aññepi garusammate;

Na kañci abhivādesiṃ, mānatthaddho anādaro.

My mother and father, and others held in high esteem—I paid homage to no one, being stiff with pride and disrespectful.

426.

426.

“Disvā vināyakaṃ aggaṃ, sārathīnaṃ varuttamaṃ;

Tapantamiva ādiccaṃ, bhikkhusaṅghapurakkhataṃ.

Having seen the supreme guide, the best of tamers, shining like the sun, and honored by the Saṅgha of bhikkhus,

427.

427.

“Mānaṃ madañca chaḍḍetvā, vippasannena cetasā;

Sirasā abhivādesiṃ, sabbasattānamuttamaṃ.

having discarded conceit and intoxication, with a mind exceptionally serene, I paid homage with my head to the supreme among all beings.

428.

428.

“Atimāno [P 0.0046] ca omāno, pahīnā susamūhatā;

Asmimāno samucchinno, sabbe mānavidhā hatā”ti.

Superiority conceit and inferiority conceit have been abandoned, thoroughly uprooted. The conceit ‘I am’ has been eradicated; all kinds of conceit are destroyed.

… Jento purohitaputto thero….

… The Elder Jenta, the son of the purohita …

10. Sumanattheragāthā

10. The Verses of the Elder Sumana

429.

429.

“Yadā [T 0.0333] navo pabbajito, jātiyā sattavassiko;

Iddhiyā abhibhotvāna, pannagindaṃ mahiddhikaṃ.

“When, newly gone forth, being only seven years of age by birth, having overpowered by psychic power the serpent king of great might,

430.

430.

“Upajjhāyassa [V 0.0225] udakaṃ, anotattā mahāsarā;

Āharāmi tato disvā, maṃ satthā etadabravi”.

I bring water for my preceptor from the great lake Anotatta. Then, having seen me, the Teacher said this:

431.

431.

“Sāriputta imaṃ passa, āgacchantaṃ kumārakaṃ;

Udakakumbhamādāya, ajjhattaṃ susamāhitaṃ.

“Sāriputta, look at this young novice coming, carrying a water pot, inwardly well-composed.

432.

432.

“Pāsādikena vattena, kalyāṇairiyāpatho;

Sāmaṇeronuruddhassa, iddhiyā ca visārado.

“Endowed with pleasing conduct and graceful deportment, this novice of Anuruddha is also skilled in psychic power.

433.

433.

“Ājānīyena ājañño, sādhunā sādhukārito;

Vinīto anuruddhena, katakiccena sikkhito.

“A thoroughbred trained by a thoroughbred, well-trained by a virtuous one, he has been disciplined by Anuruddha, trained by one who has done what had to be done.

434.

434.

“So patvā paramaṃ santiṃ, sacchikatvā akuppataṃ;

Sāmaṇero sa sumano, mā maṃ jaññāti icchatī”ti.

“Having attained the supreme peace, having realized the unshakeable, that novice Sumana wishes: ‘May no one know me.’”

… Sumano thero….

… The Elder Sumana…

11. Nhātakamunittheragāthā

11. The Verses of the Elder Nhātakamuni

435.

435.

“Vātarogābhinīto [M 0.0288] tvaṃ, viharaṃ kānane vane;

Paviddhagocare lūkhe, kathaṃ bhikkhu karissasi”.

“Afflicted by a wind-disease, dwelling in the forest grove, in a remote and rough alms-resort—how, bhikkhu, will you manage?”

436.

436.

“Pītisukhena vipulena, pharitvāna samussayaṃ;

Lūkhampi abhisambhonto, viharissāmi kānane.

“Having pervaded this entire body with abundant rapture and happiness, I will dwell in the forest, enduring even what is rough.

437.

437.

“Bhāvento satta bojjhaṅge, indriyāni balāni ca;

Jhānasokhummasampanno jhānasukhumasampanno (syā. ka.), viharissaṃ anāsavo.

“Developing the seven factors of enlightenment, the spiritual faculties, and the powers, endowed with the subtlety of jhāna, I will dwell free from taints.

438.

438.

“Vippamuttaṃ [T 0.0334] kilesehi, suddhacittaṃ anāvilaṃ;

Abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhanto, viharissaṃ anāsavo.

“Constantly contemplating the mind as freed from defilements, pure, and unstirred, I will dwell free from taints.

439.

439.

“Ajjhattañca bahiddhā ca, ye me vijjiṃsu āsavā;

Sabbe asesā ucchinnā, na ca uppajjare puna.

“Whatever taints of mine there were, internal and external, all have been cut off without remainder; they will not arise again.

440.

440.

“Pañcakkhandhā pariññātā, tiṭṭhanti chinnamūlakā;

Dukkhakkhayo anuppatto, natthi dāni punabbhavo”ti.

“The five aggregates have been fully understood; they stand with their root cut off. The destruction of suffering has been attained; now there is no further becoming.”

… Nhātakamunitthero….

… The Elder Nhātakamuni…

12. Brahmadattattheragāthā

12. The Verses of the Elder Brahmadatta

441.

441.

“Akkodhassa kuto kodho, dantassa samajīvino;

Sammadaññā vimuttassa, upasantassa tādino.

“Whence is there anger for one without anger, for one who is tamed and lives a balanced life; for one liberated through perfect knowledge, peaceful and steadfast?

442.

442.

“Tasseva [V 0.0226][P 0.0047] tena pāpiyo, yo kuddhaṃ paṭikujjhati;

Kuddhaṃ appaṭikujjhanto, saṅgāmaṃ jeti dujjayaṃ.

“He is the more evil of the two who returns anger for anger. By not returning anger for anger, one wins a battle hard to win.

443.

443.

saṃ. ni. 1.188, 250 “Ubhinnamatthaṃ carati, attano ca parassa ca;

Paraṃ saṅkupitaṃ ñatvā, yo sato upasammati.

“He practices for the welfare of both, his own and the other’s, who, knowing the other is provoked, mindfully becomes calm.

444.

444.
