“Tenāyaṃ desito dhammo, khayagāmī anuttaro;

Tassa sāsanamāgamma, labbhate taṃ asokatā”.

“By him this Dhamma has been taught, leading to the exhaustion of defilements, unsurpassed. By relying on his teaching, that sorrowlessness is obtained.”

724.

724.

Sutvāna corā isino subhāsitaṃ, nikkhippa satthāni ca āvudhāni ca;

Tamhā ca kammā viramiṃsu eke, eke ca pabbajjamarocayiṃsu.

Having heard the seer’s well-spoken words, the thieves laid down their knives and their weapons; some desisted from that deed, while others chose the going forth.

725.

725.

Te pabbajitvā sugatassa sāsane, bhāvetva bojjhaṅgabalāni paṇḍitā;

Udaggacittā sumanā katindriyā, phusiṃsu nibbānapadaṃ asaṅkhatanti.

Having gone forth in the Well-farer’s dispensation, those wise ones developed the enlightenment factors and the spiritual powers. With minds uplifted, joyful, their faculties guarded, they attained the unconditioned state of Nibbāna.

…Adhimutto thero….

Thus the Elder Adhimutta spoke these verses.

2. Pārāpariyattheragāthā

2. The Verses of the Elder Pārāpariya

726.

726.

“Samaṇassa [T 0.0372] ahu cintā, pārāpariyassa bhikkhuno;

Ekakassa nisinnassa, pavivittassa jhāyino.

A thought occurred to the ascetic, the bhikkhu Pārāpariya, while he was sitting alone in seclusion, meditating:

727.

727.

“Kimānupubbaṃ puriso, kiṃ vataṃ kiṃ samācāraṃ;

Attano kiccakārīssa, na ca kañci viheṭhaye.

“What, in sequence, should a person practice? What vow, what conduct, should one undertake, so that in doing one’s own task, one would harm no one?

728.

728.

“Indriyāni [M 0.0322] manussānaṃ, hitāya ahitāya ca;

Arakkhitāni ahitāya, rakkhitāni hitāya ca.

“The faculties of humans are for their welfare and for their harm; unguarded, they are for their harm, but guarded, they are for their welfare.

729.

729.

“Indriyāneva sārakkhaṃ, indriyāni ca gopayaṃ;

Attano kiccakārīssa, na ca kañci viheṭhaye.

“Guarding only the faculties, and protecting the faculties, one would be doing one’s own task and would harm no one.

730.

730.

“Cakkhundriyaṃ [V 0.0257] ce rūpesu, gacchantaṃ anivārayaṃ;

Anādīnavadassāvī, so dukkhā na hi muccati.

“If one does not restrain the eye faculty as it ranges among forms, not seeing the danger, one is surely not freed from suffering.

731.

731.

“Sotindriyaṃ ce saddesu, gacchantaṃ anivārayaṃ;

Anādīnavadassāvī, so dukkhā na hi muccati.

“If one does not restrain the ear faculty as it ranges among sounds, not seeing the danger, one is surely not freed from suffering.

732.

732.

“Anissaraṇadassāvī[P 0.0073], gandhe ce paṭisevati;

Na so muccati dukkhamhā, gandhesu adhimucchito.

“Not seeing the escape, if one partakes of scents, one is not freed from suffering, being infatuated with scents.

733.

733.

“Ambilaṃ madhuraggañca, tittakaggamanussaraṃ;

Rasataṇhāya gadhito, hadayaṃ nāvabujjhati.

“Repeatedly recollecting the sour, the choicest sweet, and the choicest bitter, greedy with craving for tastes, one does not awaken the heart.

734.

734.

“Subhānyappaṭikūlāni, phoṭṭhabbāni anussaraṃ;

Ratto rāgādhikaraṇaṃ, vividhaṃ vindate dukhaṃ.

“Recollecting beautiful and agreeable tangible objects, being impassioned, one experiences manifold suffering on account of that lust.

735.

735.

“Manaṃ cetehi dhammehi, yo na sakkoti rakkhituṃ;

Tato [T 0.0373] naṃ dukkhamanveti, sabbehetehi pañcahi.

“Whoever is unable to guard the mind from these phenomena, suffering follows them on account of all these five.

736.

736.

“Pubbalohitasampuṇṇaṃ, bahussa kuṇapassa ca;

Naravīrakataṃ vagguṃ, samuggamiva cittitaṃ.

“Filled with pus and blood, and with much carrion; made by a ‘hero among men,’ lovely, like a decorated casket.

737.

737.

“Kaṭukaṃ madhurassādaṃ, piyanibandhanaṃ dukhaṃ;

Khuraṃva madhunā littaṃ, ullihaṃ nāvabujjhati.

“Bitter, with a sweet taste, a painful binder to what is dear—like a razor smeared with honey, one licks it but does not understand.

738.

738.

“Itthirūpe itthisare, phoṭṭhabbepi ca itthiyā;

Itthigandhesu sāratto, vividhaṃ vindate dukhaṃ.

“Attached to a woman’s form, her voice, her touch, and her scents, one experiences manifold suffering.

739.

739.

“Itthisotāni sabbāni, sandanti pañca pañcasu;

Tesamāvaraṇaṃ kātuṃ, yo sakkoti vīriyavā.

“All the streams related to a woman flow, five through five. The energetic one is he who is able to construct a barrier against them.

740.

740.

“So atthavā so dhammaṭṭho, so dakkho so vicakkhaṇo;

Kareyya ramamānopi, kiccaṃ dhammatthasaṃhitaṃ.

“He is wise, he is established in the Dhamma, he is skilled, he is discerning. Even while taking delight, he would do the task connected with the goal and the Dhamma.

741.

741.

“Atho [M 0.0323] sīdati saññuttaṃ, vajje kiccaṃ niratthakaṃ;

‘Na taṃ kicca’nti maññitvā, appamatto vicakkhaṇo.

“One who is attached sinks down. A heedful and discerning one should avoid a useless task, recognizing, ‘That is not a task to be done.’

742.

742.

“Yañca atthena saññuttaṃ, yā ca dhammagatā rati;

Taṃ samādāya vattetha, sā hi ve uttamā rati.

“Whatever is connected with the goal, and whatever delight is founded on the Dhamma—one should undertake that and live by it, for that is truly the supreme delight.

743.

743.

“Uccāvacehupāyehi, paresamabhijigīsati;

Hantvā vadhitvā atha socayitvā, ālopati sāhasā yo paresaṃ.

“By various means, one desires to take from others. Having killed, having beaten, and then having caused them to grieve, one violently plunders others.

744.

744.

“Tacchanto āṇiyā āṇiṃ, nihanti balavā yathā;

Indriyānindriyeheva[T 0.0374], nihanti kusalo tathā.

“Just as a strong man, chipping away, drives out a peg with another peg, so the skilled one subdues the faculties with the faculties themselves.

745.

745.

“Saddhaṃ [V 0.0258] vīriyaṃ samādhiñca, satipaññañca bhāvayaṃ;

Pañca pañcahi hantvāna, anīgho yāti brāhmaṇo.

“Developing faith, energy, concentration, mindfulness, and wisdom—having slain the five with these five—the brahmin goes free from trouble.

746.

746.

“So atthavā so dhammaṭṭho, katvā vākyānusāsaniṃ;

Sabbena sabbaṃ buddhassa, so naro sukhamedhatī”ti.

“He is wise, he is established in the Dhamma. Having followed the instruction in the word of the Buddha completely in all respects, that person prospers in happiness.”

…Pārāpariyo thero….

… The Elder Pārāpariya …

3. Telakānittheragāthā

3. The Verses of the Elder Telakāni

747.

747.

“Cirarattaṃ vatātāpī, dhammaṃ anuvicintayaṃ;

Samaṃ cittassa nālatthaṃ, pucchaṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇe.

“For a long time, indeed, I was strenuous, reflecting on the Dhamma, yet I did not attain peace of mind, though I asked ascetics and brahmins.

748.

748.

“‘Ko [P 0.0074] so pāraṅgato loke, ko patto amatogadhaṃ;

Kassa dhammaṃ paṭicchāmi, paramatthavijānanaṃ’.

“‘Who in this world has gone to the far shore? Who has attained the state immersed in the Deathless? Whose Dhamma should I accept for the knowledge of the ultimate reality?’

749.

749.

“Antovaṅkagato āsi, macchova ghasamāmisaṃ;

Baddho mahindapāsena, vepacityasuro yathā.

“I was inwardly crooked, like a fish that has swallowed the bait; bound by the snare of the great Indra, just as was the asura Vepacitti.

750.

750.

“Añchāmi naṃ na muñcāmi, asmā sokapariddavā;

Ko me bandhaṃ muñcaṃ loke, sambodhiṃ vedayissati.

“I struggle with this bond, yet am not freed from this sorrow and lamentation. Who in the world, by releasing my bond, will make enlightenment known to me?

751.

751.

“Samaṇaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ vā kaṃ, ādisantaṃ pabhaṅgunaṃ.

Kassa dhammaṃ paṭicchāmi, jarāmaccupavāhanaṃ.

“What ascetic or brahmin can teach that which destroys defilements? Whose Dhamma should I accept, which carries one beyond old age and death?

752.

752.

“Vicikicchākaṅkhāganthitaṃ, sārambhabalasaññutaṃ;

Kodhappattamanatthaddhaṃ, abhijappappadāraṇaṃ.

“I was knotted by doubt and uncertainty, yoked to the force of contention, afflicted by anger, mentally rigid, and torn apart by craving.

753.

753.

“Taṇhādhanusamuṭṭhānaṃ[M 0.0324], dve ca pannarasāyutaṃ dvedhāpannarasāyutaṃ (?);

Passa [T 0.0375] orasikaṃ bāḷhaṃ, bhetvāna yadi yada (sī. aṭṭha.) hadi (?) “hadaye”ti taṃsaṃvaṇṇanā tiṭṭhati.

“See the powerful dart lodged in the breast, sprung from the bow of craving, and comprising thirty divisions. See how, having pierced the heart, it remains.

754.

754.

“Anudiṭṭhīnaṃ appahānaṃ, saṅkappaparatejitaṃ;

Tena viddho pavedhāmi, pattaṃva māluteritaṃ.

“Due to not having abandoned speculative views, and being inflamed by wrong intentions, I am pierced by that dart and tremble like a leaf struck by the wind.

755.

755.

“Ajjhattaṃ me samuṭṭhāya, khippaṃ paccati māmakaṃ;

Chaphassāyatanī kāyo, yattha sarati sabbadā.

“Arising from within me, what is ‘mine’ is quickly burned—this body of the six sense bases, wherein craving always proceeds.

756.

756.

“Taṃ na passāmi tekicchaṃ, yo metaṃ sallamuddhare;

Nānārajjena satthena nāraggena na satthena (?), nāññena vicikicchitaṃ.

“I see no physician who could extract this dart of doubt for me; not with various cords and a knife, nor by any other means.

757.

757.

“Ko me asattho avaṇo, sallamabbhantarapassayaṃ;

Ahiṃsaṃ sabbagattāni, sallaṃ me uddharissati.

“Who, without a knife and without inflicting a wound, not harming any of my limbs, will extract this dart of mine lodged deep within?

758.

758.

“Dhammappati [V 0.0259] hi so seṭṭho, visadosappavāhako;

Gambhīre patitassa me, thalaṃ pāṇiñca dassaye.

“For he, the Lord of the Dhamma, is the best, the remover of the poison of defilements. For me, who had fallen into the deep, he would show dry land and a helping hand.

759.

759.

“Rahadehamasmi ogāḷho, ahāriyarajamattike;

Māyāusūyasārambha, thinamiddhamapatthaṭe.

“I am plunged into the great lake, into irremovable dust and mud, where deceit, envy, contention, sloth, and torpor are spread about.

760.

760.

“Uddhaccameghathanitaṃ, saṃyojanavalāhakaṃ;

Vāhā vahanti kuddiṭṭhiṃ duddiṭṭhiṃ (sī. dha. pa. 339), saṅkappā rāganissitā.

“Torrents of wrong intentions, founded on lust—with restlessness as their thunder and the fetters as their storm clouds—carry away me of wrong view.

761.

761.

“Savanti sabbadhi sotā, latā ubbhijja tiṭṭhati;

Te sote ko nivāreyya, taṃ lataṃ ko hi checchati.

“Streams flow everywhere; the creeper of craving sprouts and stands fast. Who can hold back those streams? Who indeed will cut that creeper?

762.

762.

“Velaṃ [P 0.0075] karotha bhaddante, sotānaṃ sannivāraṇaṃ;

Mā te manomayo soto, rukkhaṃva sahasā luve.

“Venerable Sirs, build a dam, a restraint for these streams, lest the mind-born current should violently cut me down like a tree.

763.

763.

“Evaṃ [T 0.0376] me bhayajātassa, apārā pāramesato;

Tāṇo paññāvudho satthā, isisaṅghanisevito.

“Thus for me, in whom fear had arisen, seeking the far shore from the near, the Teacher was a shelter, armed with wisdom, attended by the assembly of seers.

764.

764.

“Sopāṇaṃ sugataṃ suddhaṃ, dhammasāramayaṃ daḷhaṃ;

Pādāsi vuyhamānassa, ‘mā bhāyī’ti ca mabravi.

“He gave me a well-made, pure, firm stairway, made of the essence of the Dhamma, as I was being swept away, and he said to me, ‘Do not fear!’

765.

765.

“Satipaṭṭhānapāsādaṃ, āruyha paccavekkhisaṃ;

Yaṃ taṃ pubbe amaññissaṃ, sakkāyābhirataṃ pajaṃ.

“Having ascended the palace of the foundations of mindfulness, I looked down upon the people who delight in their personal identity, a state I formerly esteemed.

766.

766.

“Yadā [M 0.0325] ca maggamaddakkhiṃ, nāvāya abhirūhanaṃ;

Anadhiṭṭhāya attānaṃ, titthamaddakkhimuttamaṃ.

“And when I saw the path for embarking upon the ship, without taking a stand on self, I beheld the supreme ford.

767.

767.

“Sallaṃ attasamuṭṭhānaṃ, bhavanettippabhāvitaṃ;

Etesaṃ appavattāya appavattiyā (?), desesi maggamuttamaṃ.

“For the non-occurrence of this dart—arisen from oneself and produced by the craving for existence—He taught the supreme path.

768.

768.

“Dīgharattānusayitaṃ, cirarattamadhiṭṭhitaṃ;

Buddho mepānudī ganthaṃ, visadosappavāhano”ti.

“That which had long lain latent, that which had long been established—the Buddha, the remover of the poison of defilements, has driven out that bond of mine.”

…Telakāni thero….

Thus the Elder Telakāni spoke these verses.

4. Raṭṭhapālattheragāthā

4. The Verses of the Elder Raṭṭhapāla

769.

769.

ma. ni. 2.302 “Passa cittakataṃ bimbaṃ, arukāyaṃ samussitaṃ;

Āturaṃ bahusaṅkappaṃ, yassa natthi dhuvaṃ ṭhiti.

Behold this decorated form, a body of sores, piled up, diseased, an object of many thoughts, for which there is no permanent stability.

770.

770.

“Passa cittakataṃ rūpaṃ, maṇinā kuṇḍalena ca;

Aṭṭhiṃ tacena onaddhaṃ, saha vatthehi sobhati.

Behold this decorated form, with its jewel and earring; a skeleton bound with skin, it shines together with its clothes.

771.

771.

“Alattakakatā [V 0.0260] pādā, mukhaṃ cuṇṇakamakkhitaṃ;

Alaṃ bālassa mohāya, no ca pāragavesino.

Feet dyed with lac, a face smeared with powder: enough to delude a fool, but not one who seeks the far shore.

772.

772.

“Aṭṭhapadakatā [T 0.0377] kesā, nettā añjanamakkhitā;

Alaṃ bālassa mohāya, no ca pāragavesino.

Hair arranged in eight parts, eyes smeared with collyrium: enough to delude a fool, but not one who seeks the far shore.

773.

773.

“Añjanīva navā cittā, pūtikāyo alaṅkato;

Alaṃ bālassa mohāya, no ca pāragavesino.

Like a new, decorated collyrium pot, this putrid body is adorned: enough to delude a fool, but not one who seeks the far shore.

774.

774.

“Odahi migavo pāsaṃ, nāsadā vāguraṃ migo;

Bhutvā nivāpaṃ gacchāma, kandante migabandhake.

The hunter set the snare; the deer did not approach the trap. Having eaten the bait, we go, while the deer-trapper laments.

775.

775.

“Chinno pāso migavassa, nāsadā vāguraṃ migo;

Bhutvā nivāpaṃ gacchāma, socante migaluddake.

The hunter’s snare is cut; the deer did not approach the trap. Having eaten the bait, we go, while the deer-hunter grieves.

776.

776.

“Passāmi loke sadhane manusse, laddhāna vittaṃ na dadanti mohā;

Luddhā [P 0.0076] dhanaṃ sannicayaṃ karonti, bhiyyova kāme abhipatthayanti.

I see wealthy people in the world who, having acquired riches, do not give because of delusion. Greedily they accumulate wealth and long for sensual pleasures all the more.

777.

777.

“Rājā [M 0.0326] pasayhappathaviṃ vijetvā, sasāgarantaṃ mahimāvasanto;

Oraṃ samuddassa atittarūpo, pāraṃ samuddassapi patthayetha.

A king, having conquered the earth by force and ruling the land to the ocean’s shore, being unsatisfied with the near side of the sea, would long for the far side of the sea as well.

778.

778.

“Rājā ca aññe ca bahū manussā, avītataṇhā maraṇaṃ upenti;

Ūnāva hutvāna jahanti dehaṃ, kāmehi lokamhi na hatthi titti.

A king and many other people, with craving unallayed, approach death. Still wanting, they abandon the body. In the world, there is no satisfaction from sensual pleasures.

779.

779.

“Kandanti [T 0.0378] naṃ ñātī pakiriya kese, aho vatā no amarāti cāhu;

Vatthena naṃ pārutaṃ nīharitvā, citaṃ samodhāya tato ḍahanti.

His kinsmen, with hair dishevelled, weep for him, crying, ‘Alas, our kinsman is not immortal!’ Having wrapped him in a cloth and carried him out, they place him on a pyre and then burn him.

780.

780.

“So ḍayhati sūlehi tujjamāno, ekena vatthena etena gatthena (ka.) pahāya bhoge;

Na mīyamānassa bhavanti tāṇā, ñātī ca mittā atha vā sahāyā.

He is burned, prodded with stakes, having left his possessions behind with a single cloth. For one who is dying, there are no protectors: not kinsmen, friends, or companions.

781.

781.

“Dāyādakā tassa dhanaṃ haranti, satto pana gacchati yena kammaṃ;

Na mīyamānaṃ dhanamanveti manviti (ka.) kiñci, puttā ca dārā ca dhanañca raṭṭhaṃ.

His heirs take his wealth, while the being goes according to his kamma. Nothing follows the one who is dying: not children, wife, wealth, or kingdom.

782.

782.

“Na dīghamāyuṃ labhate dhanena, na cāpi vittena jaraṃ vihanti;

Appappaṃ hidaṃ jīvitamāhu dhīrā, asassataṃ vippariṇāmadhammaṃ.

One does not obtain a long life with wealth, nor does one ward off old age with riches. The wise say this life is short, impermanent, and subject to change.

783.

783.

“Aḍḍhā daliddā ca phusanti phassaṃ, bālo ca dhīro ca tatheva phuṭṭho;

Bālo hi bālyā vadhitova seti, dhīro [T 0.0379] ca no vedhati phassaphuṭṭho.

The rich and the poor experience contact; the fool and the wise are likewise touched. Indeed, the fool, through his folly, lies as if slain; but the wise one, when touched by contact, does not tremble.

784.

784.

“Tasmā [M 0.0327] hi paññāva dhanena seyyā, yāya vosānamidhādhigacchati;

Abyositattā hi bhavābhavesu, pāpāni kammāni karoti mohā.

Therefore, wisdom is indeed better than wealth, for by it one attains the consummation here. Because of not having reached the consummation, a deluded person does evil deeds in life after life.

785.

785.

“Upeti [P 0.0077] gabbhañca parañca lokaṃ, saṃsāramāpajja paramparāya;

Tassappapañño abhisaddahanto, upeti gabbhañca parañca lokaṃ.

One enters a womb and the next world, falling into saṃsāra in succession. One of little wisdom, placing faith in such a one, also enters a womb and the next world.

786.

786.

“Coro [V 0.0261] yathā sandhimukhe gahīto, sakammunā haññati pāpadhammo;

Evaṃ pajā pecca paramhi loke, sakammunā haññati pāpadhammo.

Just as a thief of evil nature, caught at a breach, is tormented for his own deed, so too a being of evil nature, after passing away, is tormented in the next world for his own deed.

787.

787.

“Kāmā hi citrā madhurā manoramā, virūparūpena mathenti cittaṃ;

Ādīnavaṃ kāmaguṇesu disvā, tasmā ahaṃ pabbajitomhi rāja.

Sensual pleasures—varied, sweet, and delightful—churn the mind with their manifold forms. Having seen the danger in the strands of sensual pleasure, O king, I have therefore gone forth.

788.

788.

“Dumapphalānīva patanti māṇavā, daharā ca vuḍḍhā ca sarīrabhedā;

Etampi [T 0.0380] disvā pabbajitomhi rāja, apaṇṇakaṃ sāmaññameva seyyo.

Like fruits from a tree, beings fall—both young and old—at the breaking up of the body. Seeing this too, O king, I have gone forth. The ascetic life is indeed the certain, better path.

789.

789.

“Saddhāyāhaṃ pabbajito, upeto jinasāsane;

Avajjhā mayhaṃ pabbajjā, anaṇo bhuñjāmi bhojanaṃ.

I have gone forth out of faith, having entered the Victor’s Dispensation. My going forth is not barren; free of debt, I eat my food.

790.

790.

“Kāme ādittato disvā, jātarūpāni satthato;

Gabbhavokkantito dukkhaṃ, nirayesu mahabbhayaṃ.

Seeing sensual pleasures as ablaze, gold and silver as a weapon, the descent into the womb as suffering, and the great fear in the hells,

791.

791.

“Etamādīnavaṃ ñatvā, saṃvegaṃ alabhiṃ tadā;

Sohaṃ viddho tadā santo, sampatto āsavakkhayaṃ.

Having known this danger, I then gained a sense of urgency. I who was then pierced have now attained the destruction of the taints.

792.

792.

“Pariciṇṇo mayā satthā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ;

Ohito garuko bhāro, bhavanetti samūhatā.

The Teacher has been served by me; the Buddha’s teaching has been done. The heavy burden has been laid down; the guide to existence has been uprooted.

793.

793.

“Yassatthāya pabbajito, agārasmānagāriyaṃ;

So me attho anuppatto, sabbasaṃyojanakkhayo”ti.

The goal for which I went forth from home into homelessness—that goal has been attained by me: the destruction of all fetters.

… Raṭṭhapālo thero….

… The Elder Raṭṭhapāla …

5. Mālukyaputtattheragāthā

5. The Verses of the Elder Mālukyaputta

794.

794.

saṃ. ni. 4.95 “Rūpaṃ [M 0.0328] disvā sati muṭṭhā, piyaṃ nimittaṃ manasi karoto;

Sārattacitto vedeti, tañca ajjhossa tiṭṭhati.

Having seen a form, mindfulness is lost for one who attends to a pleasing sign. With an impassioned mind, one experiences it with delight, and remains, having clung to it.

795.

795.

“Tassa [T 0.0381] vaḍḍhanti vedanā, anekā rūpasambhavā;

Abhijjhā ca vihesā ca, cittamassūpahaññati;

Evamācinato dukkhaṃ, ārā nibbāna nibbānaṃ (sī.) vuccati.

For him, manifold feelings born of form increase; covetousness and vexation assail his mind. For one who thus accumulates suffering, Nibbāna is said to be far away.

796.

796.

“Saddaṃ sutvā sati muṭṭhā, piyaṃ nimittaṃ manasi karoto;

Sārattacitto vedeti, tañca ajjhossa tiṭṭhati.

Having heard a sound, mindfulness is lost for one who attends to a pleasing sign. With an impassioned mind, one feels, and remains, clinging to it.

797.

797.

“Tassa vaḍḍhanti vedanā, anekā saddasambhavā;

Abhijjhā ca vihesā ca, cittamassūpahaññati;

Evamācinato dukkhaṃ, ārā nibbāna vuccati.

For him, manifold feelings born of sound increase; covetousness and vexation assail his mind. For one who thus accumulates suffering, Nibbāna is said to be far away.

798.

798.

“Gandhaṃ ghatvā sati muṭṭhā, piyaṃ nimittaṃ manasi karoto;

Sārattacitto vedeti, tañca ajjhossa tiṭṭhati.

Having smelled an odor, mindfulness is lost for one who attends to a pleasing sign. With an impassioned mind, one feels, and remains, clinging to it.

799.

799.

“Tassa [V 0.0262] vaḍḍhanti vedanā, anekā gandhasambhavā;

Abhijjhā ca vihesā ca, cittamassūpahaññati;

Evamācinato dukkhaṃ, ārā nibbāna vuccati.

For him, manifold feelings born of odors increase; covetousness and vexation assail his mind. For one who thus accumulates suffering, Nibbāna is said to be far away.

800.

800.

“Rasaṃ bhotvā sati muṭṭhā, piyaṃ nimittaṃ manasi karoto;

Sārattacitto vedeti, tañca ajjhossa tiṭṭhati.

Having savored a taste, mindfulness is lost for one who attends to a pleasing sign. With an impassioned mind, one feels, and remains, clinging to it.

801.

801.

“Tassa [T 0.0382] vaḍḍhanti vedanā, anekā rasasambhavā;

Abhijjhā ca vihesā ca, cittamassūpahaññati;

Evamācinato dukkhaṃ, ārā nibbāna vuccati.

For him, manifold feelings born of tastes increase; covetousness and vexation assail his mind. For one who thus accumulates suffering, Nibbāna is said to be far away.

802.

802.

“Phassaṃ [P 0.0078] phussa sati muṭṭhā, piyaṃ nimittaṃ manasi karoto;

Sārattacitto vedeti, tañca ajjhossa tiṭṭhati.

Having felt a contact, mindfulness is lost for one who attends to a pleasing sign. With an impassioned mind, one feels, and remains, clinging to it.

803.

803.

“Tassa vaḍḍhanti vedanā, anekā phassasambhavā;

Abhijjhā ca vihesā ca, cittamassūpahaññati;

Evamācinato dukkhaṃ, ārā nibbāna vuccati.

For him, manifold feelings born of contacts increase; covetousness and vexation assail his mind. For one who thus accumulates suffering, Nibbāna is said to be far away.

804.

804.

“Dhammaṃ ñatvā sati muṭṭhā, piyaṃ nimittaṃ manasi karoto;

Sārattacitto vedeti, tañca ajjhossa tiṭṭhati.

Having cognized a mental object, mindfulness is lost for one who attends to a pleasing sign. With an impassioned mind, one feels, and remains, clinging to it.

805.

805.

“Tassa [M 0.0329] vaḍḍhanti vedanā, anekā dhammasambhavā;

Abhijjhā ca vihesā ca, cittamassūpahaññati;

Evamācinato dukkhaṃ, ārā nibbāna vuccati.

For him, manifold feelings born of mental objects increase; covetousness and vexation assail his mind. For one who thus accumulates suffering, Nibbāna is said to be far away.

806.

806.

“Na so rajjati rūpesu, rūpaṃ disvā patissato;

Virattacitto vedeti, tañca nājjhossa tiṭṭhati.

He is not impassioned by forms; having seen a form, he is mindful. With a dispassionate mind, he feels, and remains, not clinging to it.

807.

807.

“Yathāssa passato rūpaṃ, sevato cāpi vedanaṃ;

Khīyati nopacīyati, evaṃ so caratī sato;

Evaṃ apacinato dukkhaṃ, santike nibbāna vuccati.

Just as for him, while seeing a form and attending to a feeling, it is destroyed and does not accumulate, so he fares mindfully. For one who thus diminishes suffering, Nibbāna is said to be near.

808.

808.

“Na so rajjati saddesu, saddaṃ sutvā patissato;

Virattacitto vedeti, tañca nājjhossa tiṭṭhati.

He is not impassioned by sounds; having heard a sound, he is mindful. With a dispassionate mind, he feels, and remains, not clinging to it.

809.

809.

“Yathāssa suṇato saddaṃ, sevato cāpi vedanaṃ;

Khīyati nopacīyati, evaṃ so caratī sato;

Evaṃ apacinato dukkhaṃ, santike nibbāna vuccati.

Just as for him, while hearing a sound and attending to a feeling, it is destroyed and does not accumulate, so he fares mindfully. For one who thus diminishes suffering, Nibbāna is said to be near.

810.

810.

“Na so rajjati gandhesu, gandhaṃ ghatvā patissato;

Virattacitto vedeti, tañca nājjhossa tiṭṭhati.

He is not impassioned by odors; having smelled an odor, he is mindful. With a dispassionate mind, he feels, and remains, not clinging to it.

811.

811.

“Yathāssa [V 0.0263] ghāyato gandhaṃ, sevato cāpi vedanaṃ;

Khīyati nopacīyati, evaṃ so caratī sato;

Evaṃ apacinato dukkhaṃ, santike nibbāna vuccati.

Just as for him, while smelling an odor and attending to a feeling, it is destroyed and does not accumulate, so he fares mindfully. For one who thus diminishes suffering, Nibbāna is said to be near.

812.

812.

“Na [T 0.0383] so rajjati rasesu, rasaṃ bhotvā patissato;

Virattacitto vedeti, tañca nājjhossa tiṭṭhati.

He is not impassioned by tastes; having savored a taste, he is mindful. With a dispassionate mind, he feels, and remains, not clinging to it.

813.

813.

“Yathāssa sāyarato rasaṃ, sevato cāpi vedanaṃ;

Khīyati nopacīyati, evaṃ so caratī sato;

Evaṃ apacinato dukkhaṃ, santike nibbāna vuccati.

Just as for him, while savoring a taste and attending to a feeling, it is destroyed and does not accumulate, so he fares mindfully. For one who thus diminishes suffering, Nibbāna is said to be near.

814.

814.

“Na so rajjati phassesu, phassaṃ phussa patissato;

Virattacitto vedeti, tañca nājjhossa tiṭṭhati.

He is not impassioned by contacts; having felt a contact, he is mindful. With a dispassionate mind, he feels, and remains, not clinging to it.

815.

815.

“Yathāssa phusato phassaṃ, sevato cāpi vedanaṃ;

Khīyati nopacīyati, evaṃ so caratī sato;

Evaṃ apacinato dukkhaṃ, santike nibbāna vuccati.

Just as for him, while feeling a contact and attending to a feeling, it is destroyed and does not accumulate, so he fares mindfully. For one who thus diminishes suffering, Nibbāna is said to be near.

816.

816.

“Na so rajjati dhammesu, dhammaṃ ñatvā patissato;

Virattacitto vedeti, tañca nājjhossa tiṭṭhati.

He is not impassioned by mental objects; having cognized a mental object, he is mindful. With a dispassionate mind, he feels, and remains, not clinging to it.

817.

817.

“Yathāssa [M 0.0330] vijānato dhammaṃ, sevato cāpi vedanaṃ;

Khīyati nopacīyati, evaṃ so caratī sato;

Evaṃ apacinato dukkhaṃ, santike nibbāna vuccati”.

Just as for him, while cognizing a mental object and attending to a feeling, it is destroyed and does not accumulate, so he fares mindfully. For one who thus diminishes suffering, Nibbāna is said to be near.

… Mālukyaputto thero….

Thus the Elder Mālukyaputta spoke these verses.

6. Selattheragāthā

6. The Verses of the Elder Sela

818.

818.

“Paripuṇṇakāyo suruci, sujāto cārudassano;

Suvaṇṇavaṇṇosi bhagavā, susukkadāṭhosi vīriyavā susukkadāṭho virīyavā (sī.).

6. Perfectly complete in body, radiant, well-born, of lovely appearance; you are of golden complexion, Blessed One, you have very white teeth and are full of energy.

819.

819.

“Narassa hi sujātassa, ye bhavanti viyañjanā;

Sabbe [T 0.0384] te tava kāyasmiṃ, mahāpurisalakkhaṇā.

Whatever are the marks of a well-born man, all those marks of a Great Man are on your body.

820.

820.

“Pasannanetto sumukho, brahā uju patāpavā;

Majjhe samaṇasaṅghassa, ādiccova virocasi.

With serene eyes and a beautiful face, you are noble, upright, and majestic. In the midst of the Saṅgha of ascetics, you shine like the sun.

821.

821.

“Kalyāṇadassano bhikkhu, kañcanasannibhattaco;

Kiṃ te samaṇabhāvena, evaṃ uttamavaṇṇino.

O monk of lovely appearance, with skin like burnished gold; being of such a supreme complexion, what is the ascetic’s life to you?

822.

822.

“Rājā [V 0.0264] arahasi bhavituṃ, cakkavattī rathesabho;

Cāturanto vijitāvī, jambusaṇḍassa jambumaṇḍassa (ka.) issaro.

You are fit to be a king, a wheel-turning monarch, a lord of the chariot-riders, a conqueror of the four quarters, the lord of Jambusaṇḍa.

823.

823.

“Khattiyā bhogī rājāno bhogā rājāno (sī. ka.), bhojarājāno (syā.), anuyantā bhavanti te;

Rājābhirājā rājādhirājā (sī. ka.) manujindo, rajjaṃ kārehi gotama”.

Khattiyas, wealthy kings, would be your vassals. As a king of kings, a lord of men, rule the kingdom, Gotama!

824.

824.

“Rājāhamasmi [P 0.0079] sela, (selāti bhagavā) dhammarājā anuttaro;

Dhammena cakkaṃ vattemi, cakkaṃ appaṭivattiyaṃ”.

(The Blessed One:) “I am a king, Sela, the unsurpassed King of Dhamma. I turn the wheel by means of Dhamma, a wheel that cannot be rolled back.”

825.

825.

“Sambuddho paṭijānāsi, (iti selo brāhmaṇo) dhammarājā anuttaro;

‘Dhammena cakkaṃ vattemi’, iti bhāsatha gotama.

(Sela the brahmin:) “You claim to be a Perfectly Enlightened One, an unsurpassed King of Dhamma. ‘I turn the wheel by means of Dhamma,’ so you say, Gotama.”

826.

826.

“Ko nu senāpati bhoto, sāvako satthuranvayo anvayo (sī.);

Ko tetamanuvatteti, dhammacakkaṃ pavattitaṃ”.

“Who then is your general, venerable sir, the disciple who follows the Teacher? Who keeps this Dhamma Wheel rolling that has been set in motion by you?”

827.

827.

“Mayā [M 0.0331] pavattitaṃ cakkaṃ, (selāti bhagavā) dhammacakkaṃ anuttaraṃ;

Sāriputto anuvatteti, anujāto tathāgataṃ.

(The Blessed One:) “The unsurpassed Dhamma Wheel set in motion by me is kept rolling by Sāriputta, who is born after the Tathāgata.”

828.

828.

“Abhiññeyyaṃ abhiññātaṃ, bhāvetabbañca bhāvitaṃ;

Pahātabbaṃ pahīnaṃ me, tasmā buddhosmi brāhmaṇa.

“What is to be directly known, I have directly known; what is to be developed, I have developed; what is to be abandoned, I have abandoned. Therefore, brahmin, I am a Buddha.”

829.

829.

“Vinayassu [T 0.0385] mayi kaṅkhaṃ, adhimuñcassu brāhmaṇa;

Dullabhaṃ dassanaṃ hoti, sambuddhānaṃ abhiṇhaso.

“Dispel your doubt in me, brahmin, place your confidence. The sight of the Perfectly Enlightened Ones is exceedingly rare.”

830.

830.

“Yesaṃ ve dullabho loke, pātubhāvo abhiṇhaso;

Sohaṃ brāhmaṇa buddhosmi, sallakatto sallakanto (sī.) anuttaro.

“One of those whose appearance in the world is always rare, that Buddha am I, brahmin, the unsurpassed remover of darts.”

831.

831.

“Brahmabhūto atitulo, mārasenappamaddano;

Sabbāmitte vase vasī (syā. ka., ma. ni. 2.399; su. ni. 966) katvā, modāmi akutobhayo”.

“Become noble, incomparable, the crusher of Māra’s army; having subdued all my foes, I rejoice, free from all fear.”

832.

832.

“Idaṃ bhonto nisāmetha, yathā bhāsati cakkhumā;

Sallakatto mahāvīro, sīhova nadatī vane.

“Listen, sirs, to how the One with Vision speaks. The dart-remover, the great hero, roars like a lion in the forest.”

833.

833.

“Brahmabhūtaṃ atitulaṃ, mārasenappamaddanaṃ;

Ko disvā nappasīdeyya, api kaṇhābhijātiko.

“Having seen him—become noble, incomparable, the crusher of Māra’s army—who would not be filled with confidence, even one of dark origins?”

834.

834.

“Yo maṃ icchati anvetu, yo vā nicchati gacchatu;

Idhāhaṃ pabbajissāmi, varapaññassa santike”.

“Let him who wishes follow me; let him who does not wish depart. I myself will go forth right here in the presence of the one of excellent wisdom.”

835.

835.

“Etaṃ ce ruccati bhoto, sammāsambuddhasāsanaṃ;

Mayampi pabbajissāma, varapaññassa santike.

“If this teaching of the Perfectly Enlightened One is acceptable to you, sir, we too will go forth in the presence of the one of excellent wisdom.”

836.

836.

“Brāhmaṇā tisatā ime, yācanti pañjalīkatā;

‘Brahmacariyaṃ carissāma, bhagavā tava santike’”.

“These three hundred brahmins, with hands raised in homage, entreat you: ‘We would lead the holy life in your presence, Blessed One.’”

837.

837.

“Svākhātaṃ [V 0.0265] brahmacariyaṃ, (selāti bhagavā) sandiṭṭhikamakālikaṃ;

Yattha amoghā pabbajjā, appamattassa sikkhato”.

“The holy life is well expounded, Sela, directly visible, immediate. The going forth is not in vain for one who trains with diligence.”

838.

838.

“Yaṃ [P 0.0080] taṃ saraṇamāgamha saraṇamāgamma (sabbattha), ito aṭṭhame aṭṭhami (syā. ka.) cakkhuma;

Sattarattena bhagavā, dantāmha tava sāsane.

“O One with Vision, it was eight days ago that we came to you for refuge. Within seven nights, Blessed One, we have been tamed in your teaching.”

839.

839.

“Tuvaṃ [T 0.0386][M 0.0332] buddho tuvaṃ satthā, tuvaṃ mārābhibhū muni;

Tuvaṃ anusaye chetvā, tiṇṇo tāresimaṃ pajaṃ.

“You are the Buddha, you are the Teacher; you are the sage who vanquished Māra. Having cut off the underlying tendencies, you have crossed over and you ferry this generation across.”

840.

840.

“Upadhī te samatikkantā, āsavā te padālitā;

Sīhova anupādāno, pahīnabhayabheravo.

“Your acquisitions have been transcended, your taints have been shattered. Like a lion, without clinging, you have abandoned fear and terror.”

841.

841.

“Bhikkhavo tisatā ime, tiṭṭhanti pañjalīkatā;

Pāde vīra pasārehi, nāgā vandantu satthuno”ti.

“These three hundred bhikkhus stand with hands raised in homage. Stretch out your feet, O hero! Let these great ones pay homage to their Teacher.”

… Selo thero….

… The Elder Sela …

7. Kāḷigodhāputtabhaddiyattheragāthā

7. The Verses of the Elder Bhaddiya, Son of Kāḷigodhā

842.

842.

“Yātaṃ me hatthigīvāya, sukhumā vatthā padhāritā;

Sālīnaṃ odano bhutto, sucimaṃsūpasecano.

Formerly, I went, having sat on an elephant's neck; I wore fine garments. I ate rice of Sāli grain, with a sauce of pure meat.

843.

843.

“Sojja bhaddo sātatiko, uñchāpattāgate rato;

Jhāyati anupādāno, putto godhāya bhaddiyo.

Today, that Bhaddiya, son of Godhā, being virtuous and constantly blissful, delights in the alms gleaned into his bowl; free from clinging, he meditates.

844.

844.

“Paṃsukūlī sātatiko, uñchāpattāgate rato;

Jhāyati anupādāno, putto godhāya bhaddiyo.

A wearer of rag-robes, constantly blissful, delighting in the alms gleaned into his bowl; free from clinging, Bhaddiya, the son of Godhā, meditates.

845.

845.

“Piṇḍapātī sātatiko…pe….

An almsfood-eater, constantly blissful … etc. …

846.

846.

“Tecīvarī sātatiko…pe….

A wearer of the triple robe, constantly blissful … etc. …

847.

847.

“Sapadānacārī sātatiko…pe….

One who goes on alms round from house to house, constantly blissful … etc. …

848.

848.

“Ekāsanī sātatiko…pe….

A one-session-eater, constantly blissful … etc. …

849.

849.

“Pattapiṇḍī sātatiko…pe….

An alms-bowl-eater, constantly blissful … etc. …

850.

850.

“Khalupacchābhattī sātatiko…pe….

One who refuses food offered later, constantly blissful … etc. …

851.

851.

“Āraññiko sātatiko…pe….

A forest-dweller, constantly blissful … etc. …

852.

852.

“Rukkhamūliko [T 0.0387] sātatiko…pe….

A tree-root-dweller, constantly blissful … etc. …

853.

853.

“Abbhokāsī sātatiko…pe….

An open-air-dweller, constantly blissful … etc. …

854.

854.

“Sosāniko sātatiko…pe….

A charnel-ground-dweller, constantly blissful … etc. …

855.

855.

“Yathāsanthatiko sātatiko…pe….

One content with any lodging, constantly blissful … etc. …

856.

856.

“Nesajjiko [M 0.0333][V 0.0266] sātatiko…pe….

A sitter, constantly blissful … etc. …

857.

857.

“Appiccho sātatiko…pe….

One of few wishes, constantly blissful … etc. …

858.

858.

“Santuṭṭho sātatiko…pe….

Contented, constantly blissful … etc. …

859.

859.

“Pavivitto sātatiko…pe….

Secluded, constantly blissful … etc. …

860.

860.

“Asaṃsaṭṭho sātatiko…pe….

Not mixing with others, constantly blissful … etc. …

861.

861.

“Āraddhavīriyo sātatiko…pe….

With energy aroused, constantly blissful … etc. …

862.

862.

“Hitvā satapalaṃ kaṃsaṃ, sovaṇṇaṃ satarājikaṃ;

Aggahiṃ mattikāpattaṃ, idaṃ dutiyābhisecanaṃ.

Having abandoned a golden bowl of one hundred palas in weight, with many engravings, I took up an earthen bowl; this is the second consecration.

863.

863.

“Ucce maṇḍalipākāre, daḷhamaṭṭālakoṭṭhake;

Rakkhito khaggahatthehi, uttasaṃ vihariṃ pure.

Within high, circular ramparts, with strong towers and gatehouses, guarded by men with swords in hand, I formerly lived in fear.

864.

864.

“Sojja bhaddo anutrāsī, pahīnabhayabheravo;

Jhāyati vanamogayha, putto godhāya bhaddiyo.

Today, that Bhaddiya, son of Godhā, is fearless, with terror abandoned; having entered the forest, he meditates.

865.

865.

“Sīlakkhandhe patiṭṭhāya, satiṃ paññañca bhāvayaṃ;

Pāpuṇiṃ anupubbena, sabbasaṃyojanakkhaya”nti.

Established in the aggregate of virtue, developing mindfulness and wisdom, I have gradually reached the destruction of all fetters.

… Bhaddiyo kāḷigodhāya putto thero….

Thus the Elder Bhaddiya, son of Kāḷigodhā, spoke these verses.

8. Aṅgulimālattheragāthā

8. The Verses of the Elder Aṅgulimāla

866.

866.

“Gacchaṃ [T 0.0388] vadesi samaṇa ‘ṭṭhitomhi’, mamañca brūsi ṭhitamaṭṭhitoti;

Pucchāmi [P 0.0081] taṃ samaṇa etamatthaṃ, ‘kathaṃ ṭhito tvaṃ ahamaṭṭhitomhi’”.

“While you are walking, recluse, you say, ‘I am standing still’; and you say that I, who am standing, am not standing still. I ask you this, recluse: How are you standing still, and how am I not standing still?”

867.

867.

“Ṭhito ahaṃ aṅgulimāla sabbadā, sabbesu bhūtesu nidhāya daṇḍaṃ;

Tuvañca pāṇesu asaññatosi, tasmā ṭhitohaṃ tuvamaṭṭhitosi”.

“I, Aṅgulimāla, am standing still, having always laid aside the rod toward all beings. But you are unrestrained toward living beings; therefore, I am standing still, while you are not.”

868.

868.

“Cirassaṃ vata me mahito mahesī, mahāvanaṃ samaṇo paccapādi paccupādi (sabbattha);

Sohaṃ cajissāmi sahassapāpaṃ, sutvāna gāthaṃ tava dhammayuttaṃ”.

“Indeed, for a very long time the great seer, the recluse, has been honored by me! He has come to the great forest for my sake. Having heard your verse connected with the Dhamma, I will abandon a thousand evils.”

869.

869.

Icceva [M 0.0334] coro asimāvudhañca, sobbhe papāte narake anvakāsi akiri (ma. ni. 2.349);

Avandi coro sugatassa pāde, tattheva pabbajjamayāci buddhaṃ.

Having said just this, the robber cast his sword and weapons into a precipice, a chasm, a fissure. The robber paid homage to the feet of the Sugata and, in that very place, requested the going forth from the Buddha.

870.

870.

Buddho ca kho kāruṇiko mahesi, yo satthā lokassa sadevakassa;

‘Tamehi bhikkhū’ti tadā avoca, eseva tassa ahu bhikkhubhāvo.

Indeed, the Buddha—the compassionate Great Seer, the Teacher of the world with its devas—at that time spoke to him these words: ‘Come, bhikkhu.’ This very utterance constituted his state of being a bhikkhu.

871.

871.

“Yo [T 0.0389] ca pubbe pamajjitvā, pacchā so nappamajjati;

Somaṃ lokaṃ pabhāseti, abbhā muttova candimā.

“Whoever, having been heedless before, is afterwards not heedless, illuminates this world like the moon freed from a cloud.

872.

872.

“Yassa [V 0.0267] pāpaṃ kataṃ kammaṃ, kusalena pidhīyati pithīyati (sī. syā.);

Somaṃ lokaṃ pabhāseti, abbhā muttova candimā.

“He whose evil kamma that was done is covered over by the wholesome, illuminates this world like the moon freed from a cloud.

873.

873.

“Yo have daharo bhikkhu, yuñjati buddhasāsane;

Somaṃ lokaṃ pabhāseti, abbhā muttova candimā.

“Indeed, whichever young bhikkhu applies himself to the teaching of the Buddha, illuminates this world like the moon freed from a cloud.

874.

874.

disā hi (syā. ka., ma. ni. 2.352) “Disāpi me dhammakathaṃ suṇantu, disāpi me yuñjantu buddhasāsane;

Disāpi me te manuje bhajantu, ye dhammamevādapayanti santo.

“May my enemies listen to a talk on the Dhamma. May my enemies apply themselves to the teaching of the Buddha. May those enemies of mine associate with good people, those who cause others to accept the Dhamma.

875.

875.

“Disā hi me khantivādānaṃ, avirodhappasaṃsinaṃ;

Suṇantu dhammaṃ kālena, tañca anuvidhīyantu.

“Indeed, may my enemies, at a suitable time, listen to the Dhamma of those who speak on patience and praise non-opposition, and may they practice in accordance with it.

876.

876.

“Na hi jātu so mamaṃ hiṃse, aññaṃ vā pana kiñcanaṃ kañcinaṃ (sī. syā.), kañcanaṃ (?);

Pappuyya paramaṃ santiṃ, rakkheyya tasathāvare.

“For surely he would never harm me, nor any other being whatsoever. Having attained the supreme peace, he would protect both the trembling and the firm.

877.

877.

theragā. 19 “Udakañhi [P 0.0082] nayanti nettikā, usukārā namayanti damayanti (ka.) tejanaṃ;

Dāruṃ namayanti damayanti (ka.) tacchakā, attānaṃ damayanti paṇḍitā.

“Irrigators guide the water; fletchers straighten the arrow-shaft; carpenters shape the wood; the wise tame themselves.

878.

878.

“Daṇḍeneke [M 0.0335] damayanti, aṅkusebhi kasāhi ca;

Adaṇḍena asatthena, ahaṃ dantomhi tādinā.

“Some tame with a stick, with goads, and with whips; but I was tamed by the Such-a-One, who is without stick or weapon.

879.

879.

“‘Ahiṃsako’ti [T 0.0390] me nāmaṃ, hiṃsakassa pure sato;

Ajjāhaṃ saccanāmomhi, na naṃ hiṃsāmi kiñcanaṃ kañcinaṃ (sī. syā.), kañcanaṃ (?).

“My name is ‘Ahiṃsaka’ (Harmless), though formerly I was a ‘Hiṃsaka’ (Harmer). Today I am true to my name; I do not harm any being whatsoever.

880.

880.

“Coro ahaṃ pure āsiṃ, aṅgulimāloti vissuto;

Vuyhamāno mahoghena, buddhaṃ saraṇamāgamaṃ.

“Formerly, I was a robber renowned as Aṅgulimāla. Being swept along by the great flood, I went for refuge to the Buddha.

881.

881.

“Lohitapāṇi pure āsiṃ, aṅgulimāloti vissuto;

Saraṇagamanaṃ passa, bhavanetti samūhatā.

“Formerly, I was ‘Bloody-Handed,’ renowned as Aṅgulimāla. Behold my going for refuge! The guide to existence has been uprooted.

882.

882.

“Tādisaṃ kammaṃ katvāna, bahuṃ duggatigāminaṃ;

Phuṭṭho kammavipākena, anaṇo bhuñjāmi bhojanaṃ.

“Having done much kamma of a kind that leads to a woeful destination, though touched by the result of that kamma, I eat my food without debt.

883.

883.

“Pamādamanuyuñjanti, bālā dummedhino janā;

Appamādañca medhāvī, dhanaṃ seṭṭhaṃva rakkhati.

“Foolish, witless people indulge in heedlessness, but the wise person guards heedfulness as their best treasure.

884.

884.

“Mā pamādamanuyuñjetha, mā kāmaratisanthavaṃ sandhavaṃ (ka.);

Appamatto hi jhāyanto, pappoti paramaṃ sukhaṃ.

“Do not indulge in heedlessness; do not engage in intimacy with sensual delight. For the heedful one, meditating, attains supreme happiness.

885.

885.

“Svāgataṃ nāpagataṃ, netaṃ dummantitaṃ mama;

Savibhattesu dhammesu, yaṃ seṭṭhaṃ tadupāgamaṃ.

“A good coming, not a bad coming! This was not ill-counseled for me. Among the well-analyzed Dhammas, I have approached that which is the very best.

886.

886.

“Svāgataṃ nāpagataṃ, netaṃ dummantitaṃ mama;

Tisso vijjā anuppattā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ.

“A good coming, not a bad coming! This was not ill-counseled for me. The three knowledges have been attained; the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled.

887.

887.

“Araññe [V 0.0268] rukkhamūle vā, pabbatesu guhāsu vā;

Tattha tattheva aṭṭhāsiṃ, ubbiggamanaso tadā.

“In the forest or at the foot of a tree, in mountains or in caves—in just such places I stayed, with a terrified mind, at that time.

888.

888.

“Sukhaṃ sayāmi ṭhāyāmi, sukhaṃ kappemi jīvitaṃ;

Ahatthapāso mārassa, aho satthānukampito.

“Happily I sleep, happily I stand; happily I live my life. I am beyond the grasp of Māra. Oh, how I have been shown compassion by the Teacher!

889.

889.

“Brahmajacco [T 0.0391] pure āsiṃ, udicco ubhato ahu;

Sojja putto sugatassa, dhammarājassa satthuno.

“Formerly, I was of brahmin birth, of high lineage on both sides. Today, I am a son of the Sugata, the Teacher, the King of Dhamma.

890.

890.

“Vītataṇho anādāno, guttadvāro susaṃvuto;

Aghamūlaṃ vadhitvāna, patto me āsavakkhayo.

“Without craving, without grasping, with guarded doors and well-restrained, having destroyed the root of suffering, I have attained the destruction of the taints.

891.

891.

“Pariciṇṇo [M 0.0336] mayā satthā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ;

Ohito garuko bhāro, bhavanetti samūhatā”ti.

“The Teacher has been attended upon by me; the teaching of the Buddha has been fulfilled. The heavy burden has been laid down; the guide to existence has been uprooted.”

… Aṅgulimālo thero….

…The Elder Aṅgulimāla….

9. Anuruddhattheragāthā

9. The Verses of the Elder Anuruddha

892.

892.

“Pahāya [P 0.0083] mātāpitaro, bhaginī ñātibhātaro;

Pañca kāmaguṇe hitvā, anuruddhova jhāyatu.

“Having abandoned mother and father, sisters, kinsmen, and brothers; having given up the five strands of sensual pleasure, let Anuruddha meditate.

893.

893.

“Sameto naccagītehi, sammatāḷappabodhano;

Na tena suddhimajjhagaṃ suddhamajjhagā (sī. ka.), suddhimajjhagamā (syā.), mārassa visaye rato.

“Endowed with dance and song, and awakened by the sound of gongs and cymbals, I did not attain purity by that, delighting in the domain of Māra.

894.

894.

“Etañca samatikkamma, rato buddhassa sāsane;

Sabboghaṃ samatikkamma, anuruddhova jhāyati.

“Having transcended this, delighting in the Buddha’s teaching, having crossed over all the floods, Anuruddha meditates.

895.

895.

“Rūpā saddā rasā gandhā, phoṭṭhabbā ca manoramā;

Ete ca samatikkamma, anuruddhova jhāyati.

“Forms, sounds, tastes, smells, and delightful tangible objects—having overcome these as well, Anuruddha meditates.

896.

896.

“Piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto, eko adutiyo muni;

Esati paṃsukūlāni, anuruddho anāsavo.

“Returned from the alms round, the sage, alone, without a companion—Anuruddha, the one free from taints—seeks out dust-heap robes.

897.

897.

“Vicinī aggahī dhovi, rajayī dhārayī muni;

Paṃsukūlāni matimā, anuruddho anāsavo.

“The wise sage, Anuruddha, the one free from taints, selected, took, washed, dyed, and wore the dust-heap robes.

898.

898.

“Mahiccho [T 0.0392] ca asantuṭṭho, saṃsaṭṭho yo ca uddhato;

Tassa dhammā ime honti, pāpakā saṃkilesikā.

“For one who has great wishes and is discontented, who is sociable and restless, these evil, defiling states arise for him.

899.

899.

“Sato ca hoti appiccho, santuṭṭho avighātavā;

Pavivekarato vitto, niccamāraddhavīriyo.

“But one who is mindful and of few wishes, content and untroubled, delighting in seclusion, joyful, with energy ever aroused—

900.

900.

“Tassa [V 0.0269] dhammā ime honti, kusalā bodhipakkhikā;

Anāsavo ca so hoti, iti vuttaṃ mahesinā.

“For him these qualities are wholesome, aids to enlightenment; and he is free from taints—so it was said by the Great Sage.

901.

901.

“Mama saṅkappamaññāya, satthā loke anuttaro;

Manomayena kāyena, iddhiyā upasaṅkami.

“Knowing my intention, the Teacher, unsurpassed in the world, approached me by psychic power with a mind-made body.

902.

902.

“Yadā me ahu saṅkappo, tato uttari desayi;

Nippapañcarato buddho, nippapañcamadesayi.

“When that thought arose in me, he taught what is still higher. The Buddha, who delights in non-proliferation, taught about non-proliferation.

903.

903.

“Tassāhaṃ dhammamaññāya, vihāsiṃ sāsane rato;

Tisso vijjā anuppattā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ.

“Having understood his Dhamma, I dwelt delighting in the Dispensation. The three knowledges have been attained; the Buddha’s teaching has been fulfilled.

904.

904.

“Pañcapaññāsavassāni[M 0.0337], yato nesajjiko ahaṃ;

Pañcavīsativassāni, yato middhaṃ samūhataṃ.

“For fifty-five years I have maintained the sitter's practice; for twenty-five years drowsiness has been uprooted.”

905.

905.

dī. ni. 2.222 “Nāhu assāsapassāsā, ṭhitacittassa tādino;

Anejo santimārabbha, cakkhumā parinibbuto.

There were no in-breaths and out-breaths for the Suchlike One of steadfast mind. Unshaken, intent on peace, the One with Vision has attained final Nibbāna.

906.

906.

dī. ni. 2.222 “Asallīnena cittena, vedanaṃ ajjhavāsayi;

Pajjotasseva nibbānaṃ, vimokkho cetaso ahu.

With an unshrinking mind he endured the feeling. Like the extinguishing of a lamp was the liberation of his mind.

907.

907.

“Ete pacchimakā dāni, munino phassapañcamā;

Nāññe [T 0.0393] dhammā bhavissanti, sambuddhe parinibbute.

These now are the final states of the sage, with contact as the fifth. When the Perfectly Enlightened One has attained final Nibbāna, no other states will come to be.

908.

908.

“Natthi dāni punāvāso, devakāyasmi jālini;

Vikkhīṇo jātisaṃsāro, natthi dāni punabbhavo.

There is now no more dwelling, Jālinī, in the host of devas. The round of births is destroyed; there is now no more renewed existence.

909.

909.

“Yassa [P 0.0084] muhuttena sahassadhā, loko saṃvidito sabrahmakappo;

Vasī iddhiguṇe cutūpapāte, kāle passati devatā sa bhikkhu sabhikkhuno (sī. ka.).

He to whom the thousandfold world system, together with the Brahma realm, is known in a moment—that bhikkhu is a master of the qualities of psychic power and of passing away and rebirth; at the proper time, he sees the devas.

910.

910.

“Annabhāro annahāro (sī.) pure āsiṃ, daliddo ghāsahārako;

Samaṇaṃ paṭipādesiṃ, upariṭṭhaṃ yasassinaṃ.

In a past life, I was Annabhāra, a poor grass-carrier. I made an offering to a recluse, the famous Uparittha.

911.

911.

“Somhi sakyakule jāto, anuruddhoti maṃ vidū;

Upeto naccagītehi, sammatāḷappabodhano.

I was born in the Sakyan clan; they know me as Anuruddha. I was endowed with dance and song, awakened by the sound of gongs and cymbals.

912.

912.

“Athaddasāsiṃ sambuddhaṃ, satthāraṃ akutobhayaṃ;

Tasmiṃ cittaṃ pasādetvā, pabbajiṃ anagāriyaṃ.

Then I saw the Perfectly Enlightened One, the Teacher who is fearless from any quarter. Having gained confidence in him, I went forth into the homeless life.

913.

913.

“Pubbenivāsaṃ jānāmi, yattha me vusitaṃ pure;

Tāvatiṃsesu devesu, aṭṭhāsiṃ sakkajātiyā satajātiyā (sī.).

I know my former abodes, where I have lived in the past. I dwelt among the Tāvatiṃsa devas, having been born as Sakka.

914.

914.

“Sattakkhattuṃ [V 0.0270] manussindo, ahaṃ rajjamakārayiṃ;

Cāturanto vijitāvī, jambusaṇḍassa issaro;

Adaṇḍena asatthena, dhammena anusāsayiṃ.

Seven times I was a king of humans and exercised sovereignty, a conqueror of the four quarters, lord of Jambudīpa. Without rod or sword, I governed righteously.

915.

915.

“Ito satta tato satta, saṃsārāni catuddasa;

Nivāsamabhijānissaṃ, devaloke ṭhitā tadā.

Seven lives here and seven there—fourteen transmigrations in all; I came to know my past abodes when I was established then in the deva world.

916.

916.

“Pañcaṅgike [T 0.0394][M 0.0338] samādhimhi, sante ekodibhāvite;

Paṭippassaddhiladdhamhi, dibbacakkhu visujjhi me.

In the five-factored concentration—peaceful, unified, and developed, where tranquility had been gained—my divine eye was purified.

917.

917.

“Cutūpapātaṃ jānāmi, sattānaṃ āgatiṃ gatiṃ;

Itthabhāvaññathābhāvaṃ, jhāne pañcaṅgike ṭhito.

Established in the five-factored jhāna, I know the passing away and rebirth of beings, their coming and going, and their state of being thus or otherwise.

918.

918.

“Pariciṇṇo mayā satthā…pe… bhavanetti samūhatā.

The Teacher has been served by me… the conduit to existence is uprooted.

919.

919.

“Vajjīnaṃ veḷuvagāme, ahaṃ jīvitasaṅkhayā;

Heṭṭhato veḷugumbasmiṃ, nibbāyissaṃ anāsavo”ti.

In Veḷugāma of the Vajjis, when my life span is exhausted, I, the one free from taints, will attain final Nibbāna beneath a bamboo thicket.

… Anuruddho thero….

… The Elder Anuruddha …

10. Pārāpariyattheragāthā

10. The Verses of the Elder Pārāpariya

920.

920.

Samaṇassa ahu cintā, pupphitamhi mahāvane;

Ekaggassa nisinnassa, pavivittassa jhāyino.

A thought occurred to the recluse as he sat meditating in seclusion in the great flowering forest, his mind unified.

921.

921.

“Aññathā lokanāthamhi, tiṭṭhante purisuttame;

Iriyaṃ āsi bhikkhūnaṃ, aññathā dāni dissati.

The deportment of the bhikkhus was one way when the protector of the world, the supreme person, was present; but now it is seen to be another way.

922.

922.

“Sītavātaparittānaṃ, hirikopīnachādanaṃ;

Mattaṭṭhiyaṃ abhuñjiṃsu, santuṭṭhā itarītare.

Content with whatever they received, they used their robes only for what was necessary: for protection from cold and wind, and for covering their private parts.

923.

923.

“Paṇītaṃ yadi vā lūkhaṃ, appaṃ vā yadi vā bahuṃ;

Yāpanatthaṃ abhuñjiṃsu, agiddhā nādhimucchitā.

Whether it was exquisite or coarse, little or much, they ate for the sake of sustenance, not greedy, not infatuated.

924.

924.

“Jīvitānaṃ [P 0.0085] parikkhāre, bhesajje atha paccaye;

Na bāḷhaṃ ussukā āsuṃ, yathā te āsavakkhaye.

Regarding life's requisites, medicines, and other supports, they were not as eager as they were for the destruction of the taints.

925.

925.

“Araññe rukkhamūlesu, kandarāsu guhāsu ca;

Vivekamanubrūhantā, vihaṃsu tapparāyanā.

In the forest, at the foot of trees, in mountain clefts and caves, they dwelt developing seclusion, with that as their final goal.

926.

926.

“Nīcā [T 0.0395] niviṭṭhā subharā, mudū atthaddhamānasā;

Abyāsekā amukharā, atthacintā vasānugā.

Humble, steadfast, easy to support, gentle, with minds not obstinate; unentangled, not harsh of speech, intent on the goal, masters of themselves.

927.

927.

“Tato [V 0.0271] pāsādikaṃ āsi, gataṃ bhuttaṃ nisevitaṃ;

Siniddhā teladhārāva, ahosi iriyāpatho.

Therefore their walking, eating, and their general conduct was inspiring; their deportment was like a smooth stream of oil.

928.

928.

“Sabbāsavaparikkhīṇā, mahājhāyī mahāhitā;

Nibbutā dāni te therā, parittā dāni tādisā.

Those elders with all taints destroyed, great meditators of great benefit, are now quenched; few such ones exist now.

929.

929.

“Kusalānañca [M 0.0339] dhammānaṃ, paññāya ca parikkhayā;

Sabbākāravarūpetaṃ, lujjate jinasāsanaṃ.

Through the destruction of wholesome qualities and of wisdom, the Victor’s teaching, endowed with all the best features, falls to ruin.

930.

930.

“Pāpakānañca dhammānaṃ, kilesānañca yo utu;

Upaṭṭhitā vivekāya, ye ca saddhammasesakā.

This is the season for evil states and defilements. And those who are committed to seclusion are the remnants of the true Dhamma.

931.

931.

“Te kilesā pavaḍḍhantā, āvisanti bahuṃ janaṃ;

Kīḷanti maññe bālehi, ummattehiva rakkhasā.

Those defilements, growing, enter into many people; I think they play with fools like demons with the mad.

932.

932.

“Kilesehābhibhūtā te, tena tena vidhāvitā;

Narā kilesavatthūsu, sasaṅgāmeva ghosite.

Overcome by defilements, people run about here and there among the bases for defilement, as if in a declared battle.

933.

933.

“Pariccajitvā saddhammaṃ, aññamaññehi bhaṇḍare;

Diṭṭhigatāni anventā, idaṃ seyyoti maññare.

Having abandoned the true Dhamma, they quarrel with one another; following their own views, they think, “This is better!”

934.

934.

“Dhanañca puttaṃ bhariyañca, chaḍḍayitvāna niggatā;

Kaṭacchubhikkhahetūpi, akicchāni nisevare.

Having gone forth, leaving behind wealth, sons, and wife, they engage in improper actions even for a spoonful of alms.

935.

935.

“Udarāvadehakaṃ bhutvā, sayantuttānaseyyakā;

Kathaṃ vattenti kathā vaḍḍhenti (sī. ka.) paṭibuddhā, yā kathā satthugarahitā.

Having eaten their belly’s fill, they lie down, sleeping on their backs; when awakened, they engage in talk censured by the Teacher.

936.

936.

“Sabbakārukasippāni[T 0.0396], cittiṃ katvāna cittīkatvāna (sī.), cittaṃ katvāna (syā.) sikkhare;

Avūpasantā ajjhattaṃ, sāmaññatthoti acchati tiriñcati (?).

Having diligently learned all kinds of crafts and skills, but not being inwardly pacified, they dwell thinking, 'This is the goal of recluseship!'

937.

937.

“Mattikaṃ telacuṇṇañca, udakāsanabhojanaṃ;

Gihīnaṃ upanāmenti, ākaṅkhantā bahuttaraṃ.

They offer earthenware, oil and powder, water, seats, and food to householders, hoping for much more in return.

938.

938.

“Dantaponaṃ kapitthañca, pupphaṃ khādaniyāni ca;

Piṇḍapāte ca sampanne, ambe āmalakāni ca.

They offer tooth-cleaners and wood-apples, flowers and various edibles, excellent alms-food, mangoes, and myrobalans.

939.

939.

“Bhesajjesu yathā vejjā, kiccākicce yathā gihī;

Gaṇikāva vibhūsāyaṃ, issare khattiyā yathā.

They are like doctors with their medicines, like householders with their duties; like a courtesan with her finery, like nobles who are rulers.

940.

940.

“Nekatikā [P 0.0086] vañcanikā, kūṭasakkhī apāṭukā;

Bahūhi parikappehi, āmisaṃ paribhuñjare.

Deceitful, fraudulent, giving false evidence, crooked; with many schemes, they enjoy material things.

941.

941.

“Lesakappe pariyāye, parikappenudhāvitā;

Jīvikatthā upāyena, saṅkaḍḍhanti bahuṃ dhanaṃ.

By means of pretexts and excuses, they run after their schemes; for the sake of a living, they scrape together much wealth by some device.

942.

942.

“Upaṭṭhāpenti [M 0.0340][V 0.0272] parisaṃ, kammato no ca dhammato;

Dhammaṃ paresaṃ desenti, lābhato no ca atthato.

They gather a following through their activities, not through the Dhamma; they teach the Dhamma to others for gain, not for the true goal.

943.

943.

“Saṅghalābhassa bhaṇḍanti, saṅghato paribāhirā;

Paralābhopajīvantā, ahirīkā na lajjare.

Being external to the Saṅgha, they quarrel over the Saṅgha's gains; living on the gains of others, they are without conscience and feel no shame.

944.

944.

“Nānuyuttā tathā eke, muṇḍā saṅghāṭipārutā;

Sambhāvanaṃyevicchanti, lābhasakkāramucchitā.

Though shaven-headed and clad in the outer robe, some are not truly devoted. Infatuated with gain and honor, they desire only to be esteemed.

945.

945.

“Evaṃ nānappayātamhi, na dāni sukaraṃ tathā;

Aphusitaṃ [T 0.0397] vā phusituṃ, phusitaṃ vānurakkhituṃ.

When things have gone in these various ways, it is no longer easy to attain the unattained or to protect what has been attained.

946.

946.

“Yathā kaṇṭakaṭṭhānamhi, careyya anupāhano;

Satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvāna, evaṃ gāme munī care.

Just as one without shoes would walk carefully on thorny ground, so, having established mindfulness, a sage should walk in the village.

947.

947.

“Saritvā pubbake yogī, tesaṃ vattamanussaraṃ;

Kiñcāpi pacchimo kālo, phuseyya amataṃ padaṃ.

Remembering the ancient yogis and recollecting their conduct, even though this is the final age, one may yet touch the deathless state.

948.

948.

“Idaṃ vatvā sālavane, samaṇo bhāvitindriyo;

Brāhmaṇo parinibbāyī, isi khīṇapunabbhavo”ti.

Having said this in the sāl-tree grove, the recluse with developed faculties, the brahmin, the seer whose renewed existence is destroyed, attained final Nibbāna.

… Pārāpariyo pārāsariyo (syā.) thero….

… The Elder Pārāpariya …

Vīsatinipāto niṭṭhito.

The Chapter of the Twenties is concluded.

Tatruddānaṃ –

The summary:

Adhimutto pārāpariyo, telakāni raṭṭhapālo;

Mālukyaselo bhaddiyo, aṅguli dibbacakkhuko.

Adhimutta, Pārāpariya, Telakāni, and Raṭṭhapāla; Mālukyaputta, Sela, Bhaddiya, Aṅgulimāla, and the one with the Divine Eye.

Pārāpariyo dasete, vīsamhi parikittitā;

Gāthāyo dve satā honti, pañcatālīsa 244 gāthāyoyeva dissanti uttarinti.

These ten elders are proclaimed in the Chapter of Twenty. The verses number two hundred and forty-five.

17. Tiṃsanipāto

17. The Book of the Thirties

1. Phussattheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Phussa

949.

949.

Pāsādike [M 0.0341][V 0.0273][P 0.0087] bahū disvā, bhāvitatte susaṃvute;

Isi paṇḍarasagotto paṇḍarassa gotto (sī.), apucchi phussasavhayaṃ.

Seeing many inspiring bhikkhus, with developed selves and well-restrained, the sage of the Paṇḍarasa clan asked the one named Phussa:

950.

950.

“Kiṃchandā [T 0.0398] kimadhippāyā, kimākappā bhavissare;

Anāgatamhi kālamhi, taṃ me akkhāhi pucchito”.

“Of what inclination, of what intention, of what conduct will they be in the future time? Having been asked, declare this to me.”

951.

951.

“Suṇohi vacanaṃ mayhaṃ, isipaṇḍarasavhaya;

Sakkaccaṃ upadhārehi, ācikkhissāmyanāgataṃ.

“Listen to my word, O sage named Paṇḍarasa; attend carefully. I will declare what will be in the future.

952.

952.

“Kodhanā upanāhī ca, makkhī thambhī saṭhā bahū;

Ussukī nānāvādā ca, bhavissanti anāgate.

“In the future many will be wrathful and hostile, contemptuous, stubborn, and deceitful; they will be envious and will hold diverse views.

953.

953.

“Aññātamānino dhamme, gambhīre tīragocarā;

Lahukā agaru dhamme, aññamaññamagāravā.

“Conceited about their knowledge of the profound Dhamma, they will only frequent its shore. Frivolous, with no respect for the Dhamma, they will be disrespectful toward one another.

954.

954.

“Bahū ādīnavā loke, uppajjissantyanāgate;

Sudesitaṃ imaṃ dhammaṃ, kilesessanti kilesissanti (sī.), kilisissanti (syā. ka.) dummatī.

“Many dangers will arise in the world in the future. The foolish ones will defile this well-expounded Dhamma.

955.

955.

“Guṇahīnāpi saṅghamhi, voharantā visāradā;

Balavanto bhavissanti, mukharā assutāvino.

“Though lacking in virtue, they will be bold in speech within the Saṅgha and will become powerful—loud-mouthed and unlearned.

956.

956.

“Guṇavantopi saṅghamhi, voharantā yathātthato;

Dubbalā te bhavissanti, hirīmanā anatthikā.

“But the virtuous in the Saṅgha, who speak according to the truth, will become weak—they will be conscientious and unassertive.

957.

957.

“Rajataṃ jātarūpañca, khettaṃ vatthumajeḷakaṃ;

Dāsidāsañca dummedhā, sādiyissantyanāgate.

“In the future the foolish will accept silver and gold, fields and property, goats and sheep, and male and female slaves.

958.

958.

“Ujjhānasaññino bālā, sīlesu asamāhitā;

Unnaḷā vicarissanti, kalahābhiratā magā.

“The fools will be disposed to finding fault, uncomposed in their virtue. Arrogant and delighting in quarrels, they will wander about like wild beasts.

959.

959.

“Uddhatā ca bhavissanti, nīlacīvarapārutā;

Kuhā [T 0.0399] thaddhā lapā siṅgī, carissantyariyā viya.

“They will be restless, clad in dark blue robes. Deceitful, stubborn, talkative, and haughty, they will wander about as if they were noble ones.

960.

960.

“Telasaṇṭhehi kesehi, capalā añjanakkhikā;

Rathiyāya gamissanti, dantavaṇṇikapārutā.

“With hair smoothed by oil, fickle, with eyes painted with eyeliner, they will walk the streets clad in ivory-colored robes.

961.

961.

“Ajegucchaṃ [M 0.0342][V 0.0274] vimuttehi, surattaṃ arahaddhajaṃ;

Jigucchissanti kāsāvaṃ, odātesu samucchitā odāte susamucchitā (sī.).

“They will be disgusted by the ochre robe—the well-dyed banner of the arahants, which is not despised by the liberated—and they will be infatuated with white robes.

962.

962.

“Lābhakāmā bhavissanti, kusītā hīnavīriyā;

Kicchantā vanapatthāni, gāmantesu vasissare.

“Desirous of gain, they will be lazy and lacking in energy. Finding the forest wildernesses wearisome, they will dwell on the outskirts of villages.

963.

963.

“Ye [P 0.0088] ye lābhaṃ labhissanti, micchājīvaratā sadā;

Te teva anusikkhantā, bhajissanti asaṃyatā.

“The unrestrained will imitate and associate with those who get gain, who are always delighting in wrong livelihood.

964.

964.

“Ye ye alābhino lābhaṃ, na te pujjā bhavissare;

Supesalepi te dhīre, sevissanti na te tadā.

“Those who do not receive gain will not be revered. People then will not attend upon those wise and amiable ones.

965.

965.

“Milakkhurajanaṃ rattaṃ pilakkharajanaṃ rattaṃ (?), garahantā sakaṃ dhajaṃ;

Titthiyānaṃ dhajaṃ keci, dhārissantyavadātakaṃ.

“Reproaching their own banner, dyed with an improper dye, some will wear the white banner of the sectarians.

966.

966.

“Agāravo ca kāsāve, tadā tesaṃ bhavissati;

Paṭisaṅkhā ca kāsāve, bhikkhūnaṃ na bhavissati.

“Then they will have disrespect for the ochre robe, and the bhikkhus will have no proper reflection concerning it.

967.

967.

“Abhibhūtassa dukkhena, sallaviddhassa ruppato;

Paṭisaṅkhā mahāghorā, nāgassāsi acintiyā.

“For the elephant, overcome by suffering, pierced by a dart and afflicted with pain, the reflection that arose was terrible and inconceivable.

968.

968.

“Chaddanto hi tadā disvā, surattaṃ arahaddhajaṃ;

Tāvadeva bhaṇī gāthā, gajo atthopasaṃhitā”.

“For then the elephant Chaddanta, seeing the well-dyed banner of the arahants, immediately spoke these verses fraught with meaning:

969.

969.

dha. pa. 9; jā. 1.2.141; 1.16.122 “Anikkasāvo [T 0.0400] kāsāvaṃ, yo vatthaṃ paridhassati paridahissati (sī. syā.);

Apeto damasaccena, na so kāsāvamarahati.

“He who would wear the ochre robe while not free from stains, devoid of self-control and truth, is not worthy of the ochre robe.

970.

970.

“Yo ca vantakāsāvassa, sīlesu susamāhito;

Upeto damasaccena, sa ve kāsāvamarahati.

“But he who has purged his stains, is well established in the virtues, and is endowed with self-control and truth, he is truly worthy of the ochre robe.”

971.

971.

“Vipannasīlo dummedho, pākaṭo kāmakāriyo;

Vibbhantacitto nissukko, na so kāsāvamarahati.

“One of broken virtue, foolish, notorious for acting on his desires, with a confused mind and lacking purity—he is not worthy of the ochre robe.

972.

972.

“Yo ca sīlena sampanno, vītarāgo samāhito;

Odātamanasaṅkappo, sa ve kāsāvamarahati.

“But that person who is accomplished in virtue, free from passion, and composed, with an exceedingly pure mind and intention—he, indeed, is worthy of the ochre robe.

973.

973.

“Uddhato unnaḷo bālo, sīlaṃ yassa na vijjati;

Odātakaṃ arahati, kāsāvaṃ kiṃ karissati.

“For the agitated, arrogant fool in whom virtue is not found, what can the ochre robe accomplish? He is worthy of the white cloth.

974.

974.

“Bhikkhū [M 0.0343] ca bhikkhuniyo ca, duṭṭhacittā anādarā;

Tādīnaṃ mettacittānaṃ, niggaṇhissantyanāgate.

“In the future, monks and nuns with corrupt minds and no respect will persecute those of such a kind who possess minds of loving-kindness.

975.

975.

“Sikkhāpentāpi therehi, bālā cīvaradhāraṇaṃ;

Na suṇissanti dummedhā, pākaṭā kāmakāriyā.

“Though instructed by the elders in the wearing of the robe, the foolish ones of dull intellect will not listen—they who are notorious and act according to their desires.

976.

976.

“Te [V 0.0275] tathā sikkhitā bālā, aññamaññaṃ agāravā;

Nādiyissantupajjhāye, khaḷuṅko viya sārathiṃ.

Those fools, though instructed, being disrespectful toward one another, will not heed their preceptors, just as a rogue horse does not heed its trainer.

977.

977.

“Evaṃ anāgataddhānaṃ, paṭipatti bhavissati;

Bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnañca, patte kālamhi pacchime.

Thus, in the time to come, when the final age has arrived, such will be the corrupt practice of the monks and nuns.

978.

978.

“Purā āgacchate etaṃ, anāgataṃ mahabbhayaṃ;

Subbacā hotha sakhilā, aññamaññaṃ sagāravā.

Before this great future danger arrives, be easy to admonish, be amiable, and be respectful toward one another.

979.

979.

“Mettacittā [T 0.0401] kāruṇikā, hotha sīlesu saṃvutā;

Āraddhavīriyā pahitattā, niccaṃ daḷhaparakkamā.

Have minds of loving-kindness, be compassionate, and be restrained in the virtues. Be aroused in energy, resolute, and always firm in your striving.

980.

980.

“Pamādaṃ [P 0.0089] bhayato disvā, appamādañca khemato;

Bhāvethaṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ, phusantā amataṃ pada”nti.

Seeing negligence as a danger and diligence as security, develop the Eightfold Path, thereby realizing the deathless state.

… Phusso thero….

… The Elder Phussa …

2. Sāriputtattheragāthā

2. The Verses of the Elder Sāriputta

981.

981.

“Yathācārī yathāsato satīmā, yatasaṅkappajjhāyi appamatto;

Ajjhattarato samāhitatto, eko santusito tamāhu bhikkhuṃ.

One who comports himself accordingly, who is mindful as he should be, with restrained intentions, meditative, and diligent; who delights inwardly, with a concentrated mind, solitary and content—him they call a bhikkhu.

982.

982.

“Allaṃ sukkhaṃ vā bhuñjanto, na bāḷhaṃ suhito siyā;

Ūnūdaro mitāhāro, sato bhikkhu paribbaje.

Whether eating moist or dry food, one should not be excessively full. With a less-than-full stomach, moderate in food, a mindful bhikkhu should wander.

983.

983.

“Cattāro pañca ālope, abhutvā udakaṃ pive;

Alaṃ phāsuvihārāya, pahitattassa bhikkhuno.

Leaving four or five mouthfuls uneaten, one should drink water. This is sufficient for the comfortable abiding of a resolute bhikkhu.

984.

984.

“Kappiyaṃ taṃ ce chādeti, cīvaraṃ idamatthikaṃ idamatthitaṃ (sī.);

Alaṃ phāsuvihārāya, pahitattassa bhikkhuno.

If an allowable robe provides covering for its intended purpose, this is sufficient for the comfortable abiding of a resolute bhikkhu.

985.

985.

“Pallaṅkena [M 0.0344] nisinnassa, jaṇṇuke nābhivassati;

Alaṃ phāsuvihārāya, pahitattassa bhikkhuno.

When sitting cross-legged, if the rain does not wet one's knees, this is sufficient for the comfortable abiding of a resolute bhikkhu.

986.

986.

saṃ. ni. 4.253; itivu. 53 “Yo sukhaṃ dukkhato adda, dukkhamaddakkhi sallato;

Ubhayantarena [T 0.0402] ubhayamantare (sī.) nāhosi, kena lokasmi kiṃ siyā.

One who has seen pleasure as suffering and has seen suffering as a dart, and does not exist between the two—by what in the world could he be bound?

987.

987.

“Mā me kadāci pāpiccho, kusīto hīnavīriyo;

Appassuto anādaro, kena lokasmi kiṃ siyā.

May one with evil wishes, who is lazy, of inferior energy, unlearned, and disrespectful, never be with me. For such a person in the world, what could be accomplished by what means?

988.

988.

“Bahussuto [V 0.0276] ca medhāvī, sīlesu susamāhito;

Cetosamathamanuyutto, api muddhani tiṭṭhatu.

One who is very learned and wise, well-established in the virtues, and devoted to the calming of the mind—may he stand even upon my head.

989.

989.

“Yo papañcamanuyutto, papañcābhirato mago;

Virādhayī so nibbānaṃ, yogakkhemaṃ anuttaraṃ.

One who is given to proliferation, a deer delighting in proliferation, fails to attain Nibbāna, the unsurpassed security from the yokes.

990.

990.

“Yo ca papañcaṃ hitvāna, nippapañcapathe rato;

Ārādhayī so nibbānaṃ, yogakkhemaṃ anuttaraṃ.

But one who, having abandoned proliferation, delights in the path free from proliferation, he attains Nibbāna, the unsurpassed security from the yokes.

991.

991.

dha. pa. 98 “Gāme vā yadi vāraññe, ninne vā yadi vā thale;

Yattha arahanto viharanti, taṃ bhūmirāmaṇeyyakaṃ.

Whether in a village or in the forest, in a low-lying place or on high ground, wherever the Arahants dwell, that place is delightful.

992.

992.

“Ramaṇīyāni araññāni, yattha na ramatī jano;

Vītarāgā ramissanti, na te kāmagavesino.

Delightful are the forests where worldly people find no delight. There the passion-free will delight, for they are not seekers of sensual pleasures.

993.

993.

dha. pa. 76 “Nidhīnaṃva pavattāraṃ, yaṃ passe vajjadassinaṃ;

Niggayhavādiṃ [P 0.0090] medhāviṃ, tādisaṃ paṇḍitaṃ bhaje;

Tādisaṃ bhajamānassa, seyyo hoti na pāpiyo.

Should one see a wise person who points out faults and speaks reprovingly, like one who reveals a hidden treasure, one should associate with such a sage. For one who associates with such a person, it is better, not worse.

994.

994.

dha. pa. 77 “Ovadeyyānusāseyya, asabbhā ca nivāraye;

Satañhi so piyo hoti, asataṃ hoti appiyo.

Let him advise, let him instruct, and restrain one from what is improper. Indeed, he is dear to the good, but to the bad he is undear.

995.

995.

“Aññassa bhagavā buddho, dhammaṃ desesi cakkhumā;

Dhamme [T 0.0403] desiyamānamhi, sotamodhesimatthiko;

Taṃ me amoghaṃ savanaṃ, vimuttomhi anāsavo.

The Blessed One, the Buddha, the One with the Eye, taught the Dhamma to another. While the Dhamma was being taught, I, being desirous, inclined my ear. That listening was not in vain for me: I am liberated and free from the cankers.

996.

996.

“Neva pubbenivāsāya, napi dibbassa cakkhuno;

Cetopariyāya iddhiyā, cutiyā upapattiyā;

Sotadhātuvisuddhiyā, paṇidhī me na vijjati kathā. 378.

Not for the recollection of past lives, nor for the divine eye, nor for the psychic power of knowing the minds of others, nor for knowing the passing away and rebirth of beings, nor for the purified divine ear element—is any aspiration found in me.

997.

997.

“Rukkhamūlaṃva [M 0.0345] nissāya, muṇḍo saṅghāṭipāruto;

Paññāya uttamo thero, upatissova upatisso ca (sī. ka.) jhāyati.

Relying on the root of a tree, shaven-headed, clad in his outer robe, the Elder Upatissa, supreme in wisdom, enters jhāna.

998.

998.

“Avitakkaṃ samāpanno, sammāsambuddhasāvako;

Ariyena tuṇhībhāvena, upeto hoti tāvade.

Having entered the attainment free from initial thought, the disciple of the Perfectly Enlightened One is, at that moment, endowed with noble silence.

999.

999.

udā. 24 “Yathāpi pabbato selo, acalo suppatiṭṭhito;

Evaṃ mohakkhayā bhikkhu, pabbatova na vedhati.

Just as a rocky mountain is unmoving and well-established, so, through the destruction of delusion, a bhikkhu, like a mountain, does not tremble.

1000.

1000.

“Anaṅgaṇassa posassa, niccaṃ sucigavesino;

Vālaggamattaṃ pāpassa, abbhamattaṃva khāyati.

To a person without blemish, who is ever seeking purity, an evil deed the size of a hair-tip appears as large as a cloud.

1001.

1001.

“Nābhinandāmi [V 0.0277] maraṇaṃ, nābhinandāmi jīvitaṃ;

Nikkhipissaṃ imaṃ kāyaṃ, sampajāno patissato.

I do not delight in death, I do not delight in life. I will lay aside this body, mindful and clearly comprehending.

1002.

1002.

“Nābhinandāmi maraṇaṃ, nābhinandāmi jīvitaṃ;

Kālañca paṭikaṅkhāmi, nibbisaṃ bhatako yathā.

I do not delight in death, I do not delight in life; but I await the time, like a servant waiting for his wages.

1003.

1003.

“Ubhayena midaṃ maraṇameva, nāmaraṇaṃ pacchā vā pure vā;

Paṭipajjatha mā vinassatha, khaṇo vo mā upaccagā.

Death comes in any case, there is no non-dying, whether later or before. Strive on, lest you perish; do not let the moment pass you by.

1004.

1004.

“Nagaraṃ yathā paccantaṃ, guttaṃ santarabāhiraṃ;

Evaṃ gopetha attānaṃ, khaṇo vo mā upaccagā;

Khaṇātītā [T 0.0404] hi socanti, nirayamhi samappitā.

Just as a frontier city is guarded within and without, so you should guard yourselves. Do not let this moment pass you by, for those who miss the moment grieve when they are consigned to hell.

1005.

1005.

“Upasanto uparato, mantabhāṇī mattabhāṇī (sī.) anuddhato;

Dhunāti pāpake dhamme, dumapattaṃva māluto.

Calm and withdrawn, speaking thoughtfully, not agitated, one shakes off evil states as the wind shakes a leaf from a tree.

1006.

1006.

“Upasanto uparato, mantabhāṇī anuddhato;

Appāsi abbahi (syā.), abhāsi (?) pāpake dhamme, dumapattaṃva māluto.

Calm and withdrawn, speaking thoughtfully, not agitated, one has shed evil states as the wind sheds a leaf from a tree.

1007.

1007.

“Upasanto [P 0.0091] anāyāso, vippasanno anāvilo;

Kalyāṇasīlo medhāvī, dukkhassantakaro siyā.

Calm and untroubled, serene and clear, virtuous and wise—such a one would make an end of suffering.

1008.

1008.

“Na vissase ekatiyesu evaṃ, agārisu pabbajitesu cāpi;

Sādhūpi hutvā na asādhu honti, asādhu hutvā puna sādhu honti.

One should not place trust in some people, whether householders or renunciants. For those who were good become bad, and those who were bad can again become good.

1009.

1009.

“Kāmacchando [M 0.0346] ca byāpādo, thinamiddhañca bhikkhuno;

Uddhaccaṃ vicikicchā ca, pañcete cittakelisā.

Sensual desire and ill will, sloth and torpor, restlessness and doubt—these five are the mental defilements of a bhikkhu.

1010.

1010.

“Yassa sakkariyamānassa, asakkārena cūbhayaṃ;

Samādhi na vikampati, appamādavihārino.

For one dwelling in diligence, concentration does not waver whether one is being honored or dishonored.

1011.

1011.

“Taṃ jhāyinaṃ sātatikaṃ, sukhumadiṭṭhivipassakaṃ;

Upādānakkhayārāmaṃ, āhu sappuriso iti.

That persevering meditator who sees with subtle insight, one who delights in the destruction of clinging—him they call a superior person.

1012.

1012.

“Mahāsamuddo pathavī, pabbato anilopi ca;

Upamāya na yujjanti, satthu varavimuttiyā.

The great ocean, the earth, a mountain, and the wind—none of these is fit for a simile with the Teacher’s supreme liberation.

1013.

1013.

“Cakkānuvattako [T 0.0405] thero, mahāñāṇī samāhito;

Pathavāpaggisamāno, na rajjati na dussati.

The elder who keeps the Wheel rolling, of great wisdom and composed; like earth, water, and fire, he is neither impassioned nor repelled.

1014.

1014.

“Paññāpāramitaṃ patto, mahābuddhi mahāmati;

Ajaḷo jaḷasamāno, sadā carati nibbuto.

Having reached the perfection of wisdom, of great intelligence and great understanding; though not dull, he appears as if dull, and ever fares along, quenched.

1015.

1015.

“Pariciṇṇo mayā satthā…pe… bhavanetti samūhatā.

The Teacher has been served by me… the guide to existence has been uprooted.

1016.

1016.

“Sampādethappamādena[V 0.0278], esā me anusāsanī;

Handāhaṃ parinibbissaṃ, vippamuttomhi sabbadhī”ti.

Strive on with heedfulness—this is my instruction. Come now, I will attain final Nibbāna; I am completely liberated in every way.

… Sāriputto thero….

Thus the Elder Sāriputta spoke these verses.

3. Ānandattheragāthā

3. The Verses of the Elder Ānanda

1017.

1017.

“Pisuṇena ca kodhanena ca, maccharinā ca vibhūtanandinā;

Sakhitaṃ na kareyya paṇḍito, pāpo kāpurisena saṅgamo.

A wise person should not form a friendship with a slanderer, an angry person, a miser, or one who delights in another's ruin; for association with a bad person is evil.

1018.

1018.

“Saddhena ca pesalena ca, paññavatā bahussutena ca;

Sakhitaṃ kareyya paṇḍito, bhaddo sappurisena saṅgamo.

A wise person should form a friendship with one who is faithful, virtuous, wise, and learned; for association with a good person is a blessing.

1019.

1019.

“Passa cittakataṃ bimbaṃ…pe… yassa natthi dhuvaṃ ṭhiti.

Behold this decorated image… for which there is no lasting stability.

1020.

1020.

“Passa cittakataṃ bimbaṃ…pe… vatthehi sobhati.

Behold this decorated image… it is beautiful only with its garments.

1021.

1021.

“Alattakakatā [M 0.0347] …pe… no ca pāragavesino.

With feet dyed with lac… this is enough to delude a fool, but not one who seeks the further shore.

1022.

1022.

“Aṭṭhapadakatā…pe… no ca pāragavesino.

With hair styled in eight plaits… this is enough to delude a fool, but not one who seeks the further shore.

1023.

1023.

“Añjanīva navā…pe… no ca pāragavesino.

Like a new collyrium pot… this is enough to delude a fool, but not one who seeks the further shore.

1024.

1024.

“Bahussuto cittakathī, buddhassa paricārako;

Pannabhāro visaññutto, seyyaṃ kappeti gotamo.

Learned and an eloquent speaker, the attendant of the Buddha, with burden laid down and detached—Gotama lies down to rest.

1025.

1025.

“Khīṇāsavo visaññutto, saṅgātīto sunibbuto;

Dhāreti antimaṃ dehaṃ, jātimaraṇapāragū.

With taints destroyed, detached, having gone beyond attachments, fully quenched, he bears his final body, one who has crossed beyond birth and death.

1026.

1026.

“Yasmiṃ [P 0.0092] patiṭṭhitā dhammā, buddhassādiccabandhuno;

Nibbānagamane magge, soyaṃ tiṭṭhati gotamo.

He in whom the teachings of the Buddha, kinsman of the sun, are established on the path leading to Nibbāna—that Gotama stands firm.

1027.

1027.

“Dvāsīti [T 0.0406] buddhato gaṇhiṃ, dve sahassāni bhikkhuto;

Caturāsītisahassāni, ye me dhammā pavattino.

Eighty-two thousand I learned from the Buddha, two thousand from the bhikkhus; these eighty-four thousand teachings are current for me.

1028.

1028.

“Appassutāyaṃ puriso, balibaddova jīrati;

Maṃsāni tassa vaḍḍhanti, paññā tassa na vaḍḍhati.

This person of little learning ages like an ox: his flesh increases, but his wisdom does not grow.

1029.

1029.

“Bahussuto appassutaṃ, yo sutenātimaññati;

Andho padīpadhārova, tatheva paṭibhāti maṃ.

The learned one who despises another of little learning on account of his own learning seems to me just like a blind man holding a lamp.

1030.

1030.

“Bahussutaṃ upāseyya, sutañca na vināsaye;

Taṃ mūlaṃ brahmacariyassa, tasmā dhammadharo siyā.

One should associate with a learned person and not let one's learning be lost. This is the root of the holy life; therefore one should be a bearer of the Dhamma.

1031.

1031.

“Pubbāparaññū atthaññū, niruttipadakovido;

Suggahītañca gaṇhāti, atthañcopaparikkhati.
