Knowing what comes before and after, knowing the meaning, skilled in language and its phrasing, one grasps it well and investigates the meaning.

1032.

1032.

“Khantyā [V 0.0279] chandikato khantiyā chandito (?) hoti, ussahitvā tuleti taṃ;

Samaye so padahati, ajjhattaṃ susamāhito.

Through patient acceptance, desire is generated; having striven, one weighs it. At the right time, one exerts oneself, inwardly well composed.

1033.

1033.

“Bahussutaṃ dhammadharaṃ, sappaññaṃ buddhasāvakaṃ;

Dhammaviññāṇamākaṅkhaṃ, taṃ bhajetha tathāvidhaṃ.

One who longs for special understanding of the Dhamma should associate with such a person: one who is learned, a bearer of the Dhamma, a wise disciple of the Buddha.

1034.

1034.

“Bahussuto dhammadharo, kosārakkho mahesino;

Cakkhu sabbassa lokassa, pūjanīyo bahussuto.

Learned, a bearer of the Dhamma, the treasury-guardian of the great seer, the eye for the entire world—a learned person is worthy of veneration.

1035.

1035.

“Dhammārāmo dhammarato, dhammaṃ anuvicintayaṃ;

Dhammaṃ anussaraṃ bhikkhu, saddhammā na parihāyati.

A bhikkhu who delights in the Dhamma, rejoices in the Dhamma, contemplates the Dhamma, and recollects the Dhamma, does not fall away from the good Dhamma.

1036.

1036.

“Kāyamaccheragaruno [M 0.0348] garuko (sī.), hiyyamāne hiyyamāno (sī.) anuṭṭhahe;

Sarīrasukhagiddhassa, kuto samaṇaphāsutā.

For one who is stingy with and protective of the body, who does not exert himself when declining, who is greedy for bodily pleasure—whence can there be the comfort of a recluse?

1037.

1037.

“Na [T 0.0407] pakkhanti disā sabbā, dhammā na paṭibhanti maṃ;

Gate kalyāṇamittamhi, andhakāraṃva khāyati.

The directions are not clear to me, the teachings are no longer evident; now that my good friend is gone, it seems to be just darkness.

1038.

1038.

“Abbhatītasahāyassa, atītagatasatthuno;

Natthi etādisaṃ mittaṃ, yathā kāyagatā sati.

For one whose companion has passed away, whose Teacher is gone, there is no friend like mindfulness directed to the body.

1039.

1039.

“Ye purāṇā atītā te, navehi na sameti me;

Svajja ekova jhāyāmi, vassupetova pakkhimā.

Those of old have passed away; I do not get along with the new ones. Today I meditate all alone, like a bird that has entered its nest for the rains.

1040.

1040.

“Dassanāya abhikkante, nānāverajjake bahū;

Mā vārayittha sotāro, passantu samayo mamaṃ.

Many from various kingdoms are coming for a sight of me; do not prevent these hearers. Let them see me; this is the proper time.

1041.

1041.

“Dassanāya [P 0.0093] abhikkante, nānāverajjake puthu;

Karoti satthā okāsaṃ, na nivāreti cakkhumā.

When many from various kingdoms come for a sight of him, the Teacher grants them an opportunity; the One with Vision does not prevent them.

1042.

1042.

“Paṇṇavīsativassāni, sekhabhūtassa me sato;

Na kāmasaññā uppajji, passa dhammasudhammataṃ.

For twenty-five years, while I was a trainee, no perception of sensual desire arose in me. Behold the excellence of the Dhamma!

1043.

1043.

“Paṇṇavīsativassāni, sekhabhūtassa me sato;

Na dosasaññā uppajji, passa dhammasudhammataṃ.

For twenty-five years, while I was a trainee, no perception of ill will arose in me. Behold the excellence of the Dhamma!

1044.

1044.

“Paṇṇavīsativassāni, bhagavantaṃ upaṭṭhahiṃ;

Mettena kāyakammena, chāyāva anapāyinī anupāyinī (syā. ka.).

For twenty-five years I attended on the Blessed One with bodily deeds of loving-kindness, like a shadow that never departs.

1045.

1045.

“Paṇṇavīsativassāni, bhagavantaṃ upaṭṭhahiṃ;

Mettena vacīkammena, chāyāva anapāyinī.

For twenty-five years I attended on the Blessed One with verbal deeds of loving-kindness, like a shadow that never departs.

1046.

1046.

“Paṇṇavīsativassāni, bhagavantaṃ upaṭṭhahiṃ;

Mettena manokammena, chāyāva anapāyinī.

For twenty-five years, I attended upon the Blessed One with mental deeds of loving-kindness, like a shadow that never departs.

1047.

1047.

“Buddhassa [T 0.0408][V 0.0280] caṅkamantassa, piṭṭhito anucaṅkamiṃ;

Dhamme desiyamānamhi, ñāṇaṃ me udapajjatha.

I walked behind the Buddha as he was walking; when the Dhamma was being taught, knowledge arose in me.

1048.

1048.

“Ahaṃ sakaraṇīyomhi, sekho appattamānaso;

Satthu ca parinibbānaṃ, yo amhaṃ anukampako.

I am one with something still to do, a trainee who has not reached the goal; and the final Nibbāna of the Teacher, who was compassionate to me, is at hand.

1049.

1049.

“Tadāsi [M 0.0349] yaṃ bhiṃsanakaṃ, tadāsi lomahaṃsanaṃ;

Sabbākāravarūpete, sambuddhe parinibbute.

Then there was terror, then there was horripilation, when the Perfectly Enlightened One, endowed with all the finest qualities, attained final Nibbāna.

1050.

1050.

“Bahussuto dhammadharo, kosārakkho mahesino;

Cakkhu sabbassa lokassa, ānando parinibbuto.

Learned, a bearer of the Dhamma, the treasury-guardian of the great seer, the eye for the entire world—Ānanda has attained Parinibbāna.

1051.

1051.

“Bahussuto dhammadharo, kosārakkho mahesino;

Cakkhu sabbassa lokassa, andhakāre tamonudo.

I am learned, a bearer of the Dhamma, the treasury-guardian of the great seer. I am the eye for the entire world, a dispeller of the darkness in the gloom.

1052.

1052.

“Gatimanto satimanto, dhitimanto ca yo isi;

Saddhammadhārako thero, ānando ratanākaro.

That sage, endowed with wisdom's movement, mindfulness, and resolution, the elder Ānanda, was a bearer of the good Dhamma, a mine of jewels.

1053.

1053.

“Pariciṇṇo mayā satthā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ;

Ohito garuko bhāro, natthi dāni punabbhavo”ti.

The Teacher has been served by me, the Buddha’s teaching has been done; the heavy burden is laid down, now there is no more renewed existence.

… Ānando thero….

Thus the Elder Ānanda spoke these verses.

Tiṃsanipāto niṭṭhito.

The Section of the Thirties is finished.

Tatruddānaṃ –

The summary therein:

Phussopatisso ānando, tayotime pakittitā;

Gāthāyo tattha saṅkhātā, sataṃ pañca ca uttarīti;

Phussa, Upatissa, and Ānanda—these three elders are proclaimed. The verses therein are reckoned as one hundred and five.

18. Cattālīsanipāto

18. The Section of the Forties

1. Mahākassapattheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Mahākassapa

1054.

1054.

“Na [T 0.0409][M 0.0350][V 0.0281][P 0.0094] gaṇena purakkhato care, vimano hoti samādhi dullabho;

Nānājanasaṅgaho dukho, iti disvāna gaṇaṃ na rocaye.

One should not walk about surrounded by a group; the mind becomes disturbed and concentration is difficult to obtain. Gathering various people is painful; seeing this, one should not delight in a group.

1055.

1055.

“Na kulāni upabbaje muni, vimano hoti samādhi dullabho;

So ussukko rasānugiddho, atthaṃ riñcati yo sukhāvaho.

A sage should not frequent families; the mind becomes disturbed and concentration is difficult to obtain. One who is zealous and greedy for flavors abandons the goal that brings happiness.

1056.

1056.

“Paṅkoti hi naṃ avedayuṃ, yāyaṃ vandanapūjanā kulesu;

Sukhumaṃ salla durubbahaṃ, sakkāro kāpurisena dujjaho.

This homage and veneration in families, the wise have declared it to be mire. It is a subtle dart, hard to extract. Honor is hard for a base person to relinquish.

1057.

1057.

“Senāsanamhā oruyha, nagaraṃ piṇḍāya pāvisiṃ;

Bhuñjantaṃ purisaṃ kuṭṭhiṃ, sakkaccaṃ taṃ upaṭṭhahiṃ.

Descending from my lodging, I entered the city for almsfood. I respectfully approached a man with leprosy who was eating.

1058.

1058.

“So me taṃ (sī. ka.) pakkena hatthena, ālopaṃ upanāmayi;

Ālopaṃ pakkhipantassa, aṅguli cettha pettha (sī. ka.) chijjatha.

With his festering hand, he offered me a morsel; as he was placing the morsel, a finger broke off right there.

1059.

1059.

“Kuṭṭamūlañca kuḍḍamūlañca (sī. syā.) nissāya, ālopaṃ taṃ abhuñjisaṃ;

Bhuñjamāne vā bhutte vā, jegucchaṃ me na vijjati.

Leaning against the base of a wall, I ate that morsel. Neither while eating nor after having eaten was any disgust found in me.

1060.

1060.

“Uttiṭṭhapiṇḍo āhāro, pūtimuttañca osadhaṃ;

Senāsanaṃ rukkhamūlaṃ, paṃsukūlañca cīvaraṃ;

Yassete abhisambhutvā abhibhuñjati (?), sa ve cātuddiso naro.

Almsfood received while standing is my food, fermented urine is my medicine, the root of a tree is my lodging, and a robe from a dust-heap is my garment. Whoever has obtained these is truly a person of the four quarters.

1061.

1061.

“Yattha eke vihaññanti, āruhantā siluccayaṃ;

Tassa buddhassa dāyādo, sampajāno patissato;

Iddhibalenupatthaddho[T 0.0410], kassapo abhirūhati.

Where some are afflicted while climbing a rocky height, there the Buddha's heir, mindful and clearly comprehending, supported by spiritual power, Kassapa ascends.

1062.

1062.

“Piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto[M 0.0351], selamāruyha kassapo;

Jhāyati anupādāno, pahīnabhayabheravo.

Having returned from his alms round, Kassapa ascends the rock; he meditates without grasping, having abandoned fear and dread.

1063.

1063.

“Piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto, selamāruyha kassapo;

Jhāyati anupādāno, ḍayhamānesu nibbuto.

Having returned from his alms round, Kassapa ascends the rock; he meditates without grasping, extinguished amidst those who are burning.

1064.

1064.

“Piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto, selamāruyha kassapo;

Jhāyati anupādāno, katakicco anāsavo.

Having returned from his alms round, Kassapa ascends the rock; he meditates without grasping, his task done, free from taints.

1065.

1065.

“Karerimālāvitatā[V 0.0282][P 0.0095], bhūmibhāgā manoramā;

Kuñjarābhirudā rammā, te selā ramayanti maṃ.

Covered with garlands of Kareri flowers, the tracts of land are delightful; lovely, resounding with elephants, those rocks delight me.

1066.

1066.

“Nīlabbhavaṇṇā rucirā, vārisītā sucindharā;

Indagopakasañchannā, te selā ramayanti maṃ.

Blue-hued like clouds and beautiful, with cool water and clear streams, covered with Indagopaka insects—those rocks delight me.

1067.

1067.

“Nīlabbhakūṭasadisā, kūṭāgāravarūpamā;

Vāraṇābhirudā rammā, te selā ramayanti maṃ.

Like peaks of blue clouds, resembling excellent gabled halls, lovely, resounding with elephants—those rocks delight me.

1068.

1068.

“Abhivuṭṭhā rammatalā, nagā isibhi sevitā;

Abbhunnaditā sikhīhi, te selā ramayanti maṃ.

Drenched by rain, with delightful plateaus, mountains frequented by seers and resounding with peacocks—those rocks delight me.

1069.

1069.

“Alaṃ jhāyitukāmassa, pahitattassa me sato;

Alaṃ me atthakāmassa attakāmassa (?), pahitattassa bhikkhuno.

They are enough for me, mindful and resolute, who wishes to meditate. They are enough for me, the resolute monk who desires the goal.

1070.

1070.

“Alaṃ me phāsukāmassa, pahitattassa bhikkhuno;

Alaṃ me yogakāmassa, pahitattassa tādino.

Sufficient for me, a bhikkhu desiring comfort, with a resolute mind; sufficient for me, a steadfast one desiring the practice, with a resolute mind.

1071.

1071.

“Umāpupphena samānā, gaganāvabbhachāditā;

Nānādijagaṇākiṇṇā[T 0.0411], te selā ramayanti maṃ.

Like dark flax flowers, covered by dark clouds, teeming with flocks of various birds—those rocks delight me.

1072.

1072.

“Anākiṇṇā gahaṭṭhehi, migasaṅghanisevitā;

Nānādijagaṇākiṇṇā, te selā ramayanti maṃ.

Not crowded with householders, frequented by herds of deer, teeming with flocks of various birds—those rocks delight me.

1073.

1073.

“Acchodikā puthusilā, gonaṅgulamigāyutā;

Ambusevālasañchannā, te selā ramayanti maṃ.

With clear water and broad rocks, frequented by gaur, langurs, and deer, covered with water-moss—those rocks delight me.

1074.

1074.

“Na pañcaṅgikena turiyena, rati me hoti tādisī;

Yathā ekaggacittassa, sammā dhammaṃ vipassato.

The delight I have from the five-limbed ensemble of musical instruments is not like that which I have when, with a one-pointed mind, I rightly see the Dhamma with insight.

1075.

1075.

“Kammaṃ [M 0.0352] bahukaṃ na kāraye, parivajjeyya janaṃ na uyyame;

Ussukko so rasānugiddho, atthaṃ riñcati yo sukhāvaho.

One should not undertake much work; one should avoid people and not strive. The zealous one, greedy for flavors, relinquishes the goal that brings happiness.

1076.

1076.

“Kammaṃ bahukaṃ na kāraye, parivajjeyya anattaneyyametaṃ;

Kicchati kāyo kilamati, dukkhito so samathaṃ na vindati.

One should not do much work; one should avoid this, as it is not for one's own good. The body is troubled and becomes weary; being afflicted, one does not find tranquility.

1077.

1077.

“Oṭṭhappahatamattena, attānampi na passati;

Patthaddhagīvo carati, ahaṃ seyyoti maññati.

By a mere movement of the lips, he does not see his own self; he walks about with a stiff neck, thinking, 'I am better.'

1078.

1078.

“Aseyyo seyyasamānaṃ, bālo maññati attānaṃ;

Na taṃ viññū pasaṃsanti, patthaddhamānasaṃ naraṃ.

Though he is inferior, the fool thinks himself equal to his superior; the wise do not praise that man of obstinate conceit.

1079.

1079.

“Yo [V 0.0283] ca seyyohamasmīti, nāhaṃ seyyoti vā pana;

Hīno taṃsadiso tīnohaṃ sadiso (syā.) vāti, vidhāsu na vikampati.

But one who is not shaken by the various states of conceit, such as 'I am superior,' or 'I am not superior,' or 'I am inferior,' or 'I am equal'—

1080.

1080.

“Paññavantaṃ [P 0.0096] tathā tādiṃ, sīlesu susamāhitaṃ;

Cetosamathamanuttaṃ, tañce viññū pasaṃsare.

The wise praise such a one who is wise and steadfast, well-composed in the virtues, and devoted to the calm of mind.

1081.

1081.

“Yassa [T 0.0412] sabrahmacārīsu, gāravo nūpalabbhati;

Ārakā hoti saddhammā, nabhato puthavī yathā.

One in whom no respect is found for his companions in the holy life is far from the good Dhamma, as the sky is from the earth.

1082.

1082.

“Yesañca hiri ottappaṃ, sadā sammā upaṭṭhitaṃ;

Virūḷhabrahmacariyā te, tesaṃ khīṇā punabbhavā.

For those in whom shame and fear of wrongdoing are always well established, their holy life has flourished; for them, renewed existence is destroyed.

1083.

1083.

“Uddhato capalo bhikkhu, paṃsukūlena pāruto;

Kapīva sīhacammena, na so tenupasobhati.

A bhikkhu who is restless and fickle, though clad in a dust-heap robe, is not made beautiful by it, like a monkey in a lion's skin.

1084.

1084.

“Anuddhato acapalo, nipako saṃvutindriyo;

Sobhati paṃsukūlena, sīhova girigabbhare.

Not restless and not fickle, prudent, with restrained senses, he shines in his dust-heap robe like a lion in a mountain cave.

1085.

1085.

“Ete sambahulā devā, iddhimanto yasassino;

Dasadevasahassāni, sabbe te brahmakāyikā.

These are many devas, powerful and glorious—ten thousand devas, all of them of the Brahmā group.

1086.

1086.

“Dhammasenāpatiṃ vīraṃ, mahājhāyiṃ samāhitaṃ;

Sāriputtaṃ namassantā, tiṭṭhanti pañjalīkatā.

They stand with hands raised in reverence, paying homage to Sāriputta: the heroic General of the Dhamma, the great meditator, the concentrated one.

1087.

1087.

“‘Namo [M 0.0353] te purisājañña, namo te purisuttama;

Yassa te nābhijānāma, yampi nissāya jhāyati jhāyasi (ka. aṭṭha.).

‘Homage to you, O thoroughbred among men! Homage to you, O supreme among men! We do not know that, relying on which, you meditate.’

1088.

1088.

“‘Accheraṃ vata buddhānaṃ, gambhīro gocaro sako;

Ye mayaṃ nābhijānāma, vālavedhisamāgatā’.

‘How wonderful, indeed! Profound is the personal domain of the Buddhas, which we do not understand, though we are like archers who can split a hair.’

1089.

1089.

“Taṃ tathā devakāyehi, pūjitaṃ pūjanārahaṃ;

Sāriputtaṃ tadā disvā, kappinassa sitaṃ ahu.

Then, seeing Sāriputta—worthy of honor—being honored in that way by the host of devas, a smile arose for Kappina.

1090.

1090.

“Yāvatā buddhakhettamhi, ṭhapayitvā mahāmuniṃ;

Dhutaguṇe visiṭṭhohaṃ, sadiso me na vijjati.

Throughout the Buddha-field, excepting the Great Sage, I am pre-eminent in the ascetic qualities; there is no one equal to me.

1091.

1091.

“Pariciṇṇo [T 0.0413] mayā satthā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ;

Ohito garuko bhāro, natthi dāni punabbhavo.

The Teacher has been served by me; the Buddha's teaching has been fulfilled. The heavy burden is laid down; there is now no more renewed existence.

1092.

1092.

“Na [V 0.0284] cīvare na sayane, bhojane nupalimpati;

Gotamo anappameyyo, muḷālapupphaṃ vimalaṃva;

Ambunā nekkhammaninno, tibhavābhinissaṭo.

The immeasurable Gotama is not sullied by robes, lodging, or food, just as a spotless lotus flower is not sullied by water. He is inclined to renunciation, having escaped from the three states of existence.

1093.

1093.

“Satipaṭṭhānagīvo so, saddhāhattho mahāmuni;

Paññāsīso mahāñāṇī, sadā carati nibbuto”ti.

That Great Sage has the foundations of mindfulness for his neck, faith for his hands, and wisdom for his head; possessing great knowledge, he always fares extinguished.

… Mahākassapo thero….

The Elder Mahākassapa spoke these verses.

Cattālīsanipāto niṭṭhito.

The Chapter of the Forties is finished.

Tatruddānaṃ –

The summary verse therein:

Cattālīsanipātamhi, mahākassapasavhayo;

Ekova thero gāthāyo, cattāsīla duvepi cāti.

In the Chapter of the Forties, there is only one elder, the one named Mahākassapa; and the verses are forty-two.

19. Paññāsanipāto

19. The Chapter of the Fifties

1. Tālapuṭattheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Tālapuṭa

1094.

1094.

“Kadā [M 0.0354][V 0.0285][P 0.0097] nuhaṃ pabbatakandarāsu, ekākiyo addutiyo vihassaṃ;

Aniccato sabbabhavaṃ vipassaṃ, taṃ me idaṃ taṃ nu kadā bhavissati.

When shall I dwell in mountain caves, alone, without craving as a second companion, contemplating all existence as impermanent? When, oh when, will this thought of mine be realized?

1095.

1095.

“Kadā nuhaṃ bhinnapaṭandharo muni, kāsāvavattho [T 0.0414] amamo nirāso;

Rāgañca dosañca tatheva mohaṃ, hantvā sukhī pavanagato vihassaṃ.

When shall I, a sage wearing robes of patched cloth, clad in the saffron garment, free from attachment and without longing, having destroyed lust, hatred, and likewise delusion, dwell happily, having gone to the great forest?

1096.

1096.

“Kadā aniccaṃ vadharoganīḷaṃ, kāyaṃ imaṃ maccujarāyupaddutaṃ;

Vipassamāno vītabhayo vihassaṃ, eko vane taṃ nu kadā bhavissati.

When, repeatedly contemplating this body as impermanent, a nest of slaughter and disease, afflicted by death and old age, shall I dwell free from fear, alone in the great forest? Oh, when will that thought be realized?

1097.

1097.

“Kadā nuhaṃ bhayajananiṃ dukhāvahaṃ, taṇhālataṃ bahuvidhānuvattaniṃ;

Paññāmayaṃ tikhiṇamasiṃ gahetvā, chetvā vase tampi kadā bhavissati.

When shall I, taking the sharp sword made of wisdom, cut down the creeper of craving—which generates fear, brings suffering, and follows along in many ways—and dwell? When will that thought, too, be realized?

1098.

1098.

“Kadā nu paññāmayamuggatejaṃ, satthaṃ isīnaṃ sahasādiyitvā;

Māraṃ sasenaṃ sahasā bhañjissaṃ, sīhāsane taṃ nu kadā bhavissati.

When shall I, swiftly seizing the seers' weapon of lofty power, forged from wisdom, swiftly shatter Māra with his army while seated on the lion's seat? Oh, when will that thought be realized?

1099.

1099.

“Kadā nuhaṃ sabbhi samāgamesu, diṭṭho bhave dhammagarūhi tādibhi;

Yāthāvadassīhi jitindriyehi, padhāniyo [T 0.0415] taṃ nu kadā bhavissati.

When, striving diligently, shall I be seen in gatherings of the good—by Such Ones who revere the Dhamma, who see things as they truly are, and who have conquered their faculties? Oh, when will that thought be realized?

1100.

1100.

“Kadā nu maṃ tandi khudā pipāsā, vātātapā kīṭasarīsapā vā;

Na bādhayissanti na taṃ giribbaje, atthatthiyaṃ taṃ nu kadā bhavissati.

When will lethargy, hunger, and thirst, wind and sun, or insects and reptiles no longer afflict me as I strive for the goal in the mountain fastness? Oh, when will that thought be realized?

1101.

1101.

“Kadā [M 0.0355][P 0.0098] nu kho yaṃ viditaṃ mahesinā, cattāri saccāni sududdasāni;

Samāhitatto satimā agacchaṃ, paññāya taṃ taṃ nu kadā bhavissati.

When shall I, with a mind well-concentrated and with mindfulness, penetrate with wisdom those Four Truths, so very hard to see, which were understood by the Great Seer? Oh, when will that thought be realized?

1102.

1102.

“Kadā nu rūpe amite ca sadde, gandhe rase phusitabbe ca dhamme;

Ādittatohaṃ samathehi yutto, paññāya dacchaṃ tadidaṃ kadā me.

When shall I, endowed with states of calm, see with wisdom immeasurable forms, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena as blazing? When will this be for me?

1103.

1103.

“Kadā nuhaṃ dubbacanena vutto, tatonimittaṃ vimano na hessaṃ;

Atho pasatthopi tatonimittaṃ, tuṭṭho na hessaṃ tadidaṃ kadā me.

When, being addressed with harsh words, will I not be dejected on that account? And when praised, will I not be pleased on that account? When will this be for me?

1104.

1104.

“Kadā nu kaṭṭhe ca tiṇe latā ca, khandhe imehaṃ amite ca dhamme;

Ajjhattikāneva ca bāhirāni ca, samaṃ [T 0.0416] tuleyyaṃ tadidaṃ kadā me.

When shall I treat as equal and weigh alike wood, grass, and creepers, these aggregates, and immeasurable phenomena, both internal and external? When will this be for me?

1105.

1105.

“Kadā nu maṃ pāvusakālamegho, navena toyena sacīvaraṃ vane;

Isippayātamhi pathe vajantaṃ, ovassate taṃ nu kadā bhavissati.

When will the monsoon cloud drench me and my robe with fresh water, as I am walking in the forest on the path trodden by the seers? Oh, when will that thought be realized?

1106.

1106.

“Kadā [V 0.0286] mayūrassa sikhaṇḍino vane, dijassa sutvā girigabbhare rutaṃ;

Paccuṭṭhahitvā amatassa pattiyā, saṃcintaye taṃ nu kadā bhavissati.

When, hearing in a mountain cave the cry of the twice-born, crested peacock, shall I rise up and, for the sake of attaining the Deathless, reflect well? Oh, when will that thought be realized?

1107.

1107.

“Kadā nu gaṅgaṃ yamunaṃ sarassatiṃ, pātālakhittaṃ vaḷavāmukhañca balavāmukhañca (ka.);

Asajjamāno patareyyamiddhiyā, vibhiṃsanaṃ taṃ nu kadā bhavissati.

When shall I, unattached, cross by psychic power the Gaṅgā, the Yamunā, the Sarassatī, the Pātāla chasm, and the terrifying Mare's Mouth? Oh, when will that thought be realized?

1108.

1108.

“Kadā [M 0.0356] nu nāgova asaṅgacārī, padālaye kāmaguṇesu chandaṃ;

Nibbajjayaṃ sabbasubhaṃ nimittaṃ, jhāne yuto taṃ nu kadā bhavissati.

When shall I, like an elephant wandering unattached, yoked to jhāna and completely abandoning every sign of the beautiful, shatter the desire for sensual pleasures? Oh, when will that thought be realized?

1109.

1109.

“Kadā [P 0.0099] iṇaṭṭova daliddako daḷiddako (sī.) nidhiṃ, ārādhayitvā dhanikehi pīḷito;

Tuṭṭho bhavissaṃ [T 0.0417] adhigamma sāsanaṃ, mahesino taṃ nu kadā bhavissati.

When shall I, like a poor man in debt, oppressed by his creditors, who rejoices upon finding a treasure, be pleased, having attained the teaching of the Great Seer? Oh, when will that thought be realized?

1110.

1110.

“Bahūni vassāni tayāmhi yācito, ‘agāravāsena alaṃ nu te idaṃ’;

Taṃ dāni maṃ pabbajitaṃ samānaṃ, kiṃkāraṇā citta tuvaṃ na yuñjasi.

For many years I was begged by you, O mind: ‘Enough of this household life for you!’ Now that I have gone forth, for what reason, O mind, do you not apply yourself?

1111.

1111.

“Nanu ahaṃ citta tayāmhi yācito, ‘giribbaje citrachadā vihaṅgamā’;

Mahindaghosatthanitābhigajjino, te taṃ ramessanti vanamhi jhāyinaṃ.

Was I not begged by you, O mind: ‘In the mountain fastness, birds with colorful plumage, thundering with a voice like Indra’s, will delight you as you meditate in the forest’?

1112.

1112.

“Kulamhi mitte ca piye ca ñātake, khiḍḍāratiṃ kāmaguṇañca loke;

Sabbaṃ pahāya imamajjhupāgato, athopi tvaṃ citta na mayha tussasi.

Having abandoned family, friends, dear ones, and relatives, play, amusement, and sensual pleasures in the world—having abandoned all this, I have come here. And yet, O mind, you are not pleased with me.

1113.

1113.

“Mameva etaṃ na hi tvaṃ paresaṃ, sannāhakāle paridevitena kiṃ;

Sabbaṃ idaṃ calamiti pekkhamāno, abhinikkhamiṃ amatapadaṃ jigīsaṃ.

This mind is mine indeed, not another’s. At the time for arming, what is the use of lamentation? Seeing that all this is transient, I went forth, desiring to win the deathless state.

1114.

1114.

“Suyuttavādī dvipadānamuttamo, mahābhisakko naradammasārathi sārathī (sī.);

‘Cittaṃ [T 0.0418] calaṃ makkaṭasannibhaṃ iti, avītarāgena sudunnivārayaṃ’.

The speaker of what is fitting, the supreme among bipeds, the great physician, the charioteer of those to be tamed, has said: ‘The mind is fickle, like a monkey; for one not free from lust, it is very hard to restrain.’

1115.

1115.

“Kāmā [M 0.0357] hi citrā madhurā manoramā, aviddasū yattha sitā puthujjanā;

Te dukkhamicchanti punabbhavesino, cittena nītā niraye nirākatā.

Sensual pleasures are indeed varied, sweet, and delightful, wherein unwise ordinary people are bound. Seeking renewed existence, they desire suffering; led by the mind, they are cast down into hell, bereft of welfare.

1116.

1116.

“‘Mayūrakoñcābhirutamhi kānane, dīpīhi byagghehi purakkhato vasaṃ;

Kāye apekkhaṃ jaha mā virādhaya’, itissu maṃ citta pure niyuñjasi.

‘Dwell in the forest resounding with the calls of peacocks and herons, surrounded by leopards and tigers. Abandon attachment to the body; do not fail!’—thus, O mind, you formerly urged me.

1117.

1117.

“‘Bhāvehi [P 0.0100] jhānāni ca indriyāni ca, balāni bojjhaṅgasamādhibhāvanā;

Tisso ca vijjā phusa buddhasāsane’, itissu maṃ citta pure niyuñjasi.

‘Develop the jhānas, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, and the development of concentration. In the Buddha’s Dispensation, realize the three true knowledges!’—thus, O mind, you formerly urged me.

1118.

1118.

“‘Bhāvehi maggaṃ amatassa pattiyā, niyyānikaṃ sabbadukhakkhayogadhaṃ;

Aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ sabbakilesasodhanaṃ’, itissu maṃ citta pure niyuñjasi.

‘Develop the eight-factored path for the attainment of the Deathless—the path that leads out, that is the elixir for the destruction of all suffering, that purifies all defilements!’—thus, O mind, you formerly urged me.

1119.

1119.

“‘Dukkhanti khandhe paṭipassa yoniso, yato [T 0.0419] ca dukkhaṃ samudeti taṃ jaha;

Idheva dukkhassa karohi antaṃ’, itissu maṃ citta pure niyuñjasi.

‘Wisely contemplate the aggregates as suffering. Abandon that from which suffering arises. Make an end of suffering right here in this very life!’—thus, O mind, you formerly urged me.

1120.

1120.

“‘Aniccaṃ [V 0.0287] dukkhanti vipassa yoniso, suññaṃ anattāti aghaṃ vadhanti ca;

Manovicāre uparundha cetaso’, itissu maṃ citta pure niyuñjasi.

‘Wisely contemplate things as impermanent and suffering, as empty and not-self, as a calamity and a slaughter. Restrain the discursive thoughts of the mind!’—thus, O mind, you formerly urged me.

1121.

1121.

“‘Muṇḍo virūpo abhisāpamāgato, kapālahatthova kulesu bhikkhasu;

Yuñjassu satthuvacane mahesino’, itissu maṃ citta pure niyuñjasi.

‘Shaven-headed, of altered appearance, as if come under a curse, go begging from family to family with bowl in hand. Apply yourself to the word of the Teacher, the Great Seer!’—thus, O mind, you formerly urged me.

1122.

1122.

“‘Susaṃvutatto [M 0.0358] visikhantare caraṃ, kulesu kāmesu asaṅgamānaso;

Cando yathā dosinapuṇṇamāsiyā’, itissu maṃ citta pure niyuñjasi.

‘With self well-restrained, wander in the street, with mind unattached to sensual pleasures among the families, like the moon on a faultless full-moon night’—thus, O mind, you formerly urged me.

1123.

1123.

“‘Āraññiko hohi ca piṇḍapātiko, sosāniko hohi ca paṃsukūliko;

Nesajjiko hohi sadā dhute rato’, itissu maṃ citta pure niyuñjasi.

‘Be a forest-dweller and an alms-food-eater; be a charnel-ground-dweller and a rag-robe-wearer. Be one who practices the sitter’s observance, ever delighting in the ascetic practices!’—thus, O mind, you formerly urged me.

1124.

1124.

“Ropetva [T 0.0420] rukkhāni yathā phalesī, mūle taruṃ chettu tameva icchasi;

Tathūpamaṃ cittamidaṃ karosi, yaṃ maṃ aniccamhi cale niyuñjasi.

Just as one who seeks fruit, after planting a tree, might then wish to cut it down at the root, you do a similar thing, O mind, when you urge me back to the impermanent and fickle.

1125.

1125.

“Arūpa dūraṅgama ekacāri, na te karissaṃ vacanaṃ idānihaṃ;

Dukkhā hi kāmā kaṭukā mahabbhayā, nibbānamevābhimano carissaṃ.

O formless one, far-going, solitary-faring! I will not do your bidding now. For sensual pleasures are painful, bitter, fraught with great danger. I will fare on with my mind set only on Nibbāna.

1126.

1126.

“Nāhaṃ alakkhyā ahirikkatāya vā, na cittahetū na ca dūrakantanā;

Ājīvahetū ca ahaṃ na nikkhamiṃ, kato ca te citta paṭissavo mayā.

I did not go forth because of misfortune or shamelessness, nor due to a deranged mind, nor as a fugitive. I did not go forth for the sake of a livelihood. And a promise was made by me to you, O mind.

1127.

1127.

“‘Appicchatā sappurisehi vaṇṇitā, makkhappahānaṃ vūpasamo dukhassa’;

Itissu [P 0.0101] maṃ citta tadā niyuñjasi, idāni tvaṃ gacchasi pubbaciṇṇaṃ.

‘Fewness of wishes is praised by the good, as is the abandoning of hypocrisy and the appeasement of suffering.’ Thus, O mind, you urged me then. Now you revert to your old habits.

1128.

1128.

“Taṇhā avijjā ca piyāpiyañca, subhāni rūpāni sukhā ca vedanā;

Manāpiyā kāmaguṇā ca vantā, vante ahaṃ āvamituṃ na ussahe.

Craving and ignorance, the dear and the not-dear, beautiful forms and pleasant feelings, and agreeable sensual pleasures have all been vomited out. I am unable to swallow again what I have vomited.

1129.

1129.

“Sabbattha [T 0.0421][M 0.0359] te citta vaco kataṃ mayā, bahūsu jātīsu na mesi kopito;

Ajjhattasambhavo kataññutāya te, dukkhe ciraṃ saṃsaritaṃ tayā kate.

In all things, O mind, your word was done by me; in many births you were not angered by me. You who arise from within, through your ingratitude, I have wandered long in the suffering created by you.

1130.

1130.

“Tvaññeva no citta karosi brāhmaṇo brāhmaṇe (sī.), brāhmaṇaṃ (?) bhāvalopa-tappadhānatā gahetabbā, tvaṃ khattiyo rājadasī rājadisī (syā. ka.) karosi;

Vessā ca suddā ca bhavāma ekadā, devattanaṃ vāpi taveva vāhasā.

You alone, O mind, make us brahmins; you make us khattiyas and royal seers. At times we become vessas and suddas; and it is by your power that we attain the state of a deva.

1131.

1131.

“Taveva hetū asurā bhavāmase, tvaṃmūlakaṃ nerayikā bhavāmase;

Atho tiracchānagatāpi ekadā, petattanaṃ vāpi taveva vāhasā.

Because of you we become asuras; rooted in you, we become beings in hell. And sometimes we go to the animal realm, or attain the state of a peta—all by your power.

1132.

1132.

“Nanu dubbhissasi maṃ punappunaṃ, muhuṃ muhuṃ cāraṇikaṃva dassayaṃ;

Ummattakeneva mayā palobhasi, kiñcāpi te citta virādhitaṃ mayā.

Surely you betray me again and again, repeatedly displaying yourself like a wandering actor. You entice me as if I were mad. What wrong have I done to you, O mind?

1133.

1133.

“Idaṃ pure cittamacāri cārikaṃ, yenicchakaṃ yatthakāmaṃ yathāsukhaṃ;

Tadajjahaṃ niggahessāmi yoniso, hatthippabhinnaṃ [T 0.0422] viya aṅkusaggaho.

Formerly this mind wandered where it wished, where it liked, as it pleased. Today I will restrain it wisely, as a mahout with a hook restrains a rutting elephant.

1134.

1134.

“Satthā [V 0.0288] ca me lokamimaṃ adhiṭṭhahi, aniccato addhuvato asārato;

Pakkhanda maṃ citta jinassa sāsane, tārehi oghā mahatā suduttarā.

My Teacher has explained this world as impermanent, unstable, and essenceless. O mind, cause me to leap into the Conqueror’s Dispensation! Carry me across the great flood, so very hard to cross.

1135.

1135.

“Na te idaṃ citta yathā purāṇakaṃ, nāhaṃ alaṃ tuyha vase nivattituṃ vasena vattituṃ (?);

Mahesino pabbajitomhi sāsane, na mādisā honti vināsadhārino.

Things are not for you now, O mind, as they were before. I am no longer fit to live under your control. I have gone forth in the Great Seer’s Dispensation; those like me are not bearers of ruin.

1136.

1136.

“Nagā [M 0.0360][P 0.0102] samuddā saritā vasundharā, disā catasso vidisā adho divā;

Sabbe aniccā tibhavā upaddutā, kuhiṃ gato citta sukhaṃ ramissasi.

Mountains, oceans, rivers, and the earth; the four directions, the intermediate directions, what is below and in the heavens; all three realms of existence are impermanent and afflicted. Where can you go, O mind, to delight in happiness?

1137.

1137.

“Dhitipparaṃ kiṃ mama citta kāhisi, na te alaṃ citta vasānuvattako;

Na jātu bhastaṃ ubhatomukhaṃ chupe, dhiratthu pūraṃ nava sotasandaniṃ.

What can you do to me, O mind, a man of firm resolve? I am no longer fit to be your follower, O mind. One should never touch a two-mouthed bag. Shame on this body, full and flowing from its nine streams!

1138.

1138.

“Varāhaeṇeyyavigāḷhasevite, pabbhārakuṭṭe pakateva sundare;

Navambunā pāvusasitthakānane, tahiṃ [T 0.0423] guhāgehagato ramissasi.

Having gone to your home in a cave, you will delight there on a lovely mountain slope, beautiful as if specially made, frequented by boars and deer, in a forest sprinkled by the fresh rains of the monsoon.

1139.

1139.

“Sunīlagīvā susikhā supekhunā, sucittapattacchadanā vihaṅgamā;

Sumañjughosatthanitābhigajjino, te taṃ ramessanti vanamhi jhāyinaṃ.

Birds with lovely blue necks, fine crests, and beautiful tail-feathers, with wings of variegated colors, thundering with a sweet and lovely sound—they will delight you in the forest as you meditate.

1140.

1140.

“Vuṭṭhamhi deve caturaṅgule tiṇe, saṃpupphite meghanibhamhi kānane;

Nagantare viṭapisamo sayissaṃ, taṃ me mudū hehiti tūlasannibhaṃ.

When the sky-god has rained and the grass is four fingers high, when the cloud-like forest is in full bloom, in a mountain glen I will lie down like a tree; that bed of grass will be soft for me, like cotton.

1141.

1141.

“Tathā tu kassāmi yathāpi issaro, yaṃ labbhati tenapi hotu me alaṃ;

Na tāhaṃ kassāmi yathā atandito, biḷārabhastaṃva yathā sumadditaṃ.

I will act like a master, and be content with whatever I get. I will act diligently, making you pliant like a well-softened cat-skin bag.

1142.

1142.

“Tathā tu kassāmi yathāpi issaro, yaṃ labbhati tenapi hotu me alaṃ;

Vīriyena taṃ mayha vasānayissaṃ, gajaṃva mattaṃ kusalaṅkusaggaho.

I will act like a master, and be content with whatever I obtain. With energy I will bring you under my control, like a skilled goad-holder brings a rutting elephant.

1143.

1143.

“Tayā [M 0.0361] sudantena avaṭṭhitena hi, hayena [T 0.0424] yoggācariyova ujjunā;

Pahomi maggaṃ paṭipajjituṃ sivaṃ, cittānurakkhīhi sadā nisevitaṃ.

With you, my mind, well-tamed and steadfast, I am able to enter upon the auspicious path—always frequented by those who guard their minds—just as a trainer is able with an upright horse.

1144.

1144.

“Ārammaṇe [P 0.0103] taṃ balasā nibandhisaṃ, nāgaṃva thambhamhi daḷhāya rajjuyā;

Taṃ me suguttaṃ satiyā subhāvitaṃ, anissitaṃ sabbabhavesu hehisi.

I will bind you by force to the meditation object, like an elephant to a post with a strong rope. Well-guarded by my mindfulness and well-developed, you will be unattached in all forms of existence.

1145.

1145.

“Paññāya chetvā vipathānusārinaṃ, yogena niggayha pathe nivesiya;

Disvā samudayaṃ vibhavañca sambhavaṃ, dāyādako hehisi aggavādino.

Having cut off with wisdom your tendency to follow wrong paths, having restrained you by spiritual application and set you on the right path, having seen the origin, cessation, and arising, you will be an heir of the Foremost Proponent.

1146.

1146.

“Catubbipallāsavasaṃ adhiṭṭhitaṃ, gāmaṇḍalaṃva parinesi citta maṃ;

Nanu nūna (sī.) saṃyojanabandhanacchidaṃ, saṃsevase kāruṇikaṃ mahāmuniṃ.

O mind, you lead me about like a village boy, me who am established under the sway of the four perversions. Should you not attend upon the compassionate Great Sage, the cutter of the bonds of the fetters?

1147.

1147.

“Migo yathā seri sucittakānane, rammaṃ giriṃ pāvusaabbhamāliniṃ māliṃ (?);

Anākule tattha nage ramissaṃ ramissasi (syā. ka.), asaṃsayaṃ citta parā bhavissasi.

Just as a deer roams freely in a beautifully variegated forest, so will I delight on that untroubled mountain, a delightful peak garlanded with rain clouds. Without a doubt, O mind, you will be vanquished.

1148.

1148.

“Ye [T 0.0425][V 0.0289] tuyha chandena vasena vattino, narā ca nārī ca anubhonti yaṃ sukhaṃ;

Aviddasū māravasānuvattino, bhavābhinandī tava citta sāvakā”ti.

Those men and women who live under the sway of your will, experiencing whatever pleasure there is—they are ignorant, followers of Māra’s sway, delighting in existence. O mind, they are your disciples.

… Tālapuṭo thero….

… The Elder Tālapuṭa …

Paññāsanipāto niṭṭhito.

The Nipāta of Fifty is finished.

Tatruddānaṃ –

The summary:

Paññāsamhi nipātamhi, eko tālapuṭo suci;

Gāthāyo tattha paññāsa, puna pañca ca uttarīti.

In the Nipāta of Fifty, there is the one, the pure Tālapuṭa. The verses there are fifty and five more besides.

20. Saṭṭhinipāto

20. The Nipāta of Sixty Verses

1. Mahāmoggallānattheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Mahāmoggallāna

1149.

1149.

“Āraññikā [M 0.0362][V 0.0290][P 0.0104] piṇḍapātikā, uñchāpattāgate ratā;

Dālemu maccuno senaṃ, ajjhattaṃ susamāhitā.

As forest-dwellers and alms-food-eaters, delighting in what is obtained by gleaning, let us, inwardly well-concentrated, shatter the army of Death.

1150.

1150.

“Āraññikā piṇḍapātikā, uñchāpattāgate ratā;

Dhunāma [T 0.0426] maccuno senaṃ, naḷāgāraṃva kuñjaro.

As forest-dwellers and alms-food-eaters, delighting in what is obtained by gleaning, let us destroy the army of Death as an elephant destroys a reed hut.

1151.

1151.

“Rukkhamūlikā sātatikā, uñchāpattāgate ratā;

Dālemu maccuno senaṃ, ajjhattaṃ susamāhitā.

As persevering tree-root-dwellers, delighting in what is obtained by gleaning, let us, inwardly well-concentrated, shatter the army of Death.

1152.

1152.

“Rukkhamūlikā sātatikā, uñchāpattāgate ratā;

Dhunāma maccuno senaṃ, naḷāgāraṃva kuñjaro.

As persevering tree-root-dwellers, delighting in what is obtained by gleaning, let us destroy the army of Death as an elephant destroys a reed hut.

1153.

1153.

“Aṭṭhikaṅkalakuṭike, maṃsanhārupasibbite;

Dhiratthu pure duggandhe, paragatte mamāyase.

Fie on this foul-smelling citadel, a hut of bones stitched with flesh and sinews, this body of another that you cherish.

1154.

1154.

“Gūthabhaste taconaddhe, uragaṇḍipisācini;

Nava sotāni te kāye, yāni sandanti sabbadā.

O bag of filth bound with skin, O she-demon with a boil on your breast! There are nine streams in your body which are always flowing.

1155.

1155.

“Tava sarīraṃ navasotaṃ, duggandhakaraṃ paribandhaṃ;

Bhikkhu parivajjayate taṃ, mīḷhaṃ ca yathā sucikāmo.

Your body has nine streams, produces a foul smell, and is a hindrance. A bhikkhu avoids it, just as one who desires purity avoids excrement.

1156.

1156.

“Evañce taṃ jano jaññā, yathā jānāmi taṃ ahaṃ;

Ārakā parivajjeyya, gūthaṭṭhānaṃva pāvuse”.

If people knew you as I know you, they would avoid you from afar, like a cesspool in the rainy season.

1157.

1157.

“Evametaṃ mahāvīra, yathā samaṇa bhāsasi;

Ettha ceke visīdanti, paṅkamhiva jaraggavo.

It is just so, great hero; it is as you say, ascetic. And yet some sink down in this, like an old ox in the mud.

1158.

1158.

“Ākāsamhi haliddiyā, yo maññetha rajetave;

Aññena vāpi raṅgena, vighātudayameva taṃ.

One who would think to dye the sky with turmeric, or with any other color, would only find vexation.

1159.

1159.

“Tadākāsasamaṃ cittaṃ, ajjhattaṃ susamāhitaṃ;

Mā pāpacitte āsādi, aggikhandhaṃva pakkhimā.

My mind is like the sky, inwardly well-concentrated. Do not assail it with an evil mind, as a moth a mass of fire.

1160.

1160.

“Passa cittakataṃ bimbaṃ, arukāyaṃ samussitaṃ;

Āturaṃ bahusaṅkappaṃ, yassa natthi dhuvaṃ ṭhiti.

Behold this decorated image, a body of wounds, built up, diseased, much-fancied, for which there is no lasting stability.

1161.

1161.

“Passa [V 0.0291] cittakataṃ rūpaṃ, maṇinā kuṇḍalena ca;

Aṭṭhiṃ tacena onaddhaṃ, saha vatthehi sobhati.

Behold the decorated form, with a jewel and an earring. A bone bound with skin, it shines together with its clothes.

1162.

1162.

“Alattakakatā [M 0.0363] pādā, mukhaṃ cuṇṇakamakkhitaṃ;

Alaṃ bālassa mohāya, no ca pāragavesino.

The feet are dyed with lac, the face is smeared with powder. Enough to delude a fool, but not one who seeks the far shore.

1163.

1163.

“Aṭṭhapadakatā kesā, nettā añjanamakkhitā;

Alaṃ bālassa mohāya, no ca pāragavesino.

The hair is styled in eight plaits, the eyes are smeared with collyrium. Enough to delude a fool, but not one who seeks the far shore.

1164.

1164.

“Añjanīva navā cittā, pūtikāyo alaṅkato;

Alaṃ bālassa mohāya, no ca pāragavesino.

Like a new, painted cosmetic box, this foul body is adorned. Enough to delude a fool, but not one who seeks the far shore.

1165.

1165.

“Odahi migavo pāsaṃ, nāsadā vāguraṃ migo;

Bhutvā nivāpaṃ gacchāma, kaddante migabandhake.

The hunter set a snare, but the deer did not approach the trap. Having eaten the bait, we depart, while the deer-trapper laments.

1166.

1166.

“Chinno pāso migavassa, nāsadā vāguraṃ migo;

Bhutvā nivāpaṃ gacchāma, socante migaluddake.

The hunter’s snare is cut; the deer did not approach the trap. Having eaten the bait, we depart, while the deer-hunter grieves.

1167.

1167.

“Tadāsi yaṃ bhiṃsanakaṃ, tadāsi lomahaṃsanaṃ;

Anekākārasampanne, sāriputtamhi nibbute.

Then there was terror, then there was horror, when Sāriputta, endowed with numerous qualities, attained Nibbāna.

1168.

1168.

dī. ni. 2.221, 272; saṃ. ni. 1.186; 2.143; apa. thera 1.2.115; jā. 1.1.95 “Aniccā [T 0.0427][P 0.0105] vata saṅkhārā uppādavaya dhammino.

Upajjitvā nirujjhanti, tesaṃ vūpasamo sukho.

Impermanent, alas, are formations, their nature is to arise and pass away. Having arisen, they cease; their calming is bliss.

1169.

1169.

“Sukhumaṃ te paṭivijjhanti, vālaggaṃ usunā yathā;

Ye pañcakkhandhe passanti, parato no ca attato.

They penetrate what is subtle, as one splits a hair-tip with an arrow: those who see the five aggregates as other, and not as self.

1170.

1170.

“Ye ca passanti saṅkhāre, parato no ca attato;

Paccabyādhiṃsu nipuṇaṃ, vālaggaṃ usunā yathā.

And those who see formations as other, and not as self, have pierced the subtle, as one splits a hair-tip with an arrow.

1171.

1171.

saṃ. ni. 1.21, 97 “Sattiyā viya omaṭṭho, ḍayhamānova matthake;

Kāmarāgappahānāya, sato bhikkhu paribbaje.

As if struck by a spear, as if with one’s head on fire, a bhikkhu should wander mindfully for the abandoning of sensual lust.

1172.

1172.

saṃ. ni. 1.21, 97“Sattiyā viya omaṭṭho, ḍayhamānova matthake;

Bhavarāgappahānāya, sato bhikkhu paribbaje”.

As if struck by a spear, as if with one’s head on fire, a bhikkhu should wander mindfully for the abandoning of lust for existence.

1173.

1173.

“Codito bhāvitattena, sarīrantimadhārinā;

Migāramātupāsādaṃ, pādaṅguṭṭhena kampayiṃ.

Urged on by him of developed self, the bearer of the final body, I shook the palace of Migāra’s mother with my big toe.

1174.

1174.

“Nayidaṃ sithilamārabbha, nayidaṃ appena thāmasā;

Nibbānamadhigantabbaṃ, sabbagantha-pamocanaṃ.

Not by striving slackly, not with little strength, is Nibbāna to be attained, the release from all bonds.

1175.

1175.

“Ayañca [V 0.0292] daharo bhikkhu, ayamuttamaporiso;

Dhāreti antimaṃ dehaṃ, jetvā māraṃ savāhiniṃ savāhanaṃ (ka.).

This young bhikkhu here is a supreme person; having conquered Māra with his army, he bears his final body.

1176.

1176.

“Vivaramanupabhanti [M 0.0364] vijjutā, vebhārassa ca paṇḍavassa ca;

Nagavivaragato jhāyati, putto appaṭimassa tādino.

Lightning flashes fall in the cleft between Mount Vebhāra and Mount Paṇḍava. Having gone into that mountain cleft, the son of the peerless one, the one endowed with forbearance, enters into jhāna.

1177.

1177.

“Upasanto uparato, pantasenāsano muni;

Dāyādo [T 0.0428] buddhaseṭṭhassa, brahmunā abhivandito.

With faculties serene, delighting in jhāna, the sage accustomed to a secluded dwelling is the heir of the most excellent Buddha, venerated by Brahmā.

1178.

1178.

“Upasantaṃ uparataṃ, pantasenāsanaṃ muniṃ;

Dāyādaṃ buddhaseṭṭhassa, vanda brāhmaṇa kassapaṃ.

O brahmin, venerate Kassapa: the serene one, delighting in seclusion, the sage accustomed to a remote dwelling, the heir of the most excellent Buddha.

1179.

1179.

“Yo ca jātisataṃ gacche, sabbā brāhmaṇajātiyo;

Sottiyo vedasampanno, manussesu punappunaṃ.

One who for a hundred births might be reborn again and again among humans in all brahmin families, a learned brahmin accomplished in the Vedas—

1180.

1180.

“Ajjhāyakopi ce assa, tiṇṇaṃ vedāna pāragū;

Etassa vandanāyetaṃ, kalaṃ nāgghati soḷasiṃ.

Even if one were a scholar, a master of the three Vedas, that achievement would not be worth a sixteenth part of the merit of venerating this one.

1181.

1181.

“Yo so aṭṭha vimokkhāni, purebhattaṃ aphassayi apassayi (sī. ka.), aphussayi (syā.);

Anulomaṃ paṭilomaṃ, tato piṇḍāya gacchati.

He who, before his meal, has attained the eight liberations in both forward and reverse order, and then, having emerged from that attainment, goes for alms-food—

1182.

1182.

“Tādisaṃ bhikkhuṃ māsādi mā hani (sī.), māttānaṃ khaṇi brāhmaṇa;

Abhippasādehi manaṃ, arahantamhi tādine;

Khippaṃ pañjaliko vanda, mā te vijaṭi matthakaṃ.

Do not assail such a bhikkhu! O brahmin, do not destroy yourself. Make your mind exceedingly serene towards this Arahant, this one endowed with forbearance. Quickly, with hands raised in añjali, venerate him, lest your head should split apart.

1183.

1183.

“Neso passati saddhammaṃ, saṃsārena purakkhato;

Adhogamaṃ jimhapathaṃ, kummaggamanudhāvati.

This one does not see the good Dhamma, being engulfed by saṃsāra. He runs along the wrong track, the crooked path that leads downwards.

1184.

1184.

“Kimīva mīḷhasallitto, saṅkhāre adhimucchito;

Pagāḷho lābhasakkāre, tuccho gacchati poṭṭhilo.

Like a worm smeared with filth, infatuated with formations, sunk deep in gain and honor, Poṭṭhila goes on, empty.

1185.

1185.

“Imañca passa āyantaṃ, sāriputtaṃ sudassanaṃ;

Vimuttaṃ ubhatobhāge, ajjhattaṃ susamāhitaṃ.

And see this Sāriputta coming, so fair to behold, liberated in both ways, inwardly well-concentrated.

1186.

1186.

“Visallaṃ [P 0.0106] khīṇasaṃyogaṃ, tevijjaṃ maccuhāyinaṃ;

Dakkhiṇeyyaṃ [T 0.0429] manussānaṃ, puññakkhettaṃ anuttaraṃ.

Free from the dart, with yokes destroyed, endowed with the three knowledges, one who has abandoned death, worthy of offerings from humans, an unsurpassed field of merit.

1187.

1187.

“Ete sambahulā devā, iddhimanto yasassino;

Dasa devasahassāni, sabbe brahmapurohitā;

Moggallānaṃ namassantā, tiṭṭhanti pañjalīkatā.

These many devas, powerful and of great renown—ten thousand devas, all of them Brahmā's ministers—stand with hands raised in añjali, venerating Moggallāna.

1188.

1188.

“‘Namo [V 0.0293] te purisājañña, namo te purisuttama;

Yassa te āsavā khīṇā, dakkhiṇeyyosi mārisa’.

‘Homage to you, O thoroughbred of men! Homage to you, O supreme among men! You whose taints are destroyed; you are worthy of offerings, venerable sir.’

1189.

1189.

“Pūjito [M 0.0365] naradevena, uppanno maraṇābhibhū;

Puṇḍarīkaṃva toyena, saṅkhārenupalippati.

Honored by humans and devas, arisen in the world, a conqueror of death, he is not sullied by formations, just as a white lotus is not by water.

1190.

1190.

“Yassa muhuttena sahassadhā loko, saṃvidito sabrahmakappo vasi;

Iddhiguṇe cutupapāte kāle, passati devatā sa bhikkhu.

That bhikkhu, who in a moment fully knows the thousandfold world-system together with its Brahmā realm, has mastery in the quality of psychic power and in the passing away and rebirth of beings; at the proper time, he sees the devas.

1191.

1191.

“Sāriputtova paññāya, sīlena upasamena ca;

Yopi pāraṅgato bhikkhu, etāvaparamo siyā.

In wisdom, virtue, and peace, Sāriputta is supreme; any other bhikkhu who has gone to the far shore can, at most, be his equal.

1192.

1192.

“Koṭisatasahassassa, attabhāvaṃ khaṇena nimmine;

Ahaṃ vikubbanāsu kusalo, vasībhūtomhi iddhiyā.

I can create a hundred thousand koṭis of bodies in an instant. I am skilled in transformations; I have attained mastery in psychic power.

1193.

1193.

“Samādhivijjāvasipāramīgato, moggallānagotto asitassa sāsane;

Dhīro samucchindi samāhitindriyo, nāgo [T 0.0430] yathā pūtilataṃva bandhanaṃ.

Having gone to the perfection of mastery in concentration and knowledge, he of the Moggallāna clan, in the teaching of the Unattached One, steadfast and with faculties composed, has cut through his bonds like a great elephant tearing a rotten creeper.

1194.

1194.

“Pariciṇṇo mayā satthā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ;

Ohito garuko bhāro, bhavanetti samūhatā.

I have served the Teacher; the Buddha’s teaching has been done. The heavy burden is laid down; the conduit to existence is uprooted.

1195.

1195.

“Yassa catthāya pabbajito, agārasmānagāriyaṃ;

So me attho anuppatto, sabbasaṃyojanakkhayo.

The goal for whose sake I went forth from the home life into homelessness—that goal has been attained by me: the destruction of all fetters.

1196.

1196.

ma. ni. 1.513 “Kīdiso nirayo āsi, yattha dussī apaccatha;

Vidhuraṃ sāvakamāsajja, kakusandhañca brāhmaṇaṃ.

What kind of hell was it where Dūsī was tormented, having assailed the disciple Vidhura and the brahmin Kakusandha?

1197.

1197.

“Sataṃ āsi ayosaṅkū, sabbe paccattavedanā;

Īdiso nirayo āsi, yattha dussī apaccatha;

Vidhuraṃ sāvakamāsajja, kakusandhañca brāhmaṇaṃ.

There were a hundred iron stakes, all of which were to be experienced individually. Such was the hell where Dūsī was tormented, having assailed the disciple Vidhura and the brahmin Kakusandha.

1198.

1198.

“Yo etamabhijānāti, bhikkhu buddhassa sāvako;

Tādisaṃ bhikkhumāsajja, kaṇha dukkhaṃ nigacchasi.

The bhikkhu, a disciple of the Buddha, who directly knows this—by assailing such a bhikkhu, O Dark One, you will come to suffering.

1199.

1199.

“Majjhesarasmiṃ [P 0.0107] sarassa (sī.), sāgarasmiṃ (ka.) tiṭṭhanti, vimānā kappaṭhāyino;

Veḷuriyavaṇṇā rucirā, accimanto pabhassarā;

Accharā tattha naccanti, puthu nānattavaṇṇiyo.

In the middle of the ocean stand celestial mansions, lasting for an aeon; the color of beryl, lovely, blazing, and luminous. There many nymphs of various different hues dance.

1200.

1200.

“Yo [T 0.0431][M 0.0366] etamabhijānāti…pe… kaṇha dukkhaṃ nigacchasi.

The bhikkhu, a disciple of the Buddha, who directly knows this—by assailing such a bhikkhu, O Dark One, you will come to suffering.

1201.

1201.

“Yo ve buddhena codito, bhikkhusaṅghassa pekkhato;

Migāramātupāsādaṃ, pādaṅguṭṭhena kampayi.

He who, when urged on by the Buddha, while the Saṅgha of bhikkhus looked on, made the palace of Migāra’s Mother tremble with his big toe.

1202.

1202.

“Yo etamabhijānāti…pe… kaṇha dukkhaṃ nigacchasi.

The bhikkhu, a disciple of the Buddha, who directly knows this—by assailing such a bhikkhu, O Dark One, you will come to suffering.

1203.

1203.

“Yo [V 0.0294] vejayantapāsādaṃ, pādaṅguṭṭhena kampayi;

Iddhibalenupatthaddho, saṃvejesi ca devatā.

He who made the Vejayanta Palace tremble with his big toe, supported by the power of iddhi, and stirred up the devas.

1204.

1204.

“Yo etamabhijānāti…pe… kaṇha dukkhaṃ nigacchasi.

The bhikkhu, a disciple of the Buddha, who directly knows this—by assailing such a bhikkhu, O Dark One, you will come to suffering.

1204.

1204.

“Yo etamabhijānāti…pe… kaṇha dukkhaṃ nigacchasi.

The bhikkhu, a disciple of the Buddha, who directly knows this—by assailing such a bhikkhu, O Dark One, you will come to suffering.

1205.

1205.

“Yo vejayantapāsāde, sakkaṃ so paripucchati;

Api āvuso jānāsi, taṇhakkhayavimuttiyo;

Tassa sakko viyākāsi, pañhaṃ puṭṭho yathātathaṃ.

He who in the Vejayanta Palace questioned Sakka: ‘Friend, do you know the liberations that are the destruction of craving?’ When asked the question, that Sakka answered him truthfully.

1206.

1206.

“Yo etamabhijānāti…pe… kaṇha dukkhaṃ nigacchasi.

The bhikkhu, a disciple of the Buddha, who directly knows this—by assailing such a bhikkhu, O Dark One, you will come to suffering.

1207.

1207.

“Yo brahmānaṃ paripucchati, sudhammāyaṃ ṭhito sudhammāyā’bhito (syā.) sabhaṃ;

Ajjāpi tyāvuso sā diṭṭhi, yā te diṭṭhi pure ahu;

Passasi vītivattantaṃ, brahmaloke pabhassaraṃ.

He who, standing in the Sudhammā Assembly Hall, questioned Brahmā: ‘Friend, do you still hold that view which you held formerly? Do you see the radiance in the Brahmā world being surpassed?’

1208.

1208.

“Tassa brahmā viyākāsi, pañhaṃ puṭṭho yathātathaṃ;

Na me mārisa sā diṭṭhi, yā me diṭṭhi pure ahu.

When asked the question, Brahmā answered him truthfully: ‘Good sir, I no longer hold that view which I held formerly.’

1209.

1209.

“Passāmi vītivattantaṃ, brahmaloke pabhassaraṃ;

Sohaṃ ajja kathaṃ vajjaṃ, ahaṃ niccomhi sassato.

‘I see the radiance in the Brahmā world being surpassed. How, then, could I say today that I am permanent, eternal?’

1210.

1210.

“Yo etamabhijānāti…pe… kaṇha dukkhaṃ nigacchasi.

The bhikkhu, a disciple of the Buddha, who directly knows this—by assailing such a bhikkhu, O Dark One, you will come to suffering.

1211.

1211.

“Yo mahāneruno kūṭaṃ, vimokkhena aphassayi apassayi (sī. ka.);

Vanaṃ pubbavidehānaṃ, ye ca bhūmisayā narā.

He who, by means of liberation, touched the peak of Great Meru, and saw the people of Pubbavideha and those humans who sleep on the ground.

1212.

1212.

“Yo etamabhijānāti, bhikkhu buddhassa sāvako;

Tādisaṃ bhikkhumāsajja, kaṇha dukkhaṃ nigacchasi.

The bhikkhu, a disciple of the Buddha, who directly knows this—by assailing such a bhikkhu, O Dark One, you will come to suffering.

1213.

1213.

“Na ve aggi cetayati, ahaṃ bālaṃ ḍahāmīti;

Bālova jalitaṃ aggiṃ, āsajja naṃ paḍayhati.

A fire does not think, ‘I will burn the fool’; but the fool, on touching the blazing fire, is thereby burned.

1214.

1214.

“Evameva tuvaṃ māra, āsajja naṃ tathāgataṃ;

Sayaṃ ḍahissasi attānaṃ, bālo aggiṃva samphusaṃ.

In the very same way, Māra, by assailing the Tathāgata, you will burn yourself, like a fool touching a fire.

1215.

1215.

“Apuññaṃ [T 0.0432][M 0.0367] pasavī māro, āsajja naṃ tathāgataṃ;

Kiṃ nu maññasi pāpima, na me pāpaṃ vipaccati.

By assailing the Tathāgata, Māra has generated demerit. What do you imagine, Evil One? Do you think, ‘My evil deed does not ripen’?

1216.

1216.

“Karato te cīyate miyyate (sabbattha) ma. ni. 1.513 passitabbaṃ pāpaṃ, cirarattāya antaka;

Māra nibbinda buddhamhā, āsaṃ mākāsi bhikkhusu.

Your evil deed, as you do it, is stored up for a long time, O End-maker. Māra, desist from the Enlightened One! Entertain no designs on the bhikkhus.

1217.

1217.

“Iti [V 0.0295][P 0.0108] māraṃ atajjesi, bhikkhu bhesakaḷāvane;

Tato so dummano yakkho, tatthevantaradhāyathā”ti.

Thus the bhikkhu rebuked Māra in the Bhesakaḷā Wood. Then that disheartened yakkha vanished right there.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā mahāmoggallāno mahāmoggalāno (ka.) thero gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

Thus, it is said, the Venerable Elder Mahāmoggallāna spoke these verses.

Saṭṭhinipāto niṭṭhito.

The Book of the Sixties is finished.

Tatruddānaṃ –

The summary:

Saṭṭhikamhi nipātamhi, moggallāno mahiddhiko;

Ekova theragāthāyo, aṭṭhasaṭṭhi bhavanti tāti.

In the Book of the Sixties, Moggallāna of great psychic power is the one elder alone; those verses are sixty-eight in number.

21. Mahānipāto

21. The Great Division

1. Vaṅgīsattheragāthā

1. The Verses of the Elder Vaṅgīsa

1218.

1218.

“Nikkhantaṃ [M 0.0368][V 0.0296][P 0.0109] vata maṃ santaṃ, agārasmānagāriyaṃ;

Vitakkā upadhāvanti, pagabbhā kaṇhato ime.

Though I have gone forth in peace from the home to the homeless life, these insolent thoughts from the Dark One assail me.

1219.

1219.

“Uggaputtā mahissāsā, sikkhitā daḷhadhammino daḷhadhanvino (sī. aṭṭha.);

Samantā parikireyyuṃ, sahassaṃ apalāyinaṃ.

Like fierce warriors, great archers, well-trained and strong-bowed, a thousand who would never flee, might surround me on all sides.

1220.

1220.

“Sacepi ettakā etato (saṃ. ni. 1.209) bhiyyo, āgamissanti itthiyo;

Neva maṃ byādhayissanti byāthayissanti (?), dhamme samhi dhammesvamhi (syā. ka.) patiṭṭhito.

Even if so many women, or even more, should come, they would not afflict me, for I am firmly established in the Dhamma.

1221.

1221.

“Sakkhī [T 0.0433] hi me sutaṃ etaṃ, buddhassādiccabandhuno;

Nibbānagamanaṃ maggaṃ, tattha me nirato mano.

Indeed, this I have heard directly from the Buddha, kinsman of the sun: the path leading to Nibbāna—in that my mind delights.

1222.

1222.

“Evaṃ ce maṃ viharantaṃ, pāpima upagacchasi;

Tathā maccu karissāmi, na me maggampi dakkhasi.

If you approach me as I am dwelling thus, O Evil One, I will act in such a way, O Death, that you will not even see my path.

1223.

1223.

“Aratiñca aratiṃ (bahūsu) ratiñca pahāya, sabbaso gehasitañca vitakkaṃ;

Vanathaṃ na kareyya kuhiñci, nibbanatho avanatho sa nibbanatho arato sa hi (saṃ. ni. 1.210) bhikkhu.

Having abandoned discontent and delight, and all thoughts connected with the household life, one should not create a jungle of craving anywhere. That bhikkhu is free from craving’s jungle, free from craving.

1224.

1224.

“Yamidha pathaviñca vehāsaṃ, rūpagataṃ jagatogadhaṃ kiñci;

Parijīyati sabbamaniccaṃ, evaṃ samecca caranti mutattā.

Whatever here on earth or in the sky has form, whatever is included in the world, all perishes and is impermanent. Having thus understood, the liberated fare on.

1225.

1225.

“Upadhīsu janā gadhitāse, diṭṭhasute diṭṭhe sute (sī.) paṭighe ca mute ca;

Ettha vinodaya chandamanejo, yo hettha na limpati muni tamāhu taṃ munimāhu (saṃ. ni. 1.210).

People are greedy for the substrates of existence—for what is seen and heard, sensed and cognized. Herein, dispel desire. Being imperturbable, whoever is not smeared by these, they call a sage.

1226.

1226.

“Atha [M 0.0369] saṭṭhisitā savitakkā, puthujjanatāya puthū janatāya (saṃ. ni. 1.210) adhammā niviṭṭhā;

Na ca vaggagatassa kuhiñci, no pana duṭṭhullagāhī duṭṭhullabhāṇī (saṃ. ni. 1.210) sa bhikkhu.

Those attached to the sixty speculative views, full of thoughts, are settled in the ways of worldlings, in what is not the Dhamma. That bhikkhu does not belong to any faction, nor is he one who grasps at anything coarse.

1227.

1227.

“Dabbo [P 0.0110] cirarattasamāhito, akuhako nipako apihālu;

Santaṃ padaṃ ajjhagamā muni, paṭicca parinibbuto kaṅkhati kālaṃ.

Wise, long concentrated, not fraudulent, prudent, and without craving, the sage has attained the peaceful state. Fully extinguished, he awaits his time.

1228.

1228.

“Mānaṃ pajahassu gotama, mānapathañca jahassu asesaṃ;

Mānapathamhi sa mucchito, vippaṭisārīhuvā cirarattaṃ.

Abandon conceit, Gotama! Abandon the path of conceit completely. Infatuated by the path of conceit, you have been remorseful for a long time.

1229.

1229.

“Makkhena makkhitā pajā, mānahatā nirayaṃ papatanti;

Socanti janā cirarattaṃ, mānahatā nirayaṃ upapannā.

Beings smeared with contempt, destroyed by conceit, fall into hell. People destroyed by conceit, having arisen in hell, grieve for a long time.

1230.

1230.

“Na [V 0.0297] hi socati bhikkhu kadāci, maggajino sammā paṭipanno;

Kittiñca [T 0.0434] sukhañcānubhoti, dhammadasoti tamāhu tathattaṃ.

A bhikkhu who is a conqueror by the path and has practiced rightly never grieves. He experiences fame and happiness; they call him, in truth, ‘one who sees the Dhamma’.

1231.

1231.

“Tasmā akhilo idha akhilo (sī.), akhilodha (saṃ. ni. 1.211) padhānavā, nīvaraṇāni pahāya visuddho;

Mānañca pahāya asesaṃ, vijjāyantakaro samitāvī.

Therefore, here, one who is free from stakes, energetic, and purified, having abandoned the hindrances; having abandoned conceit completely, being stilled, he makes an end with knowledge.

1232.

1232.

“Kāmarāgena ḍayhāmi, cittaṃ me pariḍayhati;

Sādhu nibbāpanaṃ brūhi, anukampāya gotama.

I am burned by sensual lust; my mind is ablaze. Good sir, out of compassion, speak of the quenching, O Gotama.

1233.

1233.

“Saññāya [M 0.0370] vipariyesā, cittaṃ te pariḍayhati;

Nimittaṃ parivajjehi, subhaṃ rāgūpasaṃhitaṃ ( ) (saṅkhāre parato passa, dukkhato mā ca attato; nibbāpehi mahārāgaṃ, mā dayhittho punappunaṃ;) (sī. saṃ. ni. 1.212) uddānagāthāyaṃ ekasattatītisaṅkhyā ca, theragāthāṭṭhakathā ca passitabbā.

Due to a perversion of perception, your mind is ablaze. Avoid the sign of the beautiful that is connected with lust.

1234.

1234.

“Asubhāya cittaṃ bhāvehi, ekaggaṃ susamāhitaṃ;

Sati kāyagatā tyatthu, nibbidābahulo bhava.

Develop the mind on the unattractive, one-pointed and well-concentrated. Let mindfulness directed to the body be yours; be one who abounds in disenchantment.

1235.

1235.

“Animittañca bhāvehi, mānānusayamujjaha;

Tato mānābhisamayā, upasanto carissasi.

And develop the signless; abandon the underlying tendency to conceit. Then, through the full understanding of conceit, you will fare on at peace.

1236.

1236.

“Tameva vācaṃ bhāseyya, yāyattānaṃ na tāpaye;

Pare ca na vihiṃseyya, sā ve vācā subhāsitā.

One should speak only that speech by which one would not torment oneself and would not harm others. That, indeed, is well-spoken speech.

1237.

1237.

“Piyavācameva bhāseyya, yā vācā paṭinanditā;

Yaṃ anādāya pāpāni, paresaṃ bhāsate piyaṃ.

One should speak only pleasant speech, speech that is welcomed. One speaks what is pleasant to others, not adopting what is evil.

1238.

1238.

“Saccaṃ ve amatā vācā, esa dhammo sanantano;

Sacce atthe ca dhamme ca, āhu santo patiṭṭhitā.

Truth, indeed, is immortal speech; this is the eternal law. The good, they say, are established in truth, in the goal, and in the Dhamma.

1239.

1239.

“Yaṃ buddho bhāsati vācaṃ, khemaṃ nibbānapattiyā;

Dukkhassantakiriyāya, sā ve vācānamuttamā.

The speech the Buddha speaks—secure, for the attainment of Nibbāna, for making an end of suffering—that, indeed, is the best of speeches.

1240.

1240.

“Gambhīrapañño medhāvī, maggāmaggassa kovido;

Sāriputto [T 0.0435] mahāpañño, dhammaṃ deseti bhikkhunaṃ.

Of profound wisdom, intelligent, an expert in the path and the non-path, Sāriputta, of great wisdom, teaches the Dhamma to the bhikkhus.

1241.

1241.

“Saṅkhittenapi deseti, vitthārenapi bhāsati;

Sālikāyiva nigghoso, paṭibhānaṃ udiyyati udīrayi (sī.), udīyyati (syā.), udayyati (?) uṭṭhahatīti taṃsaṃvaṇṇanā.

He teaches in brief and speaks in detail. Like the sound of a myna bird, his inspired speech flows forth.

1242.

1242.

“Tassa [P 0.0111] taṃ desayantassa, suṇanti madhuraṃ giraṃ;

Sarena rajanīyena, savanīyena vaggunā;

Udaggacittā muditā, sotaṃ odhenti bhikkhavo.

While he is teaching, they listen to his sweet speech. With a voice delightful, pleasant to hear, and melodious, the bhikkhus, with elated and joyful minds, incline their ear.

1243.

1243.

“Ajja pannarase visuddhiyā, bhikkhū pañcasatā samāgatā;

Saṃyojanabandhanacchidā, anīghā khīṇapunabbhavā isī.

Today, on the fifteenth day, for the sake of purity, five hundred bhikkhus have assembled—seers who have cut the fetters and bonds, are untroubled, and for whom renewed existence is destroyed.

1244.

1244.

“Cakkavattī [V 0.0298] yathā rājā, amaccaparivārito;

Samantā anupariyeti, sāgarantaṃ mahiṃ imaṃ.

Just as a wheel-turning king, surrounded by his ministers, travels all around this earth bounded by the ocean,

1245.

1245.

“Evaṃ [M 0.0371] vijitasaṅgāmaṃ, satthavāhaṃ anuttaraṃ;

Sāvakā payirupāsanti, tevijjā maccuhāyino.

Even so do the disciples attend upon the victor in battle, the unsurpassed caravan leader—they who possess the triple knowledge and have abandoned death.

1246.

1246.

“Sabbe bhagavato puttā, palāpettha na vijjati;

Taṇhāsallassa hantāraṃ, vande ādiccabandhunaṃ.

All are sons of the Blessed One; no chaff is found here. I pay homage to the Kinsman of the Sun, the remover of the dart of craving.

1247.

1247.

“Parosahassaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, sugataṃ payirupāsati;

Desentaṃ virajaṃ dhammaṃ, nibbānaṃ akutobhayaṃ.

More than a thousand bhikkhus attend upon the Well-Farer as he teaches the stainless Dhamma: Nibbāna, which is free from fear from any quarter.

1248.

1248.

“Suṇanti dhammaṃ vimalaṃ, sammāsambuddhadesitaṃ;

Sobhati vata sambuddho, bhikkhusaṅghapurakkhato.

They listen to the immaculate Dhamma taught by the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One. Truly, the Enlightened One shines, honored by the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.

1249.

1249.

“‘Nāganāmo’si bhagavā, isīnaṃ isisattamo;

Mahāmeghova hutvāna, sāvake abhivassasi.

You are the Nāga by name, O Blessed One, the seventh of the seers. Having become like a great cloud, you rain down upon your disciples.

1250.

1250.

“Divā [T 0.0436] vihārā nikkhamma, satthudassanakamyatā;

Sāvako te mahāvīra, pāde vandati vaṅgiso.

Coming forth from his day’s abiding, desiring to see the Teacher, your disciple Vaṅgīsa venerates your feet, O great hero.

1251.

1251.

“Ummaggapathaṃ mārassa, abhibhuyya carati pabhijja khīlāni;

Taṃ passatha bandhapamuñcakaraṃ, asitaṃva bhāgaso pavibhajja.

Having overcome Māra’s devious path, he fares on, having broken the stakes. See him, the one who brings release from bonds, the unattached one who analyzes in parts.

1252.

1252.

“Oghassa hi nitaraṇatthaṃ, anekavihitaṃ maggaṃ akkhāsi;

Tasmiñca amate akkhāte, dhammadasā ṭhitā asaṃhīrā.

For the sake of crossing the flood, he has proclaimed the path in its many aspects. And when that deathless state has been proclaimed, those who see the Dhamma stand firm, unshakable.

1253.

1253.

“Pajjotakaro ativijjha ativijjha dhammaṃ (sī.), sabbaṭhitīnaṃ atikkamamaddasa atikkamamadda (sī. ka.);

Ñatvā ca sacchikatvā ca, aggaṃ so desayi dasaddhānaṃ.

The light-maker, having penetrated, saw the overcoming of all standpoints. Having known and realized it, he taught the supreme state of ten aspects.

1254.

1254.

“Evaṃ sudesite dhamme, ko pamādo vijānataṃ dhammaṃ;

Tasmā hi tassa bhagavato sāsane, appamatto sadā namassamanusikkhe.

When the Dhamma has been so well expounded, what negligence can there be for those who understand the Dhamma? Therefore, in the Blessed One’s dispensation, one should always train heedfully, paying homage.

1255.

1255.

“Buddhānubuddho yo thero, koṇḍañño tibbanikkamo;

Lābhī sukhavihārānaṃ, vivekānaṃ abhiṇhaso.

The elder who was awakened after the Buddha, Koṇḍañña of keen exertion, is a constant gainer of pleasant abidings, of states of seclusion.

1256.

1256.

“Yaṃ [M 0.0372][P 0.0112] sāvakena pattabbaṃ, satthu sāsanakārinā;

Sabbassa taṃ anuppattaṃ, appamattassa sikkhato.

Whatever is to be attained by a disciple who carries out the Teacher’s instruction, all that has been attained by him, training heedfully.

1257.

1257.

“Mahānubhāvo tevijjo, cetopariyakovido;

Koṇḍañño buddhadāyādo, pāde vandati satthuno.

Of great power, possessing the triple knowledge, an expert in encompassing the minds of others, Koṇḍañña, the Buddha’s heir, venerates the Teacher’s feet.

1258.

1258.

“Nagassa [V 0.0299] passe āsīnaṃ, muniṃ dukkhassa pāraguṃ;

Sāvakā payirupāsanti, tevijjā maccuhāyino.

Seated on the mountain slope, the sage who has gone to the far shore of suffering, disciples attend upon him, possessors of the threefold knowledge, who have abandoned death.

1259.

1259.

“Cetasā te cetasā (saṃ. ni. 1.218) anupariyeti, moggallāno mahiddhiko;

Cittaṃ [T 0.0437] nesaṃ samanvesaṃ samannesaṃ (saṃ. ni. 1.218), vippamuttaṃ nirūpadhiṃ.

Moggallāna of great psychic power, investigating their minds with his own mind, perceives in sequence their liberation, free from all substrates.

1260.

1260.

“Evaṃ sabbaṅgasampannaṃ, muniṃ dukkhassa pāraguṃ;

Anekākārasampannaṃ, payirupāsanti gotamaṃ.

Thus the disciples attend upon Gotama, the sage, who is accomplished in every aspect, who has gone to the far shore of suffering, and is endowed with numerous qualities.

1261.

1261.

“Cando yathā vigatavalāhake nabhe, virocati vītamalova bhāṇumā;

Evampi aṅgīrasa tvaṃ mahāmuni, atirocasi yasasā sabbalokaṃ.

Just as the moon shines in a cloudless sky, and the sun, free from stain, is radiant, so too, O Aṅgīrasa, great sage, you outshine the entire world with your glory.

1262.

1262.

“Kāveyyamattā vicarimha pubbe, gāmā gāmaṃ purā puraṃ;

Athaddasāma sambuddhaṃ, sabbadhammāna pāraguṃ.

Formerly, intoxicated with poetry, we wandered from village to village, from city to city. Then we saw the Perfectly Enlightened One, who has gone to the far shore of all phenomena.

1263.

1263.

“So me dhammamadesesi, muni dukkhassa pāragū;

Dhammaṃ sutvā pasīdimha, saddhā addhā (sī. aṭṭha.) no udapajjatha.

He, the sage who has gone to the far shore of suffering, taught me the Dhamma. Having heard the Dhamma, we gained confidence, and faith arose in us.

1264.

1264.

“Tassāhaṃ vacanaṃ sutvā, khandhe āyatanāni ca;

Dhātuyo ca viditvāna, pabbajiṃ anagāriyaṃ.

Having heard his word, and having understood the aggregates, the sense bases, and the elements, I went forth into the homeless life.

1265.

1265.

“Bahūnaṃ vata atthāya, uppajjanti tathāgatā;

Itthīnaṃ purisānañca, ye te sāsanakārakā.

Indeed, for the welfare of many do Tathāgatas arise—for those women and men who are practitioners of the teaching.

1266.

1266.

“Tesaṃ kho vata atthāya, bodhimajjhagamā muni;

Bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnañca, ye nirāmagataddasā.

Indeed, it was for their benefit that the sage attained enlightenment—for the bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs who have seen and entered the fixed course of rightness.

1267.

1267.

“Sudesitā cakkhumatā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Cattāri ariyasaccāni, anukampāya pāṇinaṃ.

The Four Noble Truths have been well taught by the One with Vision, the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun, out of compassion for living beings:

1268.

1268.

“Dukkhaṃ [M 0.0373] dukkhasamuppādaṃ, dukkhassa ca atikkamaṃ;

Ariyaṃ [T 0.0438] caṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ, dukkhūpasamagāminaṃ.

Suffering, the origin of suffering, the overcoming of suffering, and the Noble Eightfold Path leading to the stilling of suffering.

1269.

1269.

“Evamete tathā vuttā, diṭṭhā me te yathā tathā;

Sadattho me anuppatto, kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ.

Just as these truths were declared, so have they been seen by me. My own true welfare has been attained; the Buddha’s teaching has been fulfilled.

1270.

1270.

“Svāgataṃ vata me āsi, mama buddhassa santike;

Suvibhattesu savibhattesu (sī. ka.) dhammesu, yaṃ seṭṭhaṃ tadupāgamiṃ.

A good coming indeed it was for me, into the presence of the Buddha. Among the well-analyzed Dhammas, I have attained that which is supreme.

1271.

1271.

“Abhiññāpāramippatto, sotadhātu visodhitā;

Tevijjo iddhipattomhi, cetopariyakovido.

I have reached the perfection of the direct knowledges; the ear-element is purified. I am one with the three true knowledges, have attained psychic power, and am an expert in comprehending the minds of others.

1272.

1272.

“Pucchāmi [P 0.0113] satthāramanomapaññaṃ, diṭṭheva dhamme yo vicikicchānaṃ chettā;

Aggāḷave kālamakāsi bhikkhu, ñāto yasassī abhinibbutatto.

I ask the Teacher of supreme wisdom, the cutter of doubts in this very life: At Aggāḷava a bhikkhu passed away—he was well-known, renowned, and his being was fully extinguished.

1273.

1273.

“Nigrodhakappo [V 0.0300] iti tassa nāmaṃ, tayā kataṃ bhagavā brāhmaṇassa;

So taṃ namassaṃ acari mutyapekho, āraddhavīriyo daḷhadhammadassī.

‘Nigrodhakappa’ was the name given by you, Blessed One, to that brahmin. Seeking release, he lived paying homage to you, with energy aroused, a seer of the steadfast Dhamma.

1274.

1274.

“Taṃ sāvakaṃ sakka mayampi sabbe, aññātumicchāma samantacakkhu;

Samavaṭṭhitā no savanāya sotā hetuṃ (sī. syā.) suttanipātaṭṭhakathā passitabbā, tuvaṃ no satthā tvamanuttarosi”.

O Sakyan, O All-Seeing One, we all wish to know about that disciple. Our ears are prepared for hearing. You are our Teacher; you are the unsurpassed.

1275.

1275.

Chinda [T 0.0439] no vicikicchaṃ brūhi metaṃ, parinibbutaṃ vedaya bhūripañña;

Majjheva no bhāsa samantacakkhu, sakkova devāna sahassanetto.

Cut off our doubt, tell this to me, O One of Vast Wisdom, make known that he is fully extinguished. Speak in our very midst, O All-Seeing One, just like Sakka of a thousand eyes among the devas.

1276.

1276.

“Ye keci ganthā idha mohamaggā, aññāṇapakkhā vicikicchaṭhānā;

Tathāgataṃ patvā na te bhavanti, cakkhuñhi etaṃ paramaṃ narānaṃ.

Whatever fetters exist here—which are paths of delusion, factions of ignorance, and grounds for doubt—upon reaching the Tathāgata, they cease to be. For he is indeed the supreme eye for humankind.

1277.

1277.

“No [M 0.0374] ce hi jātu puriso kilese, vāto yathā abbhaghanaṃ vihāne;

Tamovassa nivuto sabbaloko, jotimantopi na pabhāseyyuṃ na jotimantopi narā tapeyyuṃ (su. ni. 350).

For if a man were never to dispel defilements—as the wind dispels a mass of clouds—the entire world would be shrouded in darkness; even those with light would not be able to shine.

1278.

1278.

“Dhīrā ca pajjotakarā bhavanti, taṃ taṃ ahaṃ vīra tatheva maññe;

Vipassinaṃ jānamupāgamimha, parisāsu no āvikarohi kappaṃ.

The wise are indeed makers of light, and I consider you, O Hero, to be just so. We have approached you, the one with insight, the knower. Reveal Kappa to us in this assembly.

1279.

1279.

“Khippaṃ giraṃ eraya vaggu vagguṃ, haṃsova paggayha saṇikaṃ nikūja;

Bindussarena [P 0.0114] suvikappitena, sabbeva te ujjugatā suṇoma.

Quickly utter your charming, lovely speech, like a swan stretching its neck and cooing gently. With your well-composed and melodious voice, we all, being attentive, will listen.

1280.

1280.

“Pahīnajātimaraṇaṃ [T 0.0440] asesaṃ, niggayha dhonaṃ vadessāmi paṭivediyāmi (sī. ka.) dhammaṃ;

Na kāmakāro hi hoti (sī. ka.) puthujjanānaṃ, saṅkheyyakāro ca va (bahūsu) tathāgatānaṃ.

I shall speak the Dhamma that has completely abandoned birth and death, that subdues and cleanses. For there is no acting on impulse for worldlings, whereas Tathāgatas act with deliberation.

1281.

1281.

“Sampannaveyyākaraṇaṃ tavedaṃ, samujjupaññassa samuggahītaṃ;

Ayamañjali pacchimo suppaṇāmito, mā mohayī jānamanomapañña.

This perfect explanation of you, who are of upright wisdom, has been well-grasped by me. This is my final, well-proffered gesture of reverence. O One of supreme wisdom, knowing as you do, do not cause me to be deluded.

1282.

1282.

“Paroparaṃ ariyadhammaṃ viditvā, mā mohayī jānamanomavīriya;

Vāriṃ yathā ghammani ghammatatto, vācābhikaṅkhāmi sutaṃ pavassa.

Having known the noble Dhamma both high and low, knowing as you do, do not cause me to be deluded, O One of supreme energy. Just as one scorched by heat in the hot season longs for water, so I long for your speech. Rain down what is to be heard!

1283.

1283.

“Yadatthikaṃ brahmacariyaṃ acarī, kappāyano kaccissataṃ amoghaṃ;

Nibbāyi so ādu saupādiseso anupādisesā (sī.), anupādiseso (ka.), yathā vimutto ahu taṃ suṇoma.

The holy life for the sake of a goal that Kappāyana lived—I trust it was not in vain for him? Was he extinguished with residue remaining, or without? Let us hear how he was liberated.

1284.

1284.

“‘Acchecchi [M 0.0375] taṇhaṃ idha nāmarūpe,

(Iti bhagavā) kaṇhassa sotaṃ dīgharattānusayitaṃ;

Atāri jātiṃ maraṇaṃ asesaṃ’, iccabravi [T 0.0441] bhagavā pañcaseṭṭho.

“He cut off craving here in name-and-form,” said the Blessed One, “the dark stream that has long lain latent. He crossed completely over birth and death.” Thus spoke the Blessed One, chief among the five.

1285.

1285.

“Esa sutvā pasīdāmi, vaco te isisattama;

Amoghaṃ kira me puṭṭhaṃ, na maṃ vañcesi brāhmaṇo.

Having heard your word, O seventh of the seers, I am filled with confidence. Indeed, my question was not in vain; you, Brahmin, did not deceive me.

1286.

1286.

“Yathā vādī tathā kārī, ahu buddhassa sāvako;

Acchecchi maccuno jālaṃ, tataṃ māyāvino daḷhaṃ.

A disciple of the Buddha he was, one who acted as he spoke. He cut the strong, spread-out net of the Deceiver, of Death.

1287.

1287.

“Addasa [V 0.0301] bhagavā ādiṃ, upādānassa kappiyo;

Accagā [P 0.0115] vata kappāno, maccudheyyaṃ suduttaraṃ.

O Blessed One, Kappiya saw the origin of clinging. Indeed, Kappāna has passed beyond the realm of Death, which is so very hard to cross.

1288.

1288.

“Taṃ devadevaṃ vandāmi, puttaṃ te dvipaduttama;

Anujātaṃ mahāvīraṃ, nāgaṃ nāgassa orasa”nti.

I pay homage to him, the Deva of Devas, your son, O Best of Bipeds—the great hero born in your likeness, the Nāga, true-born son of the Nāga.

Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā vaṅgīso thero gāthāyo

In this manner, indeed, the venerable elder Vaṅgīsa spoke these verses.

Abhāsitthāti.

He spoke thus.

Mahānipāto niṭṭhito.

The Great Chapter is concluded.

Tatruddānaṃ –

The summary:

Sattatimhi nipātamhi, vaṅgīso paṭibhāṇavā;

Ekova thero natthañño, gāthāyo ekasattatīti.

In the Chapter of Seventy, Vaṅgīsa the eloquent; the only elder, there is no other; the verses are seventy-one.

Niṭṭhitā theragāthāyo.

The Verses of the Elders are concluded.

Tatruddānaṃ –

The summary:

Sahassaṃ honti tā gāthā, tīṇi saṭṭhisatāni ca;

Therā ca dve satā saṭṭhi, cattāro ca pakāsitā.

Those verses are one thousand, and one hundred and sixty-three; and the elders declared are two hundred and sixty-four.

Sīhanādaṃ naditvāna, buddhaputtā anāsavā;

Khemantaṃ pāpuṇitvāna, aggikhandhāva nibbutāti.

Having roared the lion’s roar, the sons of the Buddha, free from taints, having reached the secure end, are extinguished like a mass of fire.

Theragāthāpāḷi niṭṭhitā.

The Pāḷi of the Verses of the Elders is concluded.
